articles.title: Binance Hack: How Attackers Raced to Move $6.3B
articles.text:
Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen
Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.
Attackers behind Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion hack still control billions of dollars in stolen cryptocurrency despite efforts by token issuers to freeze the proceeds.
The attack, the largest in crypto history, began at 8:04 pm UTC Thursday and the perpetrators, linked to the same North Korean hackers behind last month’s Bitget hack, immediately began converting assets.
The game plan for the hackers was to convert the assets that could be frozen, like USDT and USDC, into ones that could not, such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH).
CertiK engineer Dickson Wu traced $500 million in USDT that was sent to one address, with $325 million sold to market makers for ETH by 20:59 UTC, less than an hour after the hack began.
They were racing against some of crypto’s most powerful gatekeepers: stablecoin giants like Tether and Circle, who had already begun blacklisting addresses associated with the theft.
Binance said Friday that about $3 billion of the stolen assets were frozen onchain out of an estimated $6.3 billion total, and that it is working with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain analytics firms to trace additional funds.
The scale of the theft is mind-boggling, even in crypto terms, but with around half of the assets already frozen, how much of the stolen crypto can the perpetrators actually spend?
Crypto with an off switch
Unlike BTC or ETH, which are decentralized cryptocurrencies with no central issuer and no one to hit the pause button, centralized stablecoins like Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC have issuers that can freeze tokens held at specific addresses.
Binance said it is working with law enforcement to trace the funds. Source: Binance
That gives them the power to act swiftly in incidents like these. Tether froze around $1.567 billion in USDT in total, with the first major freeze happening just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the attacker’s main Ethereum wallet.
Related: Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses
Circle froze around $823 million in USDC three minutes later, with other issuers like Ripple and World Liberty Financial following soon after.
The ability to immobilize crypto is not exclusively a stablecoin feature, and despite not having central issuers, some decentralized protocols like Arbitrum did not sit idly by.
Arbitrum’s Security Council moved around $30.5 million in ARB and ETH into an intermediary frozen wallet, where they can only be moved after further action by the council or a vote by Arbitrum DAO governance.
One important distinction remains — frozen funds don’t necessarily equate to recovered funds. Immobilizing assets prevents the suspected attackers from spending them, but it doesn’t automatically return them to Binance or its users.
The Aave complication
Decentralized lending protocol Aave adds another layer of complexity to the equation. Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, a wallet associated with the attackers deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave V3 on Ethereum and borrowed $44.6 million of wrapped Ether (WETH), around 40 minutes before the first freeze.
LlamaRisk, an Aave risk service provider, said in its 1:00 am update that the attacker’s position subsequently held around $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt. Aave said the position remained overcollateralized and did not put protocol suppliers at risk.
Largest crypto heists of all time. Source: Elliptic
Since the USDT had already been deposited into Aave’s lending pool, blacklisting the attacker’s wallet could not automatically retrieve the collateral held by the protocol, as Aave Chan Initiative founder Marc Zeller explained:
“USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol.”
To prevent further deposits and borrowing, Aave temporarily froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments, although existing users could still withdraw funds, repay loans and liquidate positions.
Aave later lifted its precautionary freeze across V3 and V4 markets, saying its contracts were unaffected and positions remained overcollateralized.
“Just another day in crypto,” Zeller said.
So what can the attackers actually keep?
Elliptic estimated that $2.84 billion had been frozen by 7:00 am UTC on Friday, while the attackers still controlled around $3.33 billion in assets that issuers could not immobilize.
And while the freeze almost halved the attackers’ profit pool, that doesn’t mean all the remaining funds are safe to recover.
Bitcoin and Ether don’t have a centralized token issuer that can blacklist individual addresses like Tether or Circle. So once stolen assets are converted into these native cryptocurrencies, transactions can be restricted, but freezing them is a lot harder.
Binance has pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, and says user assets remain safe; according to the latest update from Binance chief executive Richard Teng, the exchange is already “recovering stolen assets for users.”
Magazine: Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself

articles.title: Tether’s Bitcoin reserves reach $8.37B in Q3 report
articles.text:
Tether’s excess reserves nearly double to $8B as Q3 profit hits $1.5B
The stablecoin issuer’s US Treasury holdings are comparable to those of major foreign holders, while its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion at the end of September.
Tether reported $1.5 billion in third-quarter operating profit as its excess reserves nearly doubled to $7.95 billion, according to figures released alongside its latest attestation prepared by independent accounting firm BDO.
The company held $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities at the end of September, leaving a reserve surplus of $7.95 billion, nearly double the $4.1 billion reported in June. Its assets included $132.4 billion in direct and indirect US Treasury bill holdings.
That exposure is comparable to South Korea’s $134.2 billion in US government debt and exceeds the United Arab Emirates’ $116.1 billion, according to August data from the US Treasury Department.
Tether also generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first nine months of 2026, with income largely driven by US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, according to the company. Its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion, up from approximately $5.8 billion at the end of June.
Tether’s USDT remains the world’s largest stablecoin, accounting for around 60% of the $297.3 billion stablecoin market, according to DefiLlama data. On Friday, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X that USDT’s user base had surpassed 700 million, with adoption concentrated in emerging markets.
The stablecoin issuer has faced years of scrutiny over its reserve transparency. In August, the company announced the completion of its first full independent financial statement audit by KPMG US, although the audited statements were not made public.

articles.title: Crypto Stocks Slide as Binance Hack Rattles Digital Asset Markets
articles.text:
Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3B Binance hack
Circle, Strategy and other crypto-linked stocks fell sharply Friday, a day after Binance disclosed a $6.3 billion security breach.
Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.
Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.
Source: Yahoo Finance
The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.
The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of a the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
Related: Binance working with FBI to recover assets following $6.3B hack
Crypto gains lift Coinbase, Strategy profits as revenue falls
Coinbase and Strategy both reported third-quarter earnings Thursday, with gains on their crypto holdings lifting profits even as revenue declined.
Coinbase reported $719 million in net income, boosted by about $715 million in gains on cryptocurrency investments. Adjusted net income, which excludes investment gains and other items, was $78 million. Net revenue fell about 34% year over year to $1.16 billion.
The exchange also reported that its prediction markets business surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue.
Strategy reported $19.53 billion in net income, largely driven by a $20.91 billion gain in the value of its Bitcoin (BTC) holdings. Revenue declined 3% year over year to $125.4 million.
Strategy also announced that Andrew Kang will step down as chief financial officer on Nov. 5.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s Quantum Threat, Ripple Bank Approval
articles.text:
Crypto Biz: Bitcoin’s quantum threat is becoming an economic problem
Bitcoin faces mounting quantum security concerns as Ripple secures a US banking charter, USDC gains ground in Europe and VanEck adds BTC to a new ETF.
The debate over quantum computing has raised serious questions about Bitcoin’s long-term security, but the economic consequences could emerge long before the technology seriously threatens the network.
Muneeb Ali, founder of Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, believes quantum computing risks are already discouraging institutional investment, even as US spot Bitcoin ETFs have amassed more than $104 billion in net assets, according to BitBo data. He warns that BTC has only a few years to prepare for the transition to quantum-resistant security, a process that could take years given the network’s history of slow and contentious upgrades.
For institutional investors drawn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement, doubts about its long-term security could complicate the investment case.
This week’s Crypto Biz explores the quantum threat, alongside new developments surrounding Ripple, VanEck and European stablecoin adoption.
Quantum computing fears are already limiting Bitcoin’s growth, Stacks founder says
Bitcoin could face a more serious security challenge if developers fail to make meaningful progress toward quantum resistance by 2028, according to Stacks founder Muneeb Ali, who warned that the network’s lengthy upgrade process leaves little room for delays.
Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction podcast, Ali said Bitcoin needs a credible roadmap for becoming quantum-resistant, with meaningful progress required by 2028. He cited 2030 as the target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant security, based on guidance from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, though advances in artificial intelligence could bring that deadline forward.
Even if developers agree on how to protect Bitcoin against quantum attacks, implementing the changes could take years. Holders would then need time to move their Bitcoin to quantum-resistant addresses.
Although some industry participants dispute the urgency of the threat, Ali argued that uncertainty alone could undermine investor confidence. He also warned that a quantum breakthrough capable of compromising Bitcoin would have consequences for the broader cryptocurrency market.
Ripple secures US federal banking charter
Ripple has received final approval from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish a national trust bank, clearing the last regulatory hurdle after securing conditional approval in December 2025.
The newly chartered Ripple National Trust Bank will operate under federal supervision, manage reserves backing the company’s RLUSD stablecoin, serve as a collateral trustee for tokenholders and provide digital asset custody. RLUSD will continue to be issued by Standard Custody & Trust Company, which is regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services.
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse welcomed the approval, declaring that “crypto and banks work better together.”
The decision follows similar final approval for Circle in July, while Coinbase, Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge remain at the conditional approval stage. Unlike traditional commercial banks, national trust banks generally cannot accept deposits or issue loans and do not carry Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation coverage.
USDC overtakes Tether in euro trading as MiCA rules take hold
Circle’s USDC has surpassed Tether’s USDt in stablecoin trading against the euro, as European Union regulations reshape competition between the world’s two largest dollar-backed stablecoins.
According to a new report from Kaiko, USDC now accounts for 56% of euro-denominated stablecoin trading, up from just 10% in January 2024. The shift accelerated after major cryptocurrency exchanges restricted USDt trading for European Economic Area customers to comply with the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
USDC’s euro order books are now roughly 40% deeper than USDt’s, suggesting stronger liquidity for traders. However, USDT remains the dominant stablecoin globally, with a circulating supply approximately 2.5 times larger than USDC’s.
The findings come after the European Banking Authority designated USDC as the bloc’s first “significant e-money token,” subjecting it to additional regulatory oversight. Kaiko suggested that the US GENIUS Act could produce similar changes in stablecoin trading, depending on how exchanges implement the new requirements.
VanEck includes Bitcoin in new multi-asset ETF
VanEck, the $244 billion asset manager, has launched an actively managed exchange-traded fund that combines traditional stocks and bonds with real assets and a small allocation to Bitcoin.
The VanEck Wealth Builder ETF (NYSE: WBMO), announced Tuesday, invests in a mix of VanEck and third-party ETFs and targets a 2% Bitcoin allocation, which can range from 1% to 5%. Rather than holding Bitcoin directly, the fund gains exposure through a spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product. The launch expands VanEck’s existing Wealth Builder model portfolios into a single ETF.
David Schassler, VanEck’s head of multi-asset solutions, said the traditional 60/40 stock-and-bond portfolio was designed for a different investment environment. He contended that adding real assets could help investors navigate a broader range of economic conditions, with Bitcoin now forming a small part of that strategy.
Crypto Biz is your weekly pulse on the business behind blockchain and crypto, delivered directly to your inbox every Thursday.

articles.title: Binance’s Record $6.3B Hack Recapped From Cointelegraph’s Live Coverage
articles.text:
Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded
A recap of Cointelegraph’s live coverage of the Binance hack, including early breach reports and the exchange’s full reimbursement pledge.
This recap summarizes Cointelegraph’s reporting on the Binance hack and has been updated with the exchange’s latest statements. The investigation is ongoing, and figures and recovery timelines may change. See our archived live coverage for the original timeline.
Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance on Thursday, in what is now the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Industry partners have frozen roughly $3 billion in affected assets, while customers await the reopening of withdrawals.
TRM Labs traced the first unauthorized transfers to around 8:05 pm UTC Thursday, with Binance wallets drained across multiple blockchains. The attackers targeted hot wallets, which exchanges keep connected to the internet to process withdrawals.
TRM attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, which the US Federal Bureau of Investigation blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. Binance has not publicly confirmed the attackers’ identity.
“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” said Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”
Binance said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the affected tokens. However, that allocation excludes the frozen assets, and the exchange said it was buying the remaining tokens through exchanges and over-the-counter deals.
A spokesperson told Cointelegraph the $5 billion was in Binance’s custody but declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security concerns. Security firm CertiK said it needed more information to verify the holdings independently.
Frozen funds are not necessarily recovered funds, and Binance has yet to disclose how much stolen crypto has actually been returned to its control.
EIP-7702’s role in the hack comes under scrutiny
Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade came under fire after attackers used it to drain a Binance wallet. EIP-7702 is a feature that lets a wallet authorize software to act on its behalf. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph that compromised signing systems likely enabled the theft.
Attackers could have stolen the funds without EIP-7702, but it may have helped them bypass safeguards and drain assets in one sweep, Ben-Natan said.
Teng said that the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to gain execution authority over a hot wallet without passing Binance’s normal approval controls. A “self-destruct mechanism” destroyed tools and traces, complicating the investigation, he said.
Binance said investigators had also uncovered additional breaches beyond the initially suspected compromised laptop. However, it reported no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked and said it expected to share further technical findings within about 48 hours.
Chainalysis observed thousands of transactions in quick succession that could indicate automated laundering, with funds circulating among addresses and sometimes returning to wallets used earlier.
Binance users await withdrawals reopening
The theft rattled crypto prices and prompted a precautionary freeze on new deposits and borrowing at decentralized lender Aave. Aave reopened its markets Friday afternoon, while Binance’s withdrawals remained suspended.
Binance said in a Friday update that it aimed to begin reopening withdrawals in stages Sunday, Nov. 1, subject to completing security checks. Deposits and other unaffected services remained operational.
The exchange said it planned to take an initial proof-of-reserves snapshot within 12 hours of the announcement, with results ready by Monday. The report is intended to show the assets Binance holds and the backing of customer balances.
Magazine: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express

articles.title: Binance’s Record $6.3B Crypto Hack as It Happened
articles.text:
As it happened: Binance’s record $6.3B crypto hack
How Binance’s $6.3 billion hack unfolded, from the first onchain alerts to $3 billion in frozen funds and a widening security investigation.
Live coverage has ended. The updates below document Cointelegraph’s reporting on the record $6.3 billion Binance hack as events unfolded.
What we know about the Binance hack:
- Binance says the estimated total impact is around $6.3 billion and the verified total value of crypto frozen is $3 billion. This could increase as investigators trace additional assets.
- Binance says deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are expected to resume as scheduled.
- Assets frozen include Tether USDt (USDT), USDC (USDC), Ripple USD (RLUSD), World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), StraitsX USD (XUSD), USDT0 (USDT0), Wrapped Beacon ETH (WBETH), Tether Gold (XAUT), Pax Gold (PAXG), Pax Dollar (USDP) and Arbitrum (ARB).
- Cybersecurity analysts suspect North Korea’s TraderTraitor is behind the attack.
- Binance says investigators have uncovered additional points of breach after initially pointing to a potentially compromised engineer’s laptop.
- Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the same tokens stolen.
Oct. 30 at 2:34 pm UTC
Binance targets withdrawals within 40 hours, reserves report by Monday
Binance is aiming to resume withdrawals within 40 hours and publish a full proof-of-reserves report by Monday, co-CEO Richard Teng said.
Teng said the exchange hopes to restore access before its Sunday deadline and provide an initial reserves snapshot ahead of Monday’s report.
Teng also disclosed that the attacker used a “self-destruct mechanism” to destroy tools and traces during the breach, complicating the investigation.
The attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to gain execution authority over a hot wallet, Teng said. That delegation “did not pass through our normal approval controls.”
Oct. 30 at 1:57 pm UTC
Aave lifts precautionary freeze across all V3 and V4 markets
New deposits and borrowing have resumed across all Aave V3 and V4 markets after a precautionary freeze following the Binance hack, the lending protocol said.
Withdrawals and repayments remained available throughout the freeze. Aave said its contracts were unaffected by the incident.
Founder Stani Kulechov confirmed that lending and borrowing were re-enabled, saying all positions remained overcollateralized.
Oct. 30 at 1:11 pm UTC
Binance working with FBI to recover assets following $6.3B hack
Binance is working with the FBI to help recover some of the funds stolen in the record $6.3 billion exploit, according to a source familiar with the matter said.
The cryptocurrency exchange revealed its cooperation with law enforcement in an X post, without specifying the agencies involved.
Oct. 30 at 12:41 pm UTC
Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses
A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the $5 billion in matching tokens is held in the exchange’s custody.
The spokesperson declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security reasons. Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.
The exchange also said it submits weekly reports on company funds to Abu Dhabi’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority under a requirement that predated the hack.
Oct. 30 at 11:07 am UTC
Yi He says Binance is buying altcoins to replace stolen tokens
Binance is buying altcoins in quantities matching those stolen in the hack as it prepares updated proof of reserves, co-CEO Yi He said.
The purchases are being made through over-the-counter deals and on exchanges, she said.
Binance’s SAFU fund and company holdings include substantial amounts of Bitcoin and Ether, Yi He said. The exchange would provide another update once the purchases were complete.
Oct. 30 at 11:00 am UTC
EIP-7702 may have helped Binance hackers bypass security checks
Attackers could have stolen Binance’s funds without Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade, but it may have helped them bypass security checks, Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph.
Ben-Natan said compromised signing systems likely enabled the attack. EIP-7702 provided “a way to do this in one sweep,” while attackers otherwise would have needed multiple transactions.
Ambire CEO Ivo Georgiev also said the funds could have been stolen through other methods. He warned that exchange engineers could overlook the need to revoke malicious EIP-7702 delegations after regaining control of their systems.
Oct. 30 at 10:55 am UTC
Binance says it reserved $6.34B in company funds for hack losses
Binance has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from the hack, the exchange said.
The company said $5 billion of those funds were already held in the same tokens affected by the attack. It was purchasing the remaining assets through market and over-the-counter transactions to address token shortfalls.
Some purchases could take longer because of low liquidity and OTC settlement times, Binance said.
The allocation excludes frozen or protected assets. About $3 billion remained frozen, with efforts to recover those funds continuing alongside law enforcement and industry partners.
Oct. 30 at 10:09 am UTC
Binance hackers may be automating laundering, Chainalysis says
The attackers behind Binance’s hack may be using automation to move and redistribute stolen funds, blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said.
“Our investigators are observing never-seen-before laundering patterns with the stolen funds from the Binance exploit,” the company said.
“Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation to obscure the trail of funds.”
Chainalysis said funds repeatedly circulated among addresses, sometimes returning to wallets used earlier in the sequence.
Oct. 30 at 08:37 am UTC
Binance finds additional breach points in hack investigation
Binance’s investigation into its $6.3 billion hack has uncovered “additional points of breach,” the exchange said, after initially pointing to a potentially compromised laptop.
The exchange said it was still gathering facts in coordination with law enforcement.
Binance said it remained on track to resume withdrawals in 45 hours, while deposits remained unaffected. Outflows from the exchange stopped when it paused withdrawals, it said.
Oct. 30 at 07:37 am UTC
Teng says Binance hack was not a single “one-click” action
The attacker behind Binance’s $6.3 billion hack did not simply use one engineer’s permissions to carry out the breach, co-CEO Richard Teng said.
In an X post, Teng said the incident involved “a more complex attack process” and was not a single “one-click” action.
“Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual,” he wrote.
Teng reiterated that preliminary findings pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which may have allowed the attacker to access an internal service and submit unauthorized withdrawals. He said investigators had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.
Binance would cover all losses using its SAFU fund and company funds, he said.
Oct. 30 at 05:01 am UTC
Analysts suspect North Korean group behind Binance hack
Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin said the Binance hack was likely carried out by North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor, citing links to a previous hack.
In a post on X, Levin put the theft at $6.4 billion, slightly above Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion impact. He said industry partners had frozen approximately $3 billion and Chainalysis was continuing to track the funds.
In a separate post, onchain investigator ZachXBT said the stolen funds from the Binance attack and the earlier Bitget exploit were commingled in the same address on Friday, after arriving via THORChain.
“This indicates the same actor is likely behind both incidents,” he said.
“The Bitget exploit was attributed to DPRK-linked TraiderTraitor, which had overlap with other previous exploits such as Kelp DAO,” he added.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan also said the attack resembled the work of North Korea, or DPRK, based on the sophisticated onchain preparations, customer sweeper contract and multiple authorizations.
TRM Labs has also attributed the attack to TraderTraitor with “high confidence,” which it said is “based on robust on and off-chain intelligence.”
TraderTraitor has also been named by the FBI as the same group responsible for the ByBit hack in February last year.
Oct. 30 at 4:17 am UTC
Binance expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours
Binance said withdrawals remain paused while it completes a security revamp of its withdrawal service and related addresses, with service expected to resume within 48 hours. Deposits are operating normally.
The exchange said the incident involved multiple factors and that its security team was tracing the full attack path through a compromised computer, which they suspect to be the entry point.
Oct. 30 at 03:49 am UTC
Binance hack could accelerate shift to DEXs: Standard Chartered
The Binance hack could push more crypto trading toward decentralized exchanges and benefit Uniswap over the longer term, according to Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, Geoffrey Kendrick.
In an email shared with Cointelegraph, Kendrick retained his $100 price target for Uniswap’s UNI token by 2030, saying the breach was “another reason why that forecast may end up being too low.”
CoinGecko research shows that the top 10 spot DEX-to-CEX ratio was 23.5% in the second quarter of 2026, climbing 2.1 percentage points from the first quarter of 2026.
“I would encourage investors to re-engage with Uniswap,” said Kendrick. “The decentralized exchange (DEX) has never had any exploits, and the hack of the largest centralized exchange (CEX), in Binance, should see the ratio of DEX to CEX trading continue to increase.”
Oct. 30 at 02:25 am UTC
Binance points to engineer’s hacked laptop in $6.3B breach
Binance said its initial investigation into the multi-billion crypto breach has pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop.
The exchange said the laptop compromise may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. It said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak, though its investigation remains ongoing.
The crypto exchange has also disclosed that the estimated total impact of the hack is $6.3 billion.
Oct. 30 at 02:21 am UTC
First Digital confirms it has frozen FDUSD involved in attack
First Digital CEO Vincent Chok said it has frozen the FDUSD stolen in the attack on Binance.
“We’re working alongside the Binance team and will share updates as we have them,” Chok told Cointelegraph in a written statement.
“Our priority is protecting FDUSD holders and stopping bad actors from moving stolen funds. Protecting users is a responsibility we all share.”
Oct. 30 at 01:19 am UTC
Bitcoin trades below $77,000 as BNB falls 8%
Bitcoin traded near $76,937, down 4.9% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. BNB fell 8% to about $693, while Ether declined 5.7% to about $2,211.
DeFi tokens also fell, with AAVE down 11.3% and Uniswap’s UNI down 10.7% over the same period.
The Bitcoin Fear and Greed Index, which tracks Bitcoin market sentiment, fell to “fear” with a score of 30, which it has not seen since August.
Oct. 30 at 12:52 am UTC
Binance says $3 billion frozen from hack
Binance said the current verified amount of assets frozen from the hack is now $3 billion.
The update came after the Arbitrum Security Council said it executed a transaction to freeze $30.5 million from the Binance exploit, involving 74.6 million Arbitrum (ARB) and 8,425 Ether (ETH).
“The Security Council acted by weighing its commitment to the security and integrity of the Arbitrum community and Arbitrum governance without impacting any Arbitrum users or applications,” it said.
“As of October 30, 2026 time, the funds have been successfully transferred to an intermediary frozen wallet,” it said.
The funds will no longer be accessible to the address that originally held the funds and can only be moved by further action of the Security Council or a vote of Arbitrum DAO governance, it added.
Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC
Chainalysis estimates $5.9 billion stolen from Binance
Chainalysis said its current estimate of the amount stolen from Binance is $5.912 billion at the time of theft, four times the amount stolen from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
Binance earlier said the verified total frozen is $2.54 billion.
Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC
Blockaid suspects Binance hack involved private key “misuse”
The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key.
“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.
Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.
Arkham CEO Miguel Morel said the attack appears to be ongoing.
Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC
Binance says deposits temporarily suspended
Binance said it has temporarily suspended deposits as it conducts security checks, freezes funds and coordinates with law enforcement. It previously confirmed it had suspended withdrawals.
“We are working around the clock and will share a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete,” the company said, adding it will “cover all losses.”
Earlier, Binance also said it had temporarily suspended Binance Alpha trading.
Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC
Wintermute and GSR disclose Binance exposure
Crypto trading firms Wintermute and GSR disclosed exposure to Binance but said they did not expect major disruption to their businesses.
The firms are market makers, which place buy and sell orders on exchanges to help other traders complete transactions. A disruption to their operations could make trading harder or more expensive across crypto markets.
GSR CEO Xin Song said its Binance exposure was less than 5% of its net equity, meaning the value of its assets minus its liabilities. He said GSR was working with Binance to understand the incident and identify ways to help.
Wintermute CEO Evgeny Gaevoy said his firm’s exposure was less than 20% of net equity and that he did not expect operational disruption.
Neither executive disclosed a dollar amount for the exposure or confirmed financial losses.
Oct. 29 at 11:40 pm UTC
Ripple freezes RLUSD linked to Binance hack
Ripple is freezing holdings of its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin linked to the Binance hack, according to Jack McDonald, the company’s senior vice president of stablecoins.
McDonald said Ripple was “actively freezing affected funds” and coordinating with relevant parties to support the investigation. He did not disclose the amount frozen.
Oct. 29 at 11:35 pm UTC
Binance says $2.54 billion frozen after hack
Binance said the verified total of assets frozen in connection with the hack had reached $2.54 billion, clarifying differing figures circulating publicly, including references to $1.8 billion.
The exchange said the total could increase as its teams work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets. Binance said it would publish further figures once verified.
Oct. 29 at 10:36 pm UTC
World Liberty Financial freezes $27 million in USD1
World Liberty Financial has frozen $27 million in US-dollar-pegged stablecoin USD1 and $2 million worth of WLFI, according to Binance co-founder Yi He.
“USD1 has taken proactive steps to freeze the $27 million in USD1 associated with the Binance hack,” said World Liberty Financial co-founder and CEO Zach Witkoff.
World Liberty Financial said it worked with BitGo to freeze the stolen WLFI and USD1 funds.
“We will cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation and support efforts to hold those responsible accountable. Protecting our users remains a top priority,” said World Liberty in a post on X.
Oct. 29 at 10:33 pm UTC
Binance says withdrawals will resume once issues resolved
Binance says its team is conducting security checks and will resume withdrawals as soon as the “security issue” is resolved.
Oct. 29 at 10:32 pm UTC
Aave freezes markets after Binance exploiter borrows $44.6 million
Decentralized lending protocol Aave froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments as a precaution following the Binance hack.
In a governance forum update posted after the freeze, risk service provider LlamaRisk said the Binance exploiter deposited 60 million USDT and borrowed 19,762 Wrapped Ether (WETH), worth about $44.6 million at the time.
The borrowing occurred between 8:58 pm and 9:01 pm UTC on Oct. 29, about 40 minutes before the first freeze. It was the exploiter’s only Aave position across all networks and versions, with no further interactions detected after 9:01 pm UTC.
The position remained backed by $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt at the update’s snapshot. LlamaRisk said it remained subject to normal liquidation and did not put Aave suppliers at risk.
The freezes covered 175 reserves on V3 across 16 networks and 117 reserves on V4 across four networks.
Users can still withdraw funds and repay loans, and liquidations continue. However, the freeze prevents new deposits and borrowing, including additional collateral deposits, leaving repayment as the only way to improve an existing position’s health factor.
LlamaRisk said markets would remain frozen until the exploiter’s funds stopped moving and Binance provided greater clarity on containment, followed by a staged reopening. It warned that a prolonged freeze could push borrowing rates higher as withdrawals reduce available liquidity.
Oct. 29 at 9:15 pm UTC
Binance investigates multibillion-dollar security breach
Binance is investigating a potential multibillion-dollar security breach involving one of its Ethereum wallets, after suspicious transfers prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to reportedly freeze billions in assets.
A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph on Thursday that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue but had not confirmed any impact on user funds. The spokesperson said its security teams were reviewing the activity and would provide updates once more information was verified.
Concerns were first raised by blockchain researcher Spreek, who posted on X that assets from a Binance-linked Ethereum wallet had been transferred to a newly created address through a contract call allegedly funded by Tornado Cash. Spreek later reported that wallets connected to the transfers had begun selling Tether USDt (USDT) through decentralized exchanges.
Blockchain analytics platform Arkham Intelligence later identified a collection of wallets labeled “binance-hacker-1029” holding approximately $5.84 billion in digital assets. The figure represents the wallets’ reported holdings rather than a confirmed estimate of stolen funds.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the activity appeared to be a hack, adding that Tether and Circle had frozen approximately $971 million and $823 million, respectively. Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.
Tether, Circle freeze over $2.36 billion
Blockchain security firm Blockaid said its team had identified roughly $3.3 billion in suspicious transfers involving Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche.
Shortly after news of the hack emerged, Tether and Circle, the two largest stablecoin issuers by market capitalization, said they had frozen a combined $2.36 billion in tokens linked to the suspected incident.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement and would continue supporting the investigation.
A few minutes later, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT linked to the potential exploit.
“Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority,” Ardoino wrote.
The Binance hack came hours after Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a compromise at a third-party provider. The prediction market platform said it had fixed the issue and pledged to reimburse affected users, with all systems reported operational by 7:05 p.m. UTC Thursday.
Reporting by Felix Ng, Bryan O’Shea, Nate Kostar and Yohan Yun.

articles.title: Binance Hack Shows Why Offshore Exchanges Need US Oversight, CFTC Chair Says - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told CNBC the $6.4 billion Binance hack “proves our exact point” for the crypto-market rules the agency proposed this month.
- Selig characterized the attack as a laptop-introduced vulnerability rather than a blockchain flaw—but Binance has since found “additional points of breach.”
- The CFTC chair cast on-chain traceability as a regulatory advantage.
The record-breaking hack of Binance is exactly why offshore crypto exchanges need U.S. oversight, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig argued, using the roughly $6.4 billion theft to press the agency’s case for a federal rulebook.
Speaking to CNBC on Friday, Selig said the breach “proves our exact point” behind the crypto-market regulations the agency proposed earlier this month.
“The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States,” he said, pitching a “federal option” that would let such venues register with the CFTC and submit to the same cybersecurity standards that govern U.S. markets.
Selig sought to downplay the role of blockchain itself in the attack. The exploit, he said, didn’t break the underlying blockchain, in this case Ethereum, or its smart contracts, but exploited a vulnerability he believed was “introduced from someone’s laptop,” the kind of incident that happens in traditional markets too.
The difference with crypto, he said, is speed: funds can move far faster, and attackers can route them through tools like Tornado Cash to obscure their trail.
Selig’s characterization, though, may be incomplete. Binance initially pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, but said Friday that its investigation had since uncovered “additional points of breach,” with CEO Richard Teng calling it “a more complex attack process” that “did not simply use one engineer’s permissions.”
And while the theft did not expose a flaw in Ethereum itself, the attack did play out partly on-chain: The attacker used EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets ordinary wallets run smart-contract code, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a “sweeper” using 50 pre-signed authorizations, draining its assets.
TRM Labs said the broader breach points to a compromise of Binance’s signing infrastructure rather than a weakness in any blockchain.
Selig framed the blockchain’s transparency as a regulatory advantage regardless. “The fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives regulators a lot of potential to be really cop on the beat here,” he said.
The comments sharpen a pitch Selig has been making for weeks. The CFTC has pressed ahead with its own crypto rulemaking rather than wait on Congress, sending the White House proposals that would define event contracts as “swaps” and floating a plan to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight, part of a broader shift in which regulators have taken the lead after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.
The Binance hack hands that effort a vivid talking point.The exploit is the largest in crypto history, with Binance setting aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and assuring users their assets are safe. The Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe, and TRM Labs and Chainalysis have tied the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

articles.title: Bitcoin Circles $77,000 as US Stocks and Gold Drop Amid Resurgent AI Fears
articles.text:
Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold
Bitcoin circled $77,000 as crypto markets navigated US stock-market downside, while the gold price fell to its lowest in a year.
Bitcoin (BTC) stayed under pressure below $80,000 at Friday’s Wall Street open as AI fears returned to intensify a broader risk-asset rout.
Key points:
- Bitcoin struggled to hold around $77,000 as risk assets fell across the board at the US open.
- The Nasdaq Composite Index fell to 25,500, its lowest levels since early August, while gold dropped to $3,891 per ounce for the first time since October 2025.
- BTC/USD risked sealing October losses or 7.7%, the most since 2014.
Tech contagion ramps up as Nasdaq drops 2.5%
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD down 1.1% on the day after dropping to its lowest levels since Sept. 18.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US stock markets opened sharply lower as traders reacted to weak forward guidance from tech giants. Intel, which on Thursday warned of weaker Q4 sales than markets had anticipated, saw its stock price drop by nearly 30% on Friday’s open.
The sell-off weighed on both tech giants and chipmakers, with analysis warning of fresh challenges to AI-sector confidence.
“With renewed fears over AI Monetization, the Equity rotation is likely to continue today but the broader indices will reflect Tech’s downside,” JPMorgan wrote in a note, quoted by CNBC.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was 2.5% lower at the time of writing at around 25,500, a level last seen on Aug. 3.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Beyond stocks, contagion spread to precious metals, with gold trading as low as $3,891 per ounce, its weakest in a year.
XAU/USD one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Bitcoin on track for weakest October since 2014
Crypto markets continued to deal with the aftermath of a multi-billion dollar hack of Binance, the largest crypto exchange.
Related: Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?
The platform said that it would cover the losses with its own capital after the theft of $6.3 billion in coins and tokens. A spokesperson told Cointelegraph that Binance had $5 billion in matching tokens currently available.
Commenting on the outlook for crypto, trading company QCP Capital warned that macro conditions, tech-sector fears and the Binance hack had “created a period of heightened market repricing.”
“Technology sector earnings guidance regarding future capital expenditure will remain a critical variable for understanding the trajectory of artificial intelligence infrastructure investment and expected profitability,” it summarized in analysis on Friday.
At $77,000, BTC/USD was set to close the month 7.7% lower — its worst October performance since 2014, per data from CoinGlass.

articles.title: Intel Stock Suffers Worst Crash in 50 Years as Weak Forecast Overshadows AI Chip Demand - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday, wiping out more than $146 billion in market value as investors reacted to a disappointing fourth-quarter forecast.
- Intel expects Q4 revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below Wall Street's $17.07 billion estimate, while adjusted earnings per share are forecast at $0.25 versus expectations of $0.43.
- Demand for AI server processors is booming, but manufacturing and packaging shortages are limiting production. Meanwhile, Intel expects the PC market to contract through 2027 and warned it probably won't generate positive free cash flow next year.
Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast that fell well short of Wall Street expectations, overshadowing an otherwise strong earnings report.
The selloff wiped out more than $146 billion in market value, and translated into the worst single-day decline in more than 50 years.
The problem is that Intel finds itself in an unusual position: demand for its processors is booming because of the AI infrastructure buildout, but the company cannot manufacture enough chips to capitalize on it. At the same time, its traditional PC business is struggling, and the factories needed to support its long-term recovery are consuming enormous amounts of money.
Intel's third-quarter numbers were actually quite good. Revenue climbed 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $0.52, beating the company's guidance of $0.38 and Wall Street's $0.40 estimate. It was the company's eighth consecutive quarter of exceeding its financial expectations, according to CFO Dave Zinsner.
The strongest performer was Intel's Data Center and AI division, which generated $7.3 billion in revenue, up 78% year over year and nearly 80% compared with the same period last year. The division's operating profit reached $3 billion, representing 42% of its revenue.
But investors were looking at what comes next. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning its midpoint guidance of $15.5 billion is roughly $1.6 billion below the $17.07 billion analysts had anticipated. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to fall to $0.25, compared with Wall Street's $0.43 estimate.
Gross margins, which measure how much revenue remains after accounting for the direct costs of making products, are also expected to deteriorate. Intel forecast a non-GAAP gross margin of 38% for Q4, down from 44.1% in the third quarter.
Three problems explain much of that deterioration: weaker PC demand, manufacturing constraints affecting server processors, and an accident at one of Intel's factories in Israel.
Intel CFO Dave Zinsner described 2027 as an investment year and warned investors not to expect positive free cash flow. Free cash flow is the money a company has left after paying operating expenses and investments in equipment and infrastructure. Intel expects to sacrifice cash generation in the short term to finance its manufacturing expansion.
"Probably not a dynamic where we are going to have positive free cash flow next year," Zinsner said during the earnings call. He added that Intel expects a return on invested capital of at least 20% on its manufacturing node investments, but acknowledged that several major projects will require substantial spending at the same time.
That spending is part of Intel's broader attempt to rebuild its manufacturing business and compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, the world's leading contract chipmaker. Intel wants to manufacture chips not only for its own products but also for outside customers, a business model known as a foundry.
The turnaround has attracted major partners. In September 2025, Nvidia invested $5 billion in Intel and agreed to collaborate on custom processors for PCs and data centers. The partnership gave Intel a financial boost while connecting its processors to Nvidia's AI ecosystem.
Intel's next-generation 18A process, the manufacturing technology behind chips such as Panther Lake, is central to the company's attempt to regain its technological edge.
More recently, a preliminary agreement with Apple to manufacture some of its chips helped send Intel shares above $130 in May. The potential deal could give Intel a significant new customer as Apple looks to diversify its manufacturing supply chain.
Those developments helped fuel optimism around Intel's recovery, but Friday's selloff shows how much still needs to go right. The company has strong demand in its data center business, yet it must increase manufacturing output, navigate a shrinking PC market and finance an expensive expansion before investors can expect consistent cash generation.

articles.title: Crypto Today: Crypto exchange Binance suffers $6.3B hack
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Coinbase led a selloff in crypto-linked stocks following Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack. Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses from the attack, which cybersecurity analysts have linked to a North Korean hacking group.
Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3B Binance hack
Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.
Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.
The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.
The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses
Binance said Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from its hack, with $5 billion already in held in the same tokens stolen.
“The $5 billion is held in the exact token assets that are required. These assets are in Binance custody,” a Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.
The spokesperson declined to disclose the wallet addresses, citing security reasons, but said that the holdings would appear in the exchange’s next proof-of-reserves report, which shows the assets it holds to back customer balances.
Binance said it provides weekly reports on its company funds to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market in the United Arab Emirates. The exchange said the requirement predated the hack.
Binance hit by $6.3 billion hack, analysts suspect North Korean group
Crypto exchange Binance said it has been hit with a security breach with an estimated $6.3 billion impact, with its initial investigation pointing to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that may have allowed attackers to submit unauthorized withdrawals.
The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak.
Industry partners helped freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets. Binance pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, saying user funds were safe.
Cybersecurity analysts have pointed to North Korean group TraderTraitor as likely having carried out the attack, citing links to a previous hack.
Withdrawals remain paused during a security revamp, with Binance expecting to resume within 48 hours.

articles.title: Worried About Crypto Hacks? Buy Bitcoin Proxies in Stock Market Instead, Say Wall Street Firms - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point told clients in Friday notes that the $6.4 billion Binance hack—the largest ever—is unlikely to derail crypto’s recovery, framing the selloff as a buying opportunity for crypto-linked stocks.
- Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal said “we would be buyers on weakness,” citing $3 billion in frozen funds; TD Cowen called it a Binance security issue, not a Bitcoin problem; Compass Point said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole.”
- Moody’s struck a more cautious note on hot-wallet and concentration risks.
Wall Street analysts are telling clients the record-breaking hack of Binance is a buying opportunity, not a reason to flee, urging investors to scoop up crypto-linked stocks while prices are depressed.
Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point said in Friday research notes that the roughly $6.3 billion theft, the largest crypto hack ever, is unlikely to derail the broader market’s recovery.
The reassurance came a day after the exploit rattled markets and sent Bitcoin sliding toward $77,000.
Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal pointed to how fast the industry moved to contain the damage, noting that stablecoin issuers and others froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen funds, with Tether freezing more than $1.5 billion, Circle about $800 million and Ripple around $200 million.
El-Assal expects shares of Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy to recover once the panic fades. “We would be buyers on weakness,” he wrote, adding that while the episode is painful, “this is not 2022.”
TD Cowen’s Lance Vitanza struck a similar note, arguing the breach exposed weaknesses in Binance’s own security rather than in the underlying technology behind Bitcoin, and framing the selloff as a chance to add to Bitcoin and the stocks of public companies that hold it.
Compass Point’s Ed Engel and Michael Donovan said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole,” while flagging that reimbursing customers could strain stablecoin supply and that rivals like Coinbase and Hyperliquid could pick up business. They are watching the $75,000 to $77,000 Bitcoin range as a key level.
The logic behind buying stocks over tokens is that regulated, exchange-listed proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy offer crypto exposure without the custody risk the hack laid bare, and tend to rebound once sentiment steadies.
Not everyone is sanguine. Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president of digital assets at Moody’s Ratings, said the incident “underscores the heightened cybersecurity risks associated with hot wallets” and “illustrates the risk concentration inherent in large, centralized intermediaries.”
He cautioned that the broader implications will hinge on “the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence.”
Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and told users their assets are safe, while the Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe and firms including TRM and Chainalysis have tied the hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

articles.title: Will Gold’s ‘Infinite Mint Bug’ Make Bitcoin More Valuable?
articles.text:
Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?
A US fusion startup says it has turned mercury into gold. Could a potential increase in the gold supply strengthen Bitcoin’s claim to be a better form of digital gold?
They say all that glitters is not gold, and that took on a completely different meaning this month when a US fusion startup claimed it had produced gold from mercury.
Rather than chemical trickery, Marathon Fusion’s process relies on nuclear transmutation. Its research paper describes how high-energy neutrons from a deuterium-tritium fusion reaction can irradiate mercury-198, producing a radioactive isotope that decays into stable gold-197.
So, if gold has what some are calling an “infinite mint bug,” what will happen to the centuries-old metal so revered for its scarcity? And what, if anything, could that mean for Bitcoin as digital gold given it has a hard-capped supply?
Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong sees events playing out in Bitcoin’s favor, and compared the creation of “net-new gold with alchemy” to the lab-grown diamond industry. “But you can’t invent anything that will increase Bitcoin supply,” he said. “There will only ever be 21M.”
Perhaps inspired by the popularity of lab-grown diamonds, Marathon co-founder and chief executive Kyle Schiller tells Magazine he’s been fielding a lot of interest from jewelers.
“We have gotten a shocking amount of interest from people who want to do jewelry,” Schiller says. “As with regular gold, I think it’ll be mostly used as a store of value.”
But before gold bugs start quaking in their boots, Marathon’s achievement is still a long way from proving gold can be produced cheaply at scale.
Nikos Kavalis, managing director at precious metals research firm Metals Focus, tells Magazine, “We are nowhere near a stage where we can talk about production significance.”
“While allusions to alchemical dreams make for great headlines, I think gold miners will get to keep their jobs for the foreseeable future!”
Can gold ever really be manufactured at scale?
The underlying nuclear process is scientifically plausible, but turning it into an economical industrial process is a whole new ball game.
Related: JPMorgan projects Bitcoin to outperform US stocks and gold over next decade
Marathon said it had produced stable gold at a rate 10 times CERN’s record, the European particle physics laboratory where scientists use powerful accelerators to study the fundamental building blocks of matter.
Nuclear fusion turned mercury into gold. Source: Marathon Fusion
But CERN’s ALICE experiment only produced an estimated 29 picograms of gold nuclei during its 2015-2018 run, and those nuclei only existed for fractions of a second before they were destroyed in collisions.
The company hasn’t publicly stated the exact quantity the experiment produced. Marathon research engineer Jake Harter tells Magazine the quantities remain extremely small, “right now still microscopic,” but the company hopes to reach “macroscopic milligram quantities in 2027.”
So the much larger numbers in Marathon’s paper are projections for a future fusion power plant, not based on output today.
The paper models production of about two tonnes of gold per gigawatt of thermal fusion power annually. To put that into context, the World Gold Council says that globally, mines produced 3,672 tonnes of gold in 2025, so a single future fusion plant’s output would be modest in comparison.
Even to reach those targets, Harter says the company would have to scale production of the enriched mercury used to produce gold, and of course it would need to build the fusion reactor itself.
“In the process of maturing this technology, we’ll also be working on studies demonstrating materials compatibility, mercury pumping and gold extraction,” he says.
Could gold follow the lab-grown diamond playbook?
It’s hard not to draw parallels like Armstrong’s between Marathon’s nuclear gold and lab-grown diamonds. Wholesale prices for lab-grown diamonds have fallen by more than 90% since 2018 as production has scaled up. Unlike older diamond substitutes like cubic zirconias, the composition of the newer lab grown diamonds is chemically identical to mined diamonds for a fraction of the price. Could the same thing happen to gold?
Marathon Fusion research paper. Source: Marathon Fusion
According to Nagham Hassan, a market analyst at investment platform eToro, the comparison with lab-grown diamonds is understandable, but “the economics are completely different.”
While diamond production became cheaper as factories scaled up, she said producing gold through nuclear fusion “would require highly complex infrastructure that does not yet exist commercially.”
Related: Bitcoin will become ‘less volatile’ and larger than gold: ‘The Bitcoin Standard’ author
Another complication is that the gold produced would be radioactive.
“The gold would need to be stored for a bit over a decade before dropping to banana-levels of [radio]activity,” Harter says, although, since most gold is “just stored as an investment,” he doesn’t see that as a major barrier to earlier commercialization.
A bigger problem is that it’s unclear whether the economics will ever stack up.
“There is no demonstration that the process is commercially viable,” Kavalis says. “There are theoretical revenue projections, but nothing about what it will cost to run the reactors.”
Would Bitcoin benefit if gold became less scarce?
Bitcoin is often described as digital gold because its supply is limited by its protocol rules and capped at 21 million but Armstrong argues that no one can invent a way to fabricate future coins.
If a future technology like nuclear fusion could create another source of gold supply, that could in theory place downward pressure on the price.
“For any asset, a substantial increase in available supply would, other things being equal, put downward pressure on its market price,” Fabian Schär, professor of distributed ledger technology and fintech at the University of Basel, tells Magazine.
“Under the hypothetical assumption of inexpensive production at scale, gold would be no exception.”
But with the first fusion reactors estimated to be at least a decade away, and plenty of questions remaining over the economic viability of this new form of alchemy, it’s unlikely to give Bitcoin prices a boost any time soon.
So for now, at least, Marathon’s work is more of a fascinating experiment with potentially interesting applications rather than an imminent threat to the gold market.
Peter Schiff and his buddies can breathe a sigh of relief.

articles.title: Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Reddit shares plunged 30.44% to $90.15 on Friday, extending their weekly decline to 44%.
- CEO Steve Huffman said Google search referrals fell by more than 1 million per week in October and warned daily active users could decline by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if the trend continues.
- Reddit forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below the roughly $1.05 billion analysts expected, despite reporting 53% revenue growth in Q3.
Reddit shares plunged 30.44% to $90.15 on Friday after CEO Steve Huffman warned that Google's AI-powered search features are cutting referral traffic and could shrink the platform's user base.
The selloff came after the company reported strong third-quarter results but issued a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast for the current quarter.
Reddit built much of its business around people discovering its discussions through Google searches, and those visitors are increasingly finding answers without ever clicking through to the platform. That puts pressure on the advertising business that has helped turn Reddit into one of the internet's fastest-growing publicly traded companies.
Reddit's third-quarter numbers initially looked healthy. Revenue climbed 53% year over year to $895 million, advertising revenue increased 54% to $847 million, and net income reached $283 million. Diluted earnings per share, which measure company profit attributable to each share while accounting for potential dilution, came in at $1.40, up 75% from a year earlier and above the $1.33 analyst consensus.
But the audience figures were less encouraging since Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active unique visitors, up 12% year over year but below the roughly 134 million analysts expected. In the U.S., the number actually fell 2% to 50.7 million, giving investors another reason to question whether the platform can maintain its growth.
Huffman delivered the warning during Thursday's earnings call, explaining that Google search referrals had fallen by more than one million on average every week during October, with the decline accelerating toward the end of the third quarter. If that pace continues, Reddit's total daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 from the current base of around 130 million.
Huffman pointed directly at Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, features that generate answers and summaries directly inside search results. Rather than sending users to websites to find information, Google increasingly gives them what they are looking for on its own page, pushing traditional search links further down.
Asked whether the changes were responsible for Reddit's declining search traffic, Huffman said the AI features had expanded aggressively in the U.S. and internationally. "The AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," he told investors.
That creates an awkward situation for Reddit—and arguably every other single media site on the internet. People can still search for Reddit discussions, but Google's results increasingly allow them to consume information from those discussions without visiting Reddit itself. Search referrals also bring back existing users, meaning fewer clicks can affect both new-user acquisition and the platform's ability to keep people engaged.
Reddit is trying to reduce that dependence by moving toward a primarily logged-in experience, which would require people to sign into an account before accessing most of the platform. The company plans to begin testing the change in selected markets outside the U.S. during the fourth quarter.
The strategy also connects to Reddit's increasingly important relationship with the AI industry. In February 2024, Reddit signed a reported $60 million-a-year data licensing deal with Google, giving the search giant access to Reddit discussions to train AI models. A few months later, the company announced a similar partnership with OpenAI, allowing the ChatGPT developer to use Reddit content while giving Reddit access to OpenAI's technology.
Those deals turned Reddit's enormous archive of human conversations into something it could sell to AI developers. But the same AI-powered search experience that benefits from Reddit's content can reduce the number of people who actually visit the site. Reddit also started tightening access to its public data and moving toward a more restricted platform which angered long term users.
The stock has now lost 44% over the past week, with Friday's 30.44% plunge accounting for a significant portion of the decline. At $90.15, Reddit is trading well below the levels it held just days ago.
The technical picture offers little immediate relief. Reddit's 50-day exponential moving average, a trend indicator that gives greater weight to recent prices, sits around $149.80, while its 200-day average is near $162.12. The 50-day average has already fallen below the 200-day average, creating a so-called death cross, a bearish signal commonly associated with a longer-term downward trend.
At $90.15, Reddit would need to climb approximately 66%—almost 70%—just to return to its 50-day average. That would only bring the share price back to the shorter-term trend line, not undo the death cross itself. With both averages sitting far above the current price, a recovery to those levels in the near term looks increasingly unlikely.

articles.title: Binance Hack: Why Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like It Did in 2018 - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, roughly 6% below its post-Fed level, after Binance's record $6.4 billion hack, versus a fall from $10,740 to $9,690 in minutes in March 2018 over an attack that Binance said stole nothing.
- Crypto's market value has grown from more than $400 billion in March 2018 to roughly $2.6 trillion, and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs now hold roughly 1.3 million coins.
- Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses, about $3 billion is frozen, and withdrawals should resume in 45 hours.
Bitcoin is down about 4% a day after the biggest crypto hack on record. In March 2018, a failed attack on the same exchange knocked nearly 11% off its price in minutes, and Binance said at the time that no funds had been stolen.
Binance has confirmed yesterday's attack, and Chainalysis and TRM Labs put the theft at roughly $6.4 billion, more than four times the previous record hack: the $1.5 billion Bybit heist of February 2025. Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, around 6% below where it traded after Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision.
More than $1.3 billion in leveraged bets was liquidated, meaning trades placed with borrowed money that exchanges close automatically when prices move against them. And yet Bitcoin is holding relatively steady, all things considered.
The 2018 incident was a phishing and theft attempt: attackers took over accounts, created API keys (credentials that let trading bots act on an account) and used them to pump the obscure coin Viacoin while 31 accounts that had pre-deposited the coin sold it. Bitcoin fell from $10,740 to $9,690 within minutes and kept dropping to about $6,600 by April 5, though the market was already in a bear run after peaking near $20,000 in December 2017.
To have a grasp of the situation, the entire crypto market was worth just over $400 billion in March 2018 and is worth roughly $2.6 trillion now.
A big reason for that, and why panic doesn't hit markets the same way anymore, is U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. Funds like BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust let people buy Bitcoin through an ordinary brokerage account, and they now hold roughly 1.3 million BTC, about 6% of the supply.
Their shareholders don’t keep coins on Binance, and sovereign wealth funds such as Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council have been buying. BlackRock’s fund alone took in $136 million on Wednesday, per Farside Investors data.
These funds don’t tend to panic sell so easily, and those funds remain locked for long periods of time.
The theft began at 4:05 p.m. ET Thursday, after U.S. markets closed, so Thursday’s preliminary $17 million of ETF inflows predate it and Friday’s flow figures are the first real read on whether those holders are selling.
The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no stablecoin issuer can freeze. The amount doesn’t account for other tokens, which would increase the holdings to more than $3 billion.
TRM and Chainalysis tie the attack to the North Korean group behind Bybit, which after that heist converted about 84% of the stolen Ethereum into Bitcoin through Thorchain, a cross-chain swap network.
Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover every loss, and it is buying the missing tokens on the open market and over the counter, meaning in private deals off the exchange. About $3 billion is frozen, deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are on track to resume in 45 hours.
Market sentiment was already soft before the theft and slid further: CoinMarketCap’s Fear and Greed index, a 0-to-100 gauge of market mood, dropped to 36 points from 43 (now in “fear” territory after being “neutral” yesterday), and Bitcoin sits about 38% below its $126,080 record. Back in 2018, the market was well in “extreme fear” territory at 12 points on the scale when the incident happened. Traders were already in panic mode, and the attack just worsened an already ugly situation.
Glassnode data show long-term holders underwater on about 4 million coins bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and HashKey analyst Tim Sun said before the hack that the market’s problem “is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest.”
So, taken all together, what it all boils down to is this: A more optimistic market, much more liquidity, active long-term investors, a clearer regulatory framework, a sense of safety thanks to that regulatory clarity, quick action by stablecoin providers, and a price trend in recovery likely all played a role in keeping Bitcoin safe from a global panic despite the record-breaking hack.

articles.title: Binance Working with FBI To Recover Assets after $6.3B Hack
articles.text:
FBI and Secret Service join response to Binance’s $6.3B hack
US agencies are investigating the theft and helping trace stolen assets, while Binance says about $3 billion has been frozen.
Update (Oct. 30 at 9:04 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include FBI and US Secret Service statements reported by Reuters and Bloomberg, along with Binance’s latest recovery and withdrawal plans.
The US FBI and Secret Service have publicly acknowledged their involvement in the response to Binance’s $6.3 billion hack as efforts continue to trace and recover stolen cryptocurrency.
The FBI told Reuters Friday it was working with government and industry partners to assess the incident’s scope and potential impacts and coordinate investigative steps.
Secret Service investigators were also “working around the clock” with private-sector partners to recover stolen funds, a spokesperson told Bloomberg on Friday.
The cryptocurrency exchange revealed its cooperation with law enforcement in a Friday X post, without specifying the agencies involved.
The exchange has separately reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the affected cryptocurrencies. A spokesperson told Cointelegraph those tokens were in Binance’s custody, but declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security concerns.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.
Withdrawals remained suspended Friday. Binance said it aimed to begin reopening them in stages from Sunday, subject to security checks, with proof-of-reserves results also expected Monday.
Binance ranks as the largest cryptocurrency exchange by reserves with $134 billion in total assets. It had processed about $6 billion in outflows during the past 24 hours, according to DefiLlama.
In February 2022, the US Department of Justice said law enforcement agencies, including the FBI, helped seize 94,000 Bitcoin (BTC), valued at $3.6 billion at the time, which were linked to the 2016 Bitfinex exchange hack.
Related: THORChain’s RUNE jumps 13% after Binance’s record $6.3B hack

articles.title: $8 Million Crypto Kidnapping Lands Texas Brothers 15-Year Prison Terms - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Texas brothers Raymond and Isiah Garcia were sentenced to a combined 326 months for a September 2025 home-invasion robbery that forced a Minnesota man to hand over more than $8 million in crypto; both pleaded guilty in June.
- The pair zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for over nine hours, even driving the victim to a cabin to retrieve hardware wallets, before fleeing and being arrested near Houston.
- Chainalysis logged 46 violent incidents against crypto holders and $30 million-plus stolen in early 2026.
Two Texas brothers have been sentenced to a combined 326 months in prison for a violent home-invasion robbery in which they held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for hours and forced the father to hand over more than $8 million in cryptocurrency.
Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced on Thursday to 180 months and 186 months respectively, or 15 and 15-and-a-half years, by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank in St. Paul, according to the Justice Department. Both had pleaded guilty in June.
According to court documents, the brothers traveled from Texas to Grant, Minnesota, and on Sept. 19, 2025, broke into the victim’s home, zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for more than nine hours while demanding access to the father’s crypto accounts.
When he failed to transfer the amount they expected, they forced him to drive one of the brothers to the family’s cabin in upstate Minnesota to retrieve additional hardware wallets and move the funds. In total, they compelled him to transfer over $8 million. The pair fled after the victim’s son called 911, and were later arrested near Houston.
“The Garcia brothers committed a brazen and calculated act of violence against the victim and his family,” U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said in a statement. The FBI’s Christopher Dotson said the brothers “violated the sanctity of a home” in “a brazen act of violence and greed.”
The case is a stark example of a “wrench attack,” in which criminals use physical force rather than hacking to seize crypto.
Such attacks have surged alongside crypto’s rising prices: Chainalysis counted 46 violent incidents in the first half of 2026 with more than $30 million stolen, while CertiK pegged losses even higher. Recent cases span a French kidnapping in which workers’ children were held hostage and a UK home invasion that ended in prison terms for the attackers.
The sentencing offers one of the clearest signals yet that U.S. courts are treating crypto wrench attacks as serious violent crime.
