articles.title: Binance Says It Holds $5B in Matching Tokens to Cover Hack Losses
articles.text:
Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses
The exchange said it set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses and would include the assets in its next proof-of-reserves report.
Binance said Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from its hack, with $5 billion already in held in the same tokens stolen.
“The $5 billion is held in the exact token assets that are required. These assets are in Binance custody,” a Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.
The spokesperson declined to disclose the wallet addresses, citing security reasons, but said that the holdings would appear in the exchange’s next proof-of-reserves report, which shows the assets it holds to back customer balances.
Binance said it provides weekly reports on its company funds to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market in the United Arab Emirates. The exchange said the requirement predated the hack.
The exchange has yet to confirm which tokens it still needs to purchase, when those purchases will be completed or how much stolen crypto has been recovered.
Related: EIP-7702 didn’t cause Binance hack, but may have amplified losses
The exchange confirmed Friday that it had suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said funds were drained from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains on Thursday and attributed the attack to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
Binance said about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen with help from blockchain partners. Those assets were excluded from the company funds set aside to cover losses.
CertiK awaits more details to verify Binance’s $5 billion holdings
CertiK told Cointelegraph that it needed more information from Binance to assess whether the claimed $5 billion in tokens matching those stolen could be independently verified on-chain.
Earlier Friday, CertiK CEO Ronghui Gu estimated that approximately $3 billion in frozen assets and Binance’s $1.17 billion emergency fund could cover about 66% of the reported losses, leaving a potential $2.1 billion gap.
Gu said the estimated gap represented about 1.3% of Binance’s reported $165 billion in exchange reserves. Those reserves include assets backing customer balances.
Binance founders cite revenue and existing holdings
Blockchain analytics company Nansen told Cointelegraph that it could not verify what funds Binance had available beyond its roughly $1.16 billion emergency fund or where the money to cover the remaining losses would come from.
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said Friday the company’s SpaceX holdings alone, linked to a $500 million investment in Elon Musk’s Twitter takeover, were worth more than $1 billion.
Binance co-founder Yi He said that the exchange’s revenue for the year was sufficient to cover the hack losses and that the company did not need to sell its stake in SpaceX.
Zhao also said Binance accumulates the cryptocurrencies it lists because customers can pay trading fees in those tokens. In a separate post, he said Gulf, Binance’s partner in Thailand, had offered financial support.
Zhao, who stepped down as CEO in 2023 and later served four months in a US prison over anti-money-laundering violations, remains a major Binance shareholder. Forbes estimated his personal fortune at approximately $115 billion.
Magazine: Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself

articles.title: Secret Service, FBI Join Binance Hack Probe as Circle Freezes $823 Million - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Binance is working with the FBI and U.S. Secret Service after hackers stole $6.4 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange, according to Reuters.
- Circle froze approximately $823 million in USDC connected to the attack, while Tether froze another $975.1 million in USDT. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company was coordinating with law enforcement.
- Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group previously linked to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.
Binance is working with the FBI and U.S. Secret Service after hackers stole $6.4 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange, as Circle joins the recovery effort by freezing more than $800 million in assets connected to the attack, according to Reuters.
A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Binance was cooperating with law enforcement agencies around the world, including both U.S. agencies. The FBI confirmed it was aware of the incident and was working with public and private partners to assess its scope and coordinate investigative steps. The Secret Service remained silent.
Investigating financial crimes is part of the Secret Service’s job, beyond its better-known responsibility of protecting the president. The agency also investigates computer crimes, unauthorized access to computer systems, and crimes involving digital currencies.
Circle, the company behind USDC, a stablecoin designed to maintain a value of $1, has separately confirmed that it is coordinating with law enforcement. CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC associated with the Binance incident and would continue supporting the investigation.
Tether, which issues the competing USDT stablecoin, froze another $1.5 billion in tokens. Both companies can blacklist specific blockchain addresses, preventing the tokens they issue from being transferred out of those wallets. That ability gives stablecoin companies an unusual role in crypto investigations: they can effectively immobilize stolen money before investigators identify the people responsible.
Tether froze more than 1.567B USDT related to a potential Binance exchange hack.
Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority.
Stay safe everyone.
— Paolo Ardoino 🤖 (@paoloardoino) October 29, 2026
This is not the first time the Secret Service has worked alongside crypto companies to investigate digital asset crimes. In April, Operation Atlantic—a joint effort involving the Secret Service, the U.K.'s National Crime Agency, Binance, Coinbase, and other crypto firms— identified more than 20,000 victims of approval phishing scams, traced $45 million in stolen funds and froze $12 million.
The Binance investigation also comes against the backdrop of a growing number of attacks attributed to North Korea. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both linked the $6.3 billion theft to TraderTraitor, a hacking group associated with the country's cyber operations. The same group has been linked to the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which the FBI also attributed to North Korean hackers.
North Korean attackers have targeted Binance itself before, including through attempts to infiltrate the exchange by posing as job applicants. In an interview with Decrypt in 2025, Binance Chief Security Officer Jimmy Su said North Korean operatives were contacting employees on LinkedIn every day, sometimes using fake interviews to deliver malware to their devices.
Binance has said it will cover all losses using company funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users, an emergency reserve designed to protect customers in the event of a security breach. CEO Richard Teng said on Friday that the company had reserved more than $6.34 billion to cover the stolen assets, while approximately $3 billion had already been located or frozen with the help of industry partners.
The exchange initially suspected that a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer had provided the attackers with access to its systems. It has since identified additional points of breach and said it found no evidence that wallet private keys had been leaked. Withdrawals remain suspended while Binance reviews its security infrastructure, with the company targeting a resumption by Sunday.

articles.title: Zcash Grants Group Offers $46M Amid Governance Backlash
articles.text:
Zcash grants group offers $124M compromise as governance backlash grows
Zcash Community Grants proposed redirecting about $124 million in existing and future funding toward mining rewards, but critics say the plan fails to address governance and accountability concerns.
Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) has proposed redirecting about $46 million in Zcash tokens from its treasury to future block rewards, but industry figures criticized the move, demanding greater accountability for the fund.
On Thursday, ZCG proposed transferring 36,200 ZEC from its roughly 91,500-ZEC treasury to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), which reserves coins for future mining rewards. If approved, the committee would retain about 55,200 ZEC, worth about $70 million at the time of writing.
The group also proposed forgoing about 62,000 ZEC ($78.5 million) in future allocations and tapering its remaining funding until the 2032 halving. Together, the changes would redirect about 98,000 ZEC (about $124 million) toward future block rewards.
Under the current arrangement, ZCG’s automatic allocation is scheduled to end in 2028. Its alternative would extend reduced funding for another four years.
ZCG said the plan was preliminary, with a full proposal to follow for community consideration.
Helius co-founder and CEO Mert Mumtaz called the proposal “nowhere near good enough,” saying the treasury was already too large and arguing that funding decisions should be accountable to ZEC holders
Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss also questioned the committee’s accountability after Mumtaz said a committee member had unfollowed him on X. Winklevoss said such behavior made someone unqualified to oversee $110 million.
The criticism follows Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe’s earlier proposal to end ZCG’s automatic 8% share of newly issued ZEC and redirect it to the NSM while leaving the existing treasury untouched.
Related: Winklevoss-backed Zcash ETF files with SEC for Nasdaq listing

articles.title: Binance Sets Aside $6.34B to Cover Hack Losses, CEO Says 'Your Assets Are Safe' - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange will cover all hacked losses, having reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds, $5 billion in the affected tokens.
- Teng said the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism to wipe tooling and traces, and an EIP-7702 delegation that bypassed Binance's normal approval controls.
- Binance aims to restore withdrawals by Sunday and publish a full proof of reserves by Monday, as the attacker keeps moving funds on Tron.
Binance will cover every dollar lost in this week's hack with its own money, CEO Richard Teng said in a video address on Friday, adding that customer funds were never touched.
"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said, according to a transcript he tweeted.
An update on the security incident. pic.twitter.com/qn2804fO5z
— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) October 30, 2026
Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens taken, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB, he said. The exchange is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels.
Teng said the hack hit Binance's own hot wallet, not customer funds. "We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," he said, adding that most user assets are held in cold wallets and only moved into a hot wallet when a user withdraws. Binance's ability to absorb a loss of this size comes from keeping much of its operating earnings in crypto, he said.
Binance had earlier said it would cover all losses from its SAFU emergency fund and company funds.
How the attack worked
Teng said the hack "was not carried out by one person." Binance initially traced it to a compromised laptop but has since found additional points of breach. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces along the way, making the attack harder to investigate, Teng said.
The attacker used EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature that lets standard wallets run smart contract code, to obtain onchain execution approval over a hot wallet, according to Teng. "That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls," he said, which is why Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and retest its infrastructure. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the theft to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
Binance hopes to restore withdrawals before its Sunday deadline, Teng said, and is carrying out a full security review covering endpoints, cloud, key management and signing. It plans to publish a full proof of reserves report by Monday, with an initial view before then.
The attacker is still moving funds. Between 11:37 a.m. and 12:12 p.m. ET on Friday, a Tron wallet that Arkham attributes to the hacker sent about 5.19 million TRX, worth roughly $1.73 million, to 12 addresses, according to Arkham data.
Update following the Binance incident:
All markets are now unfrozen across Aave V3 and V4.
They were frozen as a precaution after initial reports, which paused new deposits and borrows while withdrawals and repayments continued as normal.
Aave contracts were unaffected by the…
— Aave (@aave) October 30, 2026
Decentralized lending protocol Aave, where the attacker borrowed ETH against USDT while racing stablecoin freezes, according to TRM Labs, said on Friday that it had unfrozen all markets on its V3 and V4 deployments. It had frozen them as a precaution after the first reports of the hack, pausing new deposits and borrowing while withdrawals and repayments continued. "Aave was unaffected, and all positions remain overcollateralized," founder Stani Kulechov wrote.
Binance co-founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao said that while the $6.3 billion theft is the largest in dollar terms, it is not the largest in Bitcoin terms, pointing to Mt. Gox's loss of 650,000 BTC, more than 5% of the supply. Unlike at Mt. Gox and FTX, where nearly all users were affected, Binance is covering the losses itself, he said. "It hurts, but we survive," Zhao wrote.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Holds $76K After Binance Hack and Tech Sell-Off
articles.text:
Bitcoin price metrics hint at rebound as $1.6B liquidations follow Binance hack
Bitcoin held above $76,000 after a $6.3 billion Binance hack and a tech-stock sell-off, as momentum indicators pointed to a possible rebound.
Bitcoin (BTC) traded above $77,000 on Friday as crypto market liquidations passed $1.5 billion over 24 hours.
Key points:
- Bitcoin stemmed losses after dropping to $76,320 as markets processed details of a $6.3 billion hack on Binance.
- The effects of the hack on crypto markets were compounded by tech-stock losses that came with Q4 earnings projections. Intel Corporation (INTC) was down 26% premarket on Friday.
- Bitcoin’s relative strength index prints a bullish divergence on four-hour timeframes as sell-side pressure waned below $77,000.
US tech-stock sell-off adds to crypto jitters after Binance hack
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD dropping as low as $76,320 amid the fallout from a $6.3 billion hack of the largest cryptocurrency exchange Binance.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Rolling 24-hour liquidations of traders across the industry reached $1.56 billion. Long positions accounted for the majority of this figure at $1.31 billion, per CoinGlass data.
BTC/USD vs. crypto liquidations (screenshot). Source: CoinGlass
In its latest update on X, Binance described the attack as “complex,” reporting more than a single security breach during the episode.
“We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them,” it wrote.
Downside momentum cooled after the company confirmed that all user losses would be covered from its dedicated SAFU fund and other company resources.
The hack added to macro pressure on crypto, with US stock markets falling on Thursday after tech earnings fell short of expectations. Alphabet missed earnings and revenue targets on Wednesday. In the aftermath, GOOGL fell by 13% to $282, its lowest level since April.
Alphabet stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Intel shares plunged 26% premarket on Friday as the company issued a weaker-than-expected outlook, even though Q3 revenue and earnings beat estimates. Intel said it expects Q4 sales of $15 billion to $16 billion, versus analysts’ projected $17 billion to $18 billion.
Intel stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
BTC price bullish divergence emerges at local lows
On lower timeframes, BTC price metrics returned to levels not seen since BTC/USD hit multiyear lows near $57,000 in late June.
Related: Strategy eyes more Bitcoin buys as Saylor touts $30B credit capacity
On Thursday, price closed below the lower band of the Bollinger Bands volatility indicator, a phenomenon last observed on June 25. Such a move reflects that price is trading more than two standard deviations below its 20-day simple moving average (SMA). While Bollinger Bands do not produce buy and sell signals, a close below the lower band can imply that a mean reversion is due. The 20-day SMA currently sits at $81,324.
BTC/USD one-day chart with Bollinger Bands data. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The relative strength index (RSI), a popular leading indicator for price momentum, dropped to 34.7 on its 100-point scale on Friday. This is its lowest reading since June 30 and approaching its “oversold” zone below 30.
On the four-hour timeframe, RSI displayed a bullish divergence from the Bitcoin price, delivering a higher swing low compared to a lower low on BTC/USD. Such divergences can signal weakening seller control and a possible local trend change.
BTC/USD four-hour chart with RSI data. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

articles.title: Elon Musk, CZ Trade Blows Over SpaceX Shares After $6.4B Binance Hack - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- CZ asked Elon Musk to stop trolling Binance over its $6.3 billion hack, citing the exchange's SpaceX shares, which he values at more than $1 billion.
- Binance co-CEO Yi He said the company's annual revenue is sufficient to cover the losses without selling its SpaceX holdings. CZ later clarified that he had never suggested selling the shares.
- Binance has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, while TRM Labs and Chainalysis have attributed the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, better known as CZ, called out Elon Musk on Friday after the billionaire appeared to mock the exchange following a $6.4 billion hack—the largest in history—reminding him that Binance holds SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.
"Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," CZ wrote on X. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!"
The exchange followed Musk's response to a post estimating that, as a lot of the stolen funds have been frozen, Binance's losses could reach around $1 billion, despite holding approximately $144 billion in assets under custody.
Musk had replied to the discussion with a grimacing emoji, prompting another user to share an old post from former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried claiming his exchange had enough money to cover its losses. FTX famously collapsed weeks later.
Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop.
Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion.
Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!
— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026
CZ had initially responded to the loss estimate by saying the damage might be somewhat higher but that Binance would still be able to cover it. Musk's emoji appeared to draw an uncomfortable parallel with the FTX episode, although he did not elaborate on what he meant.
Of course, CZ didn't imply anything else about what Binance may do with its SpaceX shares.
Binance co-CEO Yi He also joined the exchange, addressing CZ in a post that appeared to respond to the suggestion that the company might need to liquidate its SpaceX holdings.
"Reporting to the major shareholder: Our company's revenue for the year is sufficient to cover the losses, so we do not yet need to sell the SpaceX shares you are bullish on," she wrote, adding a shrugging emoji.
CZ subsequently clarified that he had never suggested selling the shares. He said he was simply showing Musk some of the funds Binance had available, hoping to reassure him about the exchange's financial position.
😂 did say anything about selling SPCX shares, was just saying/showing some funds that he might know, so that he can be less worried.
— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) October 30, 2026
The argument comes as Binance deals with the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. At least $6.4 billion in crypto was taken from wallets associated with the exchange on Thursday, October 29, across multiple blockchains.
Just yesterday, initial reports showed that at least $5.57 billion had left Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Bitcoin, and Tron. The attackers moved funds through several transactions, including a transfer of more than $1.6 billion in USDT to a newly created Ethereum address.
The incident also exposed an important weakness in how cryptocurrency can be recovered after a theft. Tether and Circle, the companies behind the USDT and USDC stablecoins, froze approximately $1.8 billion in assets associated with the attackers in the initial response, then subsequently froze a total of $2.39 billion. Unlike those tokens, Ethereum cannot be frozen by a central issuer, making it harder to stop stolen funds once they are converted.
The attackers subsequently used decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap and lending protocol Aave to move funds into Ethereum. These platforms allow users to trade or borrow cryptocurrency without relying on a traditional intermediary to approve each transaction. Decrypt tracked wallets receiving tens of thousands of ETH through these operations, including 19,762 ETH borrowed against approximately $60 million in USDT.
The suspected attackers have also been linked to North Korea. In a Friday report, blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group previously blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. Chainalysis estimated the Binance theft at approximately $6.4 billion.
Binance has since said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the incident, including $5 billion already held in the same tokens that were stolen. The exchange said it is acquiring the remaining assets through market and over-the-counter purchases, which can take longer when certain tokens have limited liquidity.

articles.title: Binance $6.3B Hack Raises Questions Over Ethereum EIP-7702
articles.text:
EIP-7702 didn’t cause Binance hack, but may have amplified losses
Security experts said attackers could have drained Binance’s wallets without EIP-7702, but the Ethereum upgrade may have helped bypass withdrawal safeguards.
Compromised signing systems likely enabled Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, while Ethereum’s EIP-7702 upgrade may have helped attackers bypass security checks, according to blockchain security firm Blockaid.
Attackers could have stolen the funds without EIP-7702, Ido Ben-Natan, Blockaid’s co-founder and CEO, told Cointelegraph on Friday.
“The 7702 upgrade is a way to do this in one sweep and maybe a way to bypass some sort of checks they may have,” Ben-Natan said, explaining that attackers otherwise would have needed multiple transactions.
Binance confirmed Friday that it had suffered the $6.3 billion hack, the largest in crypto history, and pledged to cover all losses. The exchange said it uncovered additional points of breach after initially suspecting a compromised laptop belonging to one of its engineers.
EIP-7702 faced security concerns before Binance hack
Ethereum introduced Ethereum Improvement Proposal 7702 (EIP-7702) in May 2025 as part of its Pectra upgrade, allowing ordinary wallets to use smart-contract features such as bundled transactions and sponsored gas fees.
Security concerns emerged within weeks. In May 2025, crypto trading firm Wintermute reported that most early EIP-7702 delegations pointed to malicious contracts designed to automatically drain compromised wallets.
The risks resurfaced in September 2025, when holders of World Liberty Financial (WLFI) tokens reported losses linked to malicious EIP-7702 delegations.
Ethereum community member VEER cited security warnings raised during discussions of EIP-7702 in 2024.
VEER later said the Binance attack appeared broader than a single malicious signature, but that EIP-7702 gave attackers “a handy sweep button on Ethereum.”
Signing-system compromise suspected
Binance CEO Richard Teng said investigators had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked.
Ben-Natan said attackers may have used a compromised developer’s computer to gain access to Binance’s wallet-signing infrastructure.
“Eventually they got to a position where they could propose transactions to what is most likely a very secure signer that has custody of one of Binance’s hot wallets,” he said. “The takeaway is that ultimately the signer signed a transaction that they shouldn’t have,” he said.
Live updates: Binance uncovers more breach points in $6.3B hack
Ivo Georgiev, co-founder and CEO of Ethereum wallet provider Ambire, said that EIP-7702 made little difference to the attack because the hackers already had the ability to authorize transactions.
He said attackers could have drained the funds through other methods, but warned that exchange engineers might overlook the need to revoke a malicious EIP-7702 delegation after regaining control of their systems.
“This is a problem with EIP 7702, it’s just very, very poorly understood,” Georgiev said.
Ben-Natan warned that similar signing-system attacks threaten other exchanges and said transaction simulation could help detect malicious requests before they receive approval.

articles.title: What is EIP-7702? The Ethereum Upgrade Behind the $6.4B Binance Hack - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- EIP-7702 is an Ethereum upgrade, activated in May 2025, that lets standard wallets temporarily take on the abilities of smart contracts.
- It enables batched transactions, gas sponsorship and limited-permission keys, but delegated code gets full access to the wallet's funds.
- An attacker used EIP-7702 in October 2026 to drain a Binance hot wallet during a $6.4 billion hack that analysts attributed to North Korea.
Ethereum has two kinds of accounts. Externally owned accounts (EOAs), the standard wallets most people use, are controlled by a private key and can do little more than send transactions. Smart contract accounts can run code, enabling features like spending limits, account recovery and paying fees in tokens other than ETH, but most users never moved to them.
EIP-7702 is an attempt to bridge that gap. Instead of asking users to migrate to new wallets, it lets existing EOAs borrow the code of a smart contract while keeping their address and funds.
This guide explains what EIP-7702 is, how it works, why developers wanted it, and how attackers used it in the largest crypto theft on record.
What is EIP-7702?
EIP-7702, titled "Set Code for EOAs," is an Ethereum Improvement Proposal written in May 2024 by Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and developers Sam Wilson, Ansgar Dietrichs and lightclient, according to the official specification.
It was one of the headline changes in Pectra, a major Ethereum upgrade that went live on May 7, 2025.
"EIP-7702 lays the foundation we've needed for a long time," Ethereum core developer Preston Van Loon told Decrypt at the time. "While full abstraction won't be immediately available to end users with Pectra, this upgrade gives Ethereum the infrastructure to support it moving forward."
EIP-7702 is a change to Ethereum's core protocol, not a token or a separate blockchain, so there is nothing to buy.
How does EIP-7702 work?
EIP-7702 adds a new type of Ethereum transaction, the "set code transaction." It carries a list of authorizations, each signed with the private key of the account being upgraded, that names the address of a smart contract the account wants to use.
Once the transaction is processed, the account stores a small pointer, called a delegation indicator, to that contract. From then on, whenever anyone calls the account, Ethereum runs the contract's code as if it belonged to the account, with full access to its funds.
The delegation lasts until the account owner signs a new authorization, either pointing to a different contract or clearing the pointer to restore a plain EOA.
Did you know?
EIP-7702 marks delegated accounts using the byte 0xef, a code value that was banned in earlier upgrades so it could be reserved for special purposes like this.
What's so special about EIP-7702?
The specification names three main features it was designed to deliver:
- Batching: combining several actions, such as approving a token and then swapping it, into a single transaction.
- Sponsorship: letting another account, such as an app, pay transaction fees on a user's behalf, with the user possibly reimbursing it in another token.
- Privilege de-escalation: creating sub-keys with limited permissions, such as spending only a certain token or only 1% of a balance per day.
The security risks
Those same features carry risks. Because delegated code gets "unrestricted access to the account," apps should never ask users to sign an EIP-7702 authorization, and wallets should not offer an interface for it, the specification warns. "There is no safe way to provide this interface," it says.
Scammers moved quickly. Within weeks of Pectra's launch, trading firm Wintermute found that more than 80% of EIP-7702 delegations pointed to copies of the same malicious "sweeper" contract, which automatically drains wallets whose keys have leaked, The Block reported in June 2025.
EIP-7702 and the Binance hack
On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved some $6.4 billion out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it within about 20 minutes. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis both attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, the North Korean hacking group behind the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.
On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 authorizations signed in advance, according to TRM Labs. An operational wallet funded through crypto mixer Tornado Cash submitted the signed authorizations, which let the hot wallet run attacker-deployed code, and the attacker then called the wallet to sweep its assets into addresses it controlled, Chainalysis said.
Crucially, EIP-7702 delegations require a valid signature from the account being upgraded. Binance wallets on the other nine chains also sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers, which TRM said points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure rather than a flaw in Ethereum itself.
Binance has said its investigation began with a compromised engineer's laptop, and has since found "additional points of breach."
The future of EIP-7702
EIP-7702 is a first step toward full account abstraction, a long-standing goal of making every Ethereum account as flexible as a smart contract. Its authors designed it to be forward-compatible with that "endgame," so wallets built on it today should keep working as Ethereum's account model evolves.
The next step could come with Hegotá, the upgrade planned to follow Glamsterdam on Ethereum's roadmap. In February 2026, Buterin said that EIP-8141, which he called "an omnibus that wraps up and solves every remaining problem" account abstraction was meant to address, looked "possible to make happen within a year" in the Hegotá fork.
Now, account abstraction.
We have been talking about account abstraction ever since early 2016, see the original EIP-86: https://t.co/HYLSTLHgWH
Now, we finally have EIP-8141 ( https://t.co/jYqeS55j6P ), an omnibus that wraps up and solves every remaining problem that AA was…
— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) February 28, 2026
"We have been talking about account abstraction ever since early 2016," Buterin wrote, adding that developers are also discussing whether existing accounts could join the new framework, which would give them batching and sponsored transactions natively.
It is part of a wider rebuild. In July 2026, Buterin described a new draft of Ethereum's long-term roadmap as the network's biggest overhaul since the Merge, its 2022 switch to proof of stake.

articles.title: Binance Hacker Holds More Bitcoin Than Coinbase’s BTC Treasury
articles.text:
Binance hacker’s Bitcoin haul tops Coinbase’s corporate treasury
The attackers held 18,270 BTC early Friday, topping Coinbase’s reported corporate holdings, and an Ether stash exceeding 500,000 ETH.
The attackers behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack held more Bitcoin on Friday than crypto exchange Coinbase’s holding for investment and operation at the end of September.
Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery traced 18,270 Bitcoin (BTC), worth roughly $1.4 billion, to 19 addresses linked to the attacker.
Coinbase reported holding 17,954 BTC for investment and 117 BTC for operations as of Sept. 30, a combined 18,071 BTC. The Binance hacker’s haul exceeded that total by 199 BTC. Coinbase’s holdings do not include the BTC that the exchange holds for customers.
BitcoinTreasuries.net ranks Coinbase eighth among publicly traded companies by Bitcoin holdings, based on its 17,954 BTC investment balance.
Binance confirmed Friday that it had suffered a $6.3 billion hack and said about $3 billion in stolen assets had been frozen. The exchange pledged to cover all losses.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group. Binance said investigators had uncovered additional breach points after initially suspecting a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer.
According to Bitquery, 17 of the attackers’ Bitcoin addresses held 1,000 BTC each, while the remaining coins sat in two other wallets. The BTC was stolen from Binance hot wallets during a breach that affected nine blockchains in under four hours on Thursday.
Bitquery also traced 508,621 Ether (ETH) to the attackers as of the same Friday snapshot, exceeding the 495,362 ETH that BitcoinTreasuries.net attributes to The Ether Machine, which ranks third on its list of corporate Ether holders.
The attackers initially stole 200,630 ETH and accumulated the rest by swapping stolen stablecoins and other tokens, Bitquery added.
Live updates: Binance uncovers more breach points in $6.3B hack

articles.title: Israel Extradites Alleged Nomad Bridge Exploiter to US Over $2.8M Theft: Report - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Israel has extradited Alexander Block, formerly Alexander Gurevich, to the U.S. to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad in 2022.
- Prosecutors allege that his exploit exposed a flaw that other users then used to drain more than $186 million from a Nomad-controlled wallet.
- Israel's Supreme Court rejected his appeal, ruling that exploiting a programming flaw can be unlawful computer intrusion even where the software permitted it.
Israel has extradited an Israeli-Russian citizen to the United States to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad, Israel's State Attorney's Office announced on Thursday, according to a report in The Jerusalem Post.
Alexander Block, formerly known as Alexander Gurevich, was transferred to U.S. authorities early Thursday after unsuccessful appeals in Israel. He was arrested at Ben Gurion Airport in May 2025 while preparing to fly to Russia, shortly after changing his surname and obtaining a passport in his new name.
A federal grand jury in the Northern District of California indicted Block in August 2023 on four counts of computer fraud, one count of transporting stolen property and three counts of money laundering, according to Israel's Supreme Court judgment in the case. The U.S. requested his extradition in December 2024.
According to the U.S. extradition request, as set out in the judgment, a June 2022 software update left a flaw in Nomad's smart contracts that let users receive tokens on one blockchain without locking up the equivalent assets on another. Block, operating under the username "Bitlik," allegedly made six test transfers before carrying out four main transfers around August 1, 2022, receiving tokens worth more than $2.8 million. He then allegedly moved the tokens through several wallets and converted them into other cryptocurrencies to conceal their origin.
His actions exposed the flaw to other Nomad users, who drained a Nomad-controlled wallet holding more than $186 million in user funds, the request alleges. A few days later, Block returned some of the tokens and contacted a senior Nomad official on Telegram, offering to return the rest in exchange for payment for finding the flaw. He later cut off contact, and Nomad went to U.S. law enforcement.
The Supreme Court ruling
The Jerusalem District Court approved Block's extradition in July 2025. On appeal, he argued that the transactions used functions available within Nomad's automated system, and that the public record of blockchain transfers undermined the money laundering allegations.
The Supreme Court rejected both arguments, holding that exploiting a programming flaw could constitute unlawful computer intrusion even where the software technically permitted the action, The Jerusalem Post reported. It also found that publicly visible transactions do not necessarily identify the people behind wallets or rule out efforts to conceal where funds came from.
Supreme Court President Isaac Amit later rejected Block's request for a further hearing, according to the State Attorney's Office.
The August 2022 exploit drained Nomad of nearly all its funds. Because it took little technical knowledge to copy the original attack, Paradigm researcher Sam Sun likened what followed to "a frenzied free-for-all," Decrypt reported at the time.
In December 2025, the Federal Trade Commission proposed a settlement with Illusory Systems, Nomad's operator, saying the bridge lost $186 million after hackers exploited a poorly tested software update. The settlement would require the company to return recovered funds to users who have not been reimbursed. Nomad recovered about $22 million in the days after the hack.

articles.title: RUNE Token Surges 13% Following $6.3B Binance Hack
articles.text:
THORChain’s RUNE jumps 13% after Binance’s record $6.3B hack
North Korean hackers previously used THORChain to move funds stolen from Bybit and Bitget, prompting calls for the protocol to intervene.
THORChain’s RUNE token rose more than 13% on Friday after Binance confirmed a $6.3 billion hack.
RUNE climbed to $0.67 at the time of writing from a local low of $0.59 at 12:20 a.m. UTC, according to TradingView data.
Onchain investigator ZachXBT reported Friday that funds stolen from Binance and September’s Bitget hack had passed through THORChain before being combined at the same Ethereum address.
ZachXBT said the Bitget attack had been attributed to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor. TRM Labs and Chainalysis also linked the Binance hack to the group.
THORChain allows users to swap assets across blockchains. North Korean hackers previously used the protocol to launder funds stolen in the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in February 2025. The protocol was also used to move funds stolen in the $388 million Bitget hack.
Following Bitget’s exploit, CEO Gracy Chen called on THORChain to block the attacker’s addresses, saying, “Decentralization is a design principle, not a shield for facilitating known stolen funds.”
THORChain rejected the request, saying it has no mechanism to block individual swaps. It said node operators can pause trading for an entire blockchain or across its network to address security risks.
The Bybit hack also divided contributors as core developer Pluto announced his departure after a halt on Ether trading was reversed. Validator TCB threatened to leave unless the protocol stopped processing North Korea-linked funds.
Related: THORChain generates $5M in fees, $5.4B in volume since Bybit hack

articles.title: Morning Minute: Binance’s $6.4B Hack Overshadows Hyperliquid’s Biggest Day - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors rebound fall 1-2% alongside stocks; BTC at $77.5k
- Binance hacked for $6.4B by NK, roughly half frozen; Binance to cover losses out of SAFU fund
- AAVE forced to freeze v3 and v4 markets on Ethereum after attacker used them
- Polymarket paused trading after front-end extension hacked, leading to user losses
- HYPE soars after NYSE partnership, Druckenmiller and Elon touts
Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Overshadows Hyperliquid’s Biggest Day
Someone stole about $6.4 billion from Binance. That is, by a wide margin, the biggest crypto theft that has ever happened, four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.
The money left across three different blockchains: roughly $3.5 billion in ETH, $1.4 billion in BTC, and $630 million on Tron (final accounting still underway).
Luckily, stablecoin issuers can freeze their own tokens; it’s a kill switch built into USDT and USDC. Tether and Circle used it, locking up about $2.39 billion between them. That’s 43% of the haul. That leaves somewhere between $2.6 and $3.2 billion still out there.
Aave also stepped in, freezing its V3 and V4 markets on Ethereum. That’s precautionary, given the worry is an attacker using stolen money to borrow against and leave the protocol holding bad debt.
As this was playing out, Binance stated it’s “aware of reports of a potential security issue” and that user funds are “completely safe,” and paused withdrawals on multiple networks. The clearest comment came from CZ, who no longer runs Binance but is its largest shareholder: it “does look like a hack,” and he expects user funds to be “fully covered.” Later in the evening, Binance announced that it has reserved over $6.34B in company funds to cover losses. So funds are indeed “safu.”
ZachXBT shared that the Binance hack funds were commingled with funds from the $388M Bitget exploit, leading him to believe it’s the same hacker group out of North Korea behind the attack. As for how it happened, Binance pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop which was compromised, allowing the attacks to submit the unauthorized transactions, before identifying "additional points of breach" in the following hours.
Markets did what you’d expect. Bitcoin fell below $797,000, ETH fell sub-$2,200 and BNB sub-$700. Over $1.33B in positions got liquidated on the day.
Unfortunately, this came after what was shaping up to be one of the most positive days for a crypto project in its history.
Earlier on Thursday, Trade.xyz announced that Intercontinental Exchange (the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange) is investing in it. The plan is a regulated U.S. venue offering round-the-clock perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid: stocks, indices, commodities, currencies and crypto, with its own exchange and clearing setup, pending CFTC approval.
Stanley Druckenmiller is joining as well, the first of a small group of outside market figures. He already owns the trade; his family office disclosed a $23 million position in Hyperliquid Strategies earlier this year.
So Hyperliquid has its path to a fully regulated perps offering inside the U.S., claims Stanley Druckenmiller as an investor (and a tout on X), and ICE’s CEO said that Hyperliquid was “bigger than NASDAQ.” Doesn’t get much better than that.
I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz) as they partner with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States. As a market participant, I am looking forward to to using their innovative product to enhance my investment process.
— Stan Druckenmiller (@standuquesne) October 29, 2026
HYPE shot as high as $97 on the day, up more than 20% at peak, before falling to $89 in the Binance hack aftermath. As of this morning, it’s at $93 and still up 8% on the day.
Unfortunately, now we have to deal with the Binance hack aftermath. Hyperliquid is a likely winner as a primary DEX option vs CEXs like Binance (which will likely be less trusted now.) But there’s also a good chance of the entire market being dragged down by fears of more exploits looming.
We will find out soon enough. Expect a bumpy ride…
🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are red in the Binance hack aftermath; BTC -3.6% at $77.5k; ETH -4% at $2,235; SOL -4% at $97; HYPE +8% at $92; ZEC -2% at $1,250
- Top alt movers include PEPE (+8%), SKY (+5%) and ZRO (+2%)
- Oil +2% at $104; Gold -1.2% at $3,980
- Stock futures are red after Amazon fell 12% post-earnings; DOW flat, Nasdaq -2.6%
- Aave froze every DAO-operated V3 and V4 market (292 reserves across 16 networks) after a wallet tied to the Binance exploiter deposited $60 million in USDT and borrowed 19,762 WETH worth about $44.6 million in a three-minute window
- Coinbase posted $719 million in Q3 profit against analyst expectations of a 15-cent loss, though about $715 million of it came from gains on crypto the company holds
- Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna, Carnival and Arcos Dorados blocked tokenized versions of their shares on the OKX-ICE venue, taking the count to 38 in two weeks
- Crypto groups have spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races, with Fairshake and its affiliates accounting for $150.8 million through October 20
- Roughly $11 billion in Bitcoin options expire on Deribit Friday, about 135,000 BTC and a third of open interest, with max pain at $78,000 against a market near $81,500 and calls outnumbering puts nearly two to one
- Trezor told anyone who bought one of its wallets from reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds immediately, after a customer in Indonesia reported finding an extra circuit board inside a Safe 5 with a cellular module that reads whatever the screen displays
Corporate Treasuries & ETFs
- The Bitcoin ETFs saw $17M in net inflows on Thursday; the ETH ETFs saw $105M in net outflows
- Strategy reported $19.53 billion in Q3 net income, nearly all of it a $20.91 billion paper gain on Bitcoin
Meme Coin Tracker
- Meme leaders were mostly red; DOGE -4%, SHIB -3%, PEPE +8%, PENGU -8%, TRUMP -8%, SPX -10%, BONK -4%
- Robinhood chain leaders were red; Pons -15% to $160M; Cashcat -10% at $90M; AI -12% at $63M; Index +50% led top movers
- Solana top movers included Hyperchan +40x, Purr +50%, and GTA6 +25%; Stonk -8% to $105M
💰 Token, Airdrop & Protocol Tracker

articles.title: Trezor Warns CryptoBilis Buyers Over Suspected Wallet Implant
articles.text:
Trezor warns CryptoBilis buyers to move funds over suspected implant
Trezor urged customers who bought devices from CryptoBilis since March to move their funds after a report of a suspected hardware implant.
Trezor has urged customers who bought its hardware wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds after a report of a suspected implant in a Safe 5 device.
Trezor said Friday that a customer in Indonesia reported an unauthorized circuit board inside a Trezor Safe 5 bought on Tokopedia in August. According to the report, the suspected implant could capture information displayed on the device’s screen, including wallet recovery phrases, and transmit it over a cellular network.
Trezor said it had not yet examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.
“We haven’t had the device in our lab yet, but we’re treating the report as credible, and we’d rather warn people now than wait for confirmation and find out someone lost their funds in the meantime,” Trezor chief commercial officer Danny Sanders told Cointelegraph.
A Trezor spokesperson said that the company described sales through the reseller as “very small” but declined to provide figures.
The spokesperson added that Trezor has not established where the suspected tampering occurred and is reviewing its hardware protections, acknowledging that existing safeguards, including seals and packaging, are not sufficient on their own.
Ledger tampering and earlier warnings to Trezor
The warning follows reports of crypto losses involving Ledger wallets sold through CryptoBilis that surfaced on Oct. 9. Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one device.
Security researcher Joe Grand previously told Cointelegraph that he had alerted Trezor in August about tampered Trezor One and Model T wallets bought through unauthorized sellers on TikTok and Facebook. Trezor said its earlier claim of no evidence of compromised devices applied only to new wallets sold through authorized resellers.
Trezor said at the time that its setup checks targeted counterfeit devices and modified firmware, while the implant found in a CryptoBilis-sold Ledger read the screen without changing the firmware. A stolen recovery phrase can let an attacker restore a wallet on another device and move its funds.
Trezor announced plans to reduce its reseller network on Oct. 13.
Related: Tampered Ledger wallets cost Singapore users $2.7M: Police

articles.title: TRM and Chainalysis Tie $6.4B Binance Hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.
- Chainalysis said it saw Binance funds commingling with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit, which had been attributed to North Korean actors.
- Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover losses, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.
Three blockchain analytics firms have attributed this week's hack of Binance to North Korea, with two of the largest naming TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group, as responsible for what both describe as the largest crypto theft on record.
TRM Labs said it made the attribution "with high confidence," based on "robust on and off-chain intelligence." It put the theft at about $6.36 billion, moved out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes from 4:05 p.m. ET on Thursday. That is about four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025, which the FBI attributed to the same group, TRM noted.
Chainalysis, which put the total at about $6.4 billion, said the strongest evidence came when its investigators saw funds stolen from Binance commingling in real time with funds from last month's Bitget exploit, which had been attributed to North Korean actors.
A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had "high confidence" North Korea was behind the hack. Singapore-based Pangolin Intelligence also told CNN it believed a North Korean hacking unit was responsible, based on "analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents." North Korea has previously denied hacking allegations.
TRM and Chainalysis both said the attacker's operational wallet was funded through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixer. TRM said that and other features, including staging that began well before the theft, matched earlier North Korea-linked attacks such as the Bybit hack and April's KelpDAO exploit.
How the attack worked
On Ethereum, the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation, a feature introduced in Ethereum's Pectra upgrade that lets an ordinary wallet run smart contract code, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 pre-signed authorizations prepared in advance, according to TRM. Binance wallets on the other nine chains sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's assessment, that points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure.
Binance has said its investigation began with a compromised engineer's laptop, but has since uncovered "additional points of breach." The Bybit attack also began with a single compromised machine: North Korean hackers planted malicious code in the infrastructure of wallet provider Safe after compromising a Safe developer's computer, Decrypt reported at the time.
The attacker has moved quickly to launder what it could not keep. Chainalysis said it is seeing "never-seen-before laundering patterns," with thousands of transactions in a short period suggesting the use of automation to circulate funds repeatedly among addresses. The attacker also sold USDT to market makers and borrowed ETH against USDT on lending protocol Aave to race issuers' freezes, according to TRM, and now holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion beyond any issuer's reach.
Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial have frozen about $2.67 billion in stablecoins, and Arbitrum's Security Council froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB, TRM said. Binance puts the total frozen at about $3 billion.
Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.
The company has already publicly committed to cover losses through… pic.twitter.com/UqtBd37Fpj
— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026
In an update on Friday, Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the incident, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen. It is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels, which "can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity," the exchange said. Those figures do not include frozen assets.
"We will weather this storm," Binance said.
North Korean hackers have long targeted the exchange. In August 2025, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su told Decrypt that North Korean attackers try to get hired at Binance every day, and called them the single biggest threat to crypto companies. On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity over North Korean IT worker schemes that moved millions of dollars in crypto.

articles.title: Strategy Eyes More Bitcoin Buys With $30B Credit Capacity
articles.text:
Strategy eyes more Bitcoin buys as Saylor touts $30B credit capacity
Michael Saylor says Strategy could create up to $30 billion in digital credit without new common-stock fundraising or further Bitcoin price gains, as the company plans more BTC purchases.
Bitcoin treasury company Strategy is looking to finance more Bitcoin purchases through preferred-share offerings, with executive chairman Michael Saylor saying it has the capacity to create as much as $30 billion in digital credit.
During Strategy’s third-quarter earnings call, Saylor said the company could generate the amount using its existing balance sheet, without an additional common-stock capital raise or further Bitcoin price appreciation.
“We could create $10 billion, $20 billion, $30 billion of digital credit,” Saylor said.
The potential financing capacity highlights the company’s shift toward preferred shares such as STRC to fund Bitcoin accumulation rather than relying primarily on convertible debt or common-share sales.
CEO Phong Le said during the call that issuing digital credit would be the main method for acquiring more Bitcoin. “The primary way to acquire Bitcoin is by issuing digital credit,” Le said.
Le said that if Strategy raised $1 billion to $2 billion in a month through STRC, it could put some proceeds into dollar reserves and spend the rest on Bitcoin.
The company reported $19.53 billion in third-quarter net income, driven largely by a $20.91 billion gain in the value of its digital assets. Its Bitcoin holdings reached 848,517 BTC as of Oct. 25, up 26% year to date.
The $30 billion figure represents a possible capacity, not an announced fundraising target.
Strategy also disclosed that CFO Andrew Kang will step down on Nov. 5 for personal reasons, with Le overseeing the finance function until Reza Virasteh takes over as CFO on Jan. 1, 2027.
Related: Strategy skips Bitcoin purchases, spends $205M on STRC buybacks

articles.title: North Korea’s TraderTraitor Linked to $6.3B Binance Hack
articles.text:
North Korea’s TraderTraitor linked to $6.3B Binance hack
TRM Labs said it has high confidence in the attribution, while ZachXBT identified stolen funds from the Binance and Bitget hacks converging at the same address.
Cybersecurity researchers from TRM Labs and Chainalysis, along with onchain investigator ZachXBT, have linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.
TRM Labs attributed the attack to TraderTraitor with “high confidence,” citing onchain and offchain intelligence.
ZachXBT said funds stolen from Binance and the earlier Bitget exploit were commingled at the same address after moving through THORChain.
“This indicates the same actor is likely behind both incidents,” he said, adding that the Bitget attack had been attributed to TraderTraitor.
Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin also pointed to TraderTraitor, saying the group stole $6.4 billion, slightly above Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion impact.
“We assess Binance hack for $6.4B was likely done by DPRK group TraderTraitor due to links to previous hack,” he said.
The attribution follows an earlier assessment by Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan, who told Cointelegraph that the attack’s sophistication and onchain preparations resembled North Korean activity.
US authorities have linked TraderTraitor to some of crypto’s largest thefts, including the Bybit hack in February 2025. The FBI also joined US and Japanese investigators in attributing the theft of more than $300 million from DMM Bitcoin in May 2024 to the North Korean actors.
The FBI says TraderTraitor targets company employees through social engineering. In the DMM case, an attacker posing as a recruiter sent a malicious coding test to an employee of wallet provider Ginco. Investigators said the resulting access was likely used to manipulate a legitimate transaction request, diverting funds to attacker-controlled wallets.
Related: Bitget CEO suspects North Korea behind $352M hack, citing IP clues

articles.title: Maple locks $280M in XRP collateral and upcoming maturity dates threaten liquidations
articles.text:
Quick Take
- DefiLlama attributes roughly $281 million of Maple collateral to XRPL, while the underlying loans originate from Ethereum pools.
- Three XRP-backed positions carry about $151.8 million in nominal stablecoin principal, with December and January maturities.
- Renewals can extend XRP collateral use, while repayments followed by authorized releases could reduce the pledged footprint.
XRP Ledger's reported DeFi value includes roughly $280 million in XRP collateral backing Maple loans funded from Ethereum pools, offering a reason to hold the token while borrowing stablecoins.
Yet the staying power depends on what happens to those loans. Maple reported about 225 million XRP across its syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT products, and three displayed XRP-backed positions carry approximately $151.8 million in nominal stablecoin principal, with maturities in December and January.
Borrowing against XRP can let an existing holder access liquidity while keeping exposure to the token. Renewals can extend that use, repayments can lead to authorized releases, and a failed margin call can lead to sales.
The credit behind XRPL's collateral total
Maple's syrupUSDC disclosure listed 142,766,086.05 XRP valued at $177.7 million, and its syrupUSDT disclosure listed 82,314,668.8 XRP valued at $102.5 million.
Together, the reported balances total about 225 million XRP and $280.2 million in displayed collateral.
| Product | Loan principal | XRP collateral value | Maturity | 
|---|---|---|---|
| syrupUSDC | 41.6 million USDC | $74.2 million | Dec. 4, 2026 | 
| syrupUSDC | 55 million USDC | $103.5 million | Dec. 12, 2026 | 
| syrupUSDT | 55.2 million USDT | $102.5 million | Jan. 15, 2027 | 
The combined principal is approximately $151.8 million at a nominal dollar per USDC or USDT. The two syrupUSDC loan collateral values are already included in that product's XRP total.
Three positions also do not establish three distinct beneficial borrowers. Maple's Borrower Hub supports multiple legal entities within one organization, so loan count alone cannot show how widely the exposure is distributed.
The public disclosures do not establish these positions' exact collateral-release approvals or timing, so repayment would be key for the token holding demand, in conjunction with what collateral is released, retained, or pledged again.
DefiLlama showed Maple's XRPL allocation at $281.1 million and total XRPL DeFi value at roughly $318 million in the same retrieval window. The key to interpreting that large contribution is where the collateral sits.
The Maple adapter says loans are issued from Ethereum pools while collateral is custodied on its native chain, crediting XRP to XRPL. This is native XRP supporting credit originated elsewhere, and is also specific to XRP-backed positions.
The adapter explicitly disables historical backfilling because its collateral metadata is current, so asking for an old block would return today's collateral and rewrite the past with present holdings.
That limits the chart's historical meaning: current holdings cannot establish when XRP was acquired or how much entered during a comparable earlier period.
How repayments and margin calls change XRP demand
The displayed collateral levels were 178.3% and 188.2% for the two USDC positions and 185.7% for the USDT position.
Maple's undated, currently hosted default procedure says initial, margin-call, and liquidation loan-to-value levels are set for each loan at origination. A margin call starts a 12-to-24-hour timer and gives the borrower instructions to top up collateral or repay.
Posting additional XRP could increase the tokens committed to the loan, whether drawn from existing holdings or acquired separately. Paying down debt offers another response and need not increase XRP collateral.
An uncured call, a breached liquidation threshold, or specified contractual default can authorize liquidation. Under the procedure, collateral-sale proceeds reduce principal, interest, and fees before a residual shortfall is impaired, so liquidation can turn pledged XRP into sales.
The strongest evidence of durable credit use would be XRP remaining committed through renewals that continue to require it, or being pledged against replacement loans after existing obligations are repaid. Larger token quantities would show a bigger collateral footprint.
Conversely, repayments followed by authorized releases would reduce the amount supporting this credit. A lower dollar-valued balance alone would be ambiguous because price changes can shrink collateral value without any tokens leaving.
The December and January maturities provide concrete points to watch for those changes. Until then, Maple's disclosures show XRP performing a financing role. Whether that role sustains demand for XRP beyond the current loans will depend on borrowers continuing to need the token as collateral.

articles.title: Trezor Warns CryptoBilis Buyers After Report of Hardware Implant in Safe 5 - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Trezor said it received a credible report of a hardware implant in a Safe 5 bought from reseller CryptoBilis in August, though it hasn't examined the device yet.
- The implant reportedly reads the wallet backup from the screen and sends it over a mobile network, which Trezor says appears similar to Ledger's case.
- Trezor urged anyone who bought one of its wallets from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to move their funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase.
Hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor has warned customers who bought its devices from reseller CryptoBilis to move their funds, after a buyer reported finding a hardware implant inside a Trezor Safe 5, the company said on Friday.
A customer in Indonesia reported the implant through Trezor's responsible disclosure program on October 28, according to a company blog post. The Safe 5 was bought from CryptoBilis through Indonesian e-commerce platform Tokopedia in August 2026.
CryptoBilis update
We've been made aware, through responsible disclosure, of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device bought from the reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026.
No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to us.
IMPORTANT: If you bought a Trezor from… pic.twitter.com/TiaKfHBnX2
— Trezor (@Trezor) October 30, 2026
The report describes an extra circuit board fitted between the device's main board and its screen, with a cellular module and an antenna. According to the report, which Trezor said it has not verified, the board reads what the screen shows, including the wallet backup, and sends it out over a mobile network whenever the device is plugged in.
Trezor has not yet received the device, but said it is treating the report as credible based on the customer's description and a video interview. "What we've seen looks sophisticated enough that we decided to warn customers now," it said. "Waiting for lab confirmation would leave CryptoBilis buyers exposed in the meantime."
No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to Trezor, the company said.
Trezor urged anyone who bought one of its wallets from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase as soon as possible, and not to reuse the old phrase on any device. Buyers who have not yet set up their device should not use it. Affected customers can keep their CryptoBilis device and contact Trezor Support for a replacement.
The CryptoBilis incident
Trezor removed CryptoBilis as a reseller on October 9, after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger began investigating losses among customers who bought its devices from the Southeast Asian reseller. Trezor has since inspected four of its devices bought from CryptoBilis, a Safe 7, two Safe 5s and a Safe 3, and found no evidence of tampering.
Ledger's Donjon security team found an implant in Ledger devices sold through CryptoBilis that reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the screen during setup and sends it out over LTE. Trezor's blog says the newly reported implant "appears to operate similarly," though the company added that it won't draw comparisons while investigations are ongoing and doesn't know who is behind it.
Ledger has said that all confirmed losses involve devices bought from CryptoBilis, and asked resellers in seven Asian markets to pull its devices. One of the largest victims was a scammer who lost more than 60 BTC, worth about $4.8 million, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis.

articles.title: MetaMask adds Stellar integration, but cross-chain bridges require manual setup
articles.text:
Quick Take
- MetaMask added Stellar to Mobile and Extension on Oct. 29, placing addresses in existing multichain accounts.
- MetaMask’s documented flow needs at least 1 XLM initially, plus 0.5 XLM reserved for each token trustline.
- MetaMask warns bridging without a trustline can lose funds, while ordinary Stellar sends without one fail.
MetaMask added Stellar as a default network on Oct. 29, giving users a new route for stablecoin payments within the wallet.
Before an unfunded account can receive assets such as USDC through MetaMask's documented flow, it needs XLM funding and the receiving token activated.
The launch announcement says Stellar is live in MetaMask Mobile and Extension, with a Stellar address derived from the recovery phrase in existing users' multichain accounts. That brings the payments network into an account they already use, alongside assets on other networks.
Fund the account, then activate the token
MetaMask's Stellar instructions require a first deposit of at least 1 XLM for a new, unfunded address.
To prepare for USDC, users open Manage Tokens, enable the desired token, open its entry marked Inactive, choose Activate, and confirm the transaction. Merely adding the token to the visible list does not complete activation.
Under Stellar's current reserve rules, an ordinary unsponsored account must maintain 1 XLM, plus another 0.5 XLM for each ordinary trustline. Other account entries can increase the minimum, and transaction fees need spendable XLM above the reserve. The locked balance remains in the account.
Stellar's network rules also allow another account to sponsor these reserves, including the base account reserve.
Users need spendable XLM to complete activation: the reserve increase and network fee cannot come from the amount already locked.
A swap between tokens already on Stellar can automatically create a trustline in MetaMask. For a cross-chain swap into a non-XLM token, MetaMask requires the receiving trustline to be activated manually first.
MetaMask says it prompts users before bridge confirmation and warns that bridged funds can be lost if the trustline is missing when they arrive.
That warning differs from an ordinary Stellar token send to a recipient without the required trustline. In that case, MetaMask says the send fails.

articles.title: Binance Hack Could Boost Uniswap: Standard Chartered
articles.text:
Binance hack could accelerate shift to DEXs: Standard Chartered
Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick said the breach could accelerate a shift toward decentralized trading and strengthen his case for Uniswap’s UNI token reaching $100 by 2030.
The Binance hack could accelerate a shift in crypto trading toward decentralized exchanges, benefiting Uniswap over the longer term, according to Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, Geoffrey Kendrick.
In an email shared with Cointelegraph, Kendrick said the breach should drive further growth in decentralized exchanges’ share of trading relative to centralized platforms, though investors should wait until after the impact of the Binance attack has time to play out in the markets.
“I would encourage investors to re-engage with Uniswap,” said Kendrick. “The decentralized exchange (DEX) has never had any exploits, and the hack of the largest centralized exchange (CEX), in Binance, should see the ratio of DEX to CEX trading continue to increase.”
CoinGecko research shows that the top 10 spot DEX-to-CEX ratio was 23.5% in the second quarter of 2026, climbing 2.1 percentage points from the first quarter of 2026.
Kendrick said he retains his $100 price target for Uniswap (UNI) for 2030, but said the Binance hack is “another reason why that forecast may end up being too low.”
The forecast builds on Standard Chartered’s earlier thesis that assets locked in DeFi could reach $2.7 trillion by 2030, with Uniswap emerging as a key trading venue for tokenized assets.
Looking at the broader implications of the Binance hack, Kendrick said he expects there will be further negative price action in the near term.
Cointelegraph reported that cryptocurrency markets extended their decline early Friday following the Binance hack, with BNB down more than 8% over 24 hours and Bitcoin trading near $77,000. Decentralized finance tokens also declined. Aave’s AAVE fell 11.3% to $118.54, while Uniswap’s UNI dropped 10.4% to $6.48, according to CoinGecko.
“Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base,” said Kendrick.
Live updates: Binance says $6.3B hack involved compromised engineer’s laptop

articles.title: Binance Finds 'Additional Points of Breach' in $6.3B Hack - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Binance has estimated the total impact of Thursday's security incident at around $6.3 billion, and said about $3 billion of it has been frozen onchain.
- The firm initially pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, but now says its investigation has uncovered "additional points of breach."
- The exchange said it will cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company funds, and has reopened deposits while withdrawals remain suspended.
Binance has uncovered "additional points of breach" in Thursday's security incident, which it estimates cost around $6.3 billion, the exchange said on Friday, after initially pointing to a compromised engineer's laptop.
In an announcement late Thursday, Binance said a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop may have allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak," the exchange said.
Investigation update: Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.
This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination… pic.twitter.com/FQQ3vKT6GU
— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026
Binance CEO Richard Teng said on Friday that the attacker "did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action," describing "a more complex attack process." "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual," he wrote.
"This was a complex attack," Binance said in its latest update, adding that it is still gathering the facts. Outflows stopped when it paused withdrawals, and it remains on track to resume them in 45 hours, the exchange said.
I want to speak to you directly about what happened.
Bottom line - your money is safe, and we're covering every loss.
Our initial investigation suggests this security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. That gave an attacker access to a…
— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) October 30, 2026
About $3 billion of the affected assets has been frozen onchain with the help of blockchain partners, Binance said. The exchange said it will cover all losses from its SAFU fund, an emergency reserve for users, and from company funds, and that "user funds are safe."
Binance initially suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization, and is working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the funds. By Friday morning, deposits were "operating as normal," Teng said, while withdrawals remain suspended as the exchange completes "a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses."
"We'll share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and every fact is verified—and publish an updated Proof of Reserves once remediation is complete," Teng wrote.
Blockchain analytics firm Arkham put the haul at $6.01 billion, taken from Binance hot wallets on nine blockchains between 4:10 p.m. and 7:05 p.m. ET on Thursday, it said in a tweet. Issuers had frozen $2.80 billion of it, but $2.9 billion in Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and other tokens could still be moved, according to Arkham.
The attacker has kept moving funds. Early Friday, the wallets sent $38.82 million in Ethereum to a new address, while still holding $1.12 billion in ETH, Arkham said. Hours later, a Tron address tagged by Arkham as belonging to the attacker sent about $2.1 million in TRX to nine new addresses in 14 transfers, according to Arkham data.
The stablecoin freeze
Stablecoin issuers moved quickly as the funds left Binance. Tether and Circle froze about 975.1 million USDT and 823 million USDC held in the main receiving wallet, worth about $1.8 billion, Decrypt reported on Thursday, when an onchain tally put the drain at $5.57 billion. Binance co-founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao thanked the two issuers for their "quick freeze."
As of Friday morning, Arkham's entity page for the attacker showed holdings of about 18,270 BTC, 488,364 ETH, 663.6 million TRX and 970,551 SOL, alongside frozen stablecoin balances.
