articles.title: Antarctica’s “Doomsday Glacier” could raise sea levels twice as much as predicted
articles.text:
Antarctica’s “Doomsday Glacier” could raise sea levels twice as much as predicted
A startling new model reveals that Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier could cause twice as much sea level rise as previously predicted, even without additional global warming.
- Date:
- October 28, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Irvine
- Summary:
- Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier may be melting twice as much as previously predicted, even without additional global warming. Scientists discovered that warm ocean water is penetrating miles beneath the ice, weakening its foundations and accelerating its retreat. A new model predicts that the glacier could add up to 30 millimeters to global sea levels by 2100, with a 60% chance of losing a crucial stabilizing ridge.
- Share:
A new computer model suggests that Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier, often called the "Doomsday Glacier," could contribute far more to rising sea levels than scientists previously estimated. Developed by researchers at the University of California, Irvine, and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the model predicts that melting from the massive West Antarctic glacier could raise global sea levels by as much as 30 millimeters by 2100. That is double earlier projections, even without any additional warming of the climate.
The findings, published in Nature Communications, reveal why earlier models may have underestimated the glacier's retreat. Instead of treating the boundary between grounded and floating ice as a narrow line, researchers accounted for a much broader area where ocean water can reach beneath the glacier. With this change, the model reproduced historical changes in Thwaites from the 1990s to the present that were four times more pronounced than those represented by conventional models.
Warm Ocean Water Is Melting Antarctica's Ice From Below
"Glaciologists have long based their assumptions of ice sheet dynamics on the 'grounding line,' a discreet, narrow and mostly stable demarcation where ice leaves the land and begins floating on water," said lead author Mattia Poinelli, who was a UC Irvine postdoctoral scholar in Earth system science when the research was conducted. "We have come to acknowledge a different arrangement beneath Earth's major ocean-terminating glaciers. Satellite observations demonstrate the existence of a 'grounding zone,' sometimes kilometers wide, where warm ocean water is reaching deep underneath the ice sheets and causing vigorous melting."
Thwaites Glacier lies in West Antarctica's Amundsen Sea Embayment, a region responsible for approximately one third of the Antarctic Ice Sheet's total mass loss. Over recent decades, the glacier has become thinner and retreated rapidly. Scientists have also observed its ice flowing increasingly quickly, but traditional computer models have struggled to reproduce the acceleration detected by satellites.
To investigate the discrepancy, the UC Irvine-led research team compared its simulations with more than two decades of observations. The researchers also analyzed synthetic aperture radar measurements collected by Finland's ICEYE satellite constellation, which revealed fluctuations extending across several kilometers of the grounding zone along the glacier's main trunk.
The satellite evidence shows that seawater travels several kilometers beneath ice that remains grounded on the seafloor. As tides rise and fall, the water lifts the ice and repeatedly exposes its underside to warm, pressurized seawater. The water reaches Antarctica's coastline through ocean currents that have been altered by climate change, creating conditions that accelerate melting beneath the glacier.
Thwaites Glacier Could Lose a Critical Underwater Anchor
The consequences extend beyond the melting itself. According to Poinelli, who is also a NASA JPL research affiliate and now works as a project scientist at UCLA, the movement of water beneath Thwaites is weakening its connection to underwater ridges that help keep the glacier in place. As these natural supports lose their grip, the ice can flow faster, and the glacier can retreat more rapidly.
"The Thwaites main trunk is being temporarily stabilized by the Mouginot Ridge," he said. "Once that ridge is unpinned, the glacier will continually retreat across a predominantly retrograde seafloor toward its next topographic high, the South Ridge."
The team's simulations suggest that this critical change could happen before 2100. When the model includes a grounding zone measuring 4 to 6 kilometers across, it predicts a 60% probability that Thwaites will become detached from Mouginot Ridge by the end of the century.
"When you factor in key physical processes and calibrate against historical observations, you gain a reliable pathway for narrowing uncertainty in projections," Poinelli said.
New Model Points to Greater Coastal Flooding Risks
The updated projections suggest that scientists may have underestimated the contribution Thwaites Glacier will make to future sea level rise. By more accurately representing how warm ocean water interacts with the underside of the ice, the new model produces results that better match the glacier's observed changes and indicate substantially greater ice loss ahead.
"We have documented and quantified the impacts of climate change on our planet's sensitive ice sheets for decades, but a mounting realization gained in recent years of what is happening on the undersides of glaciers like Thwaites is leading to an even greater sense of alarm," said co-author Eric Rignot, UC Irvine professor of Earth system science. "Most projections up to the present have struggled to match the rapidity of the mass loss because of missing physics; our new model with more complete physics is able to match the record and then produces projections that are twice as large as before. These results predict greater risk of and exposure for coastal flooding than anticipated in the coming decades."
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Irvine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Mattia Poinelli, Eric Rignot, Hélène Seroussi, Joshua Cuzzone, Tyler Pelle, Eric Larour. Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model. Nature Communications, 2026; 17 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-77976-1

articles.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.text:
A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- University of Nottingham
- Summary:
- A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.
- Share:
A simple daily fiber supplement may offer a surprising new way to relieve knee arthritis pain while improving muscle strength. In a clinical trial led by researchers at the University of Nottingham, people with knee osteoarthritis (OA) who took a prebiotic fiber called inulin experienced significant reductions in pain, improved grip strength, and decreased sensitivity to pain.
The supplement also appeared to be considerably easier for participants to stick with than a digital physical therapy program. Only 3.6% of those assigned to inulin alone dropped out of the study, compared with 21% of those assigned to physical therapy alone.
Published in the journal Nutrients, the findings suggest that improving gut health could become an additional strategy for managing arthritis. They also reveal an intriguing connection between the bacteria living in our digestive system, the way our bodies process pain, and muscle function.
A Simple Dietary Change Could Help Relieve Arthritis Pain
Knee osteoarthritis affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide and is a major cause of chronic pain and disability, especially among older adults. The condition develops as the tissues within the knee joint, including the cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, gradually deteriorate. This can lead to pain, stiffness, swelling, and difficulty with everyday activities such as walking or climbing stairs.
Treatment typically focuses on reducing symptoms and maintaining mobility. Pain medications can provide relief but may cause unwanted side effects, while physical therapy and regular exercise can help improve joint function. However, keeping up with an exercise program can be difficult, particularly for people already struggling with persistent pain.
The new research raises the possibility that a simple dietary supplement could provide another way to manage symptoms.
"This study raises the exciting possibility that a simple dietary change -- adding a fiber supplement to your breakfast or yogurt -- could meaningfully reduce pain and improve physical function," said Dr. Afroditi Kouraki, lead author of the study from the School of Medicine at the University of Nottingham.
The supplement tested in the study was inulin, a naturally occurring fiber found in foods such as chicory root, Jerusalem artichokes, and certain other vegetables. Unlike many nutrients, inulin is not broken down by digestive enzymes in the small intestine. Instead, it passes into the large intestine, where beneficial bacteria can use it as food.
How Gut Bacteria May Influence Arthritis Pain
Researchers are increasingly discovering that the gut microbiome, the vast community of microorganisms living in the digestive tract, influences much more than digestion. These microbes interact with the immune system, produce biologically active compounds, and may even affect how the nervous system responds to pain.
Inulin is classified as a prebiotic because it nourishes certain beneficial gut bacteria rather than directly supplying living microorganisms, as probiotics do.
When bacteria ferment inulin, they produce substances known as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). One of the most important is butyrate, a compound that helps support the intestinal lining and can influence inflammation and biological pathways involved in pain.
The researchers found that participants taking inulin had increased levels of butyrate, suggesting that the supplement was influencing activity within the gut microbiome.
They also observed higher levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), a hormone released by the gut that helps regulate blood sugar and appetite and has also been linked to pain regulation and muscle health.
GLP-1 has attracted widespread attention because it is the hormone targeted by medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy. However, the inulin supplement used in this trial was not a GLP-1 medication. Instead, researchers examined whether supporting beneficial gut bacteria could influence the body's own production of the hormone.
One particularly interesting finding was that higher GLP-1 levels were associated with better grip strength. Although this does not establish that GLP-1 caused the improvement, it suggests that changes originating in the digestive system may be connected to muscle function as well as pain.
Fiber Supplement vs. Physical Therapy
To investigate these effects, the researchers conducted the INSPIRE trial, a six-week randomized controlled study involving 117 adults with knee osteoarthritis.
Participants were assigned to one of four treatment groups: a daily inulin supplement alone, digitally supported physical therapy exercises (PSE) alone, a combination of inulin and physical therapy, or a placebo.
This design allowed researchers to examine the effects of the supplement and exercise separately, as well as investigate whether combining them offered additional benefits.
Both inulin and physical therapy independently reduced knee pain, indicating that each approach provided meaningful symptom relief.
However, the supplement produced additional improvements that were not observed with physical therapy alone. Participants taking inulin demonstrated better grip strength and reduced pain sensitivity.
Pain sensitivity reflects how strongly the nervous system responds to potentially painful stimulation. Reducing that sensitivity could be particularly valuable for people with osteoarthritis, because persistent pain is not always explained by the amount of visible damage within a joint. Changes in how the nervous system processes pain can also contribute to discomfort.
The improved grip strength was another unexpected result, suggesting that the supplement's effects might extend beyond the knee itself.
The researchers also found a substantial difference in how many participants completed their assigned treatments. Only 3.6% of the inulin-only group dropped out, compared with 21% of the physical therapy-only group.
This difference suggests that taking a daily fiber supplement may be easier to incorporate into a regular routine than following a structured exercise program.
A Surprising Connection Between Gut Health, Muscles, and Pain
Dr. Kouraki said: "Our findings suggest that targeting gut health with a prebiotic supplement is a safe, well-tolerated, and effective way to reduce pain in people with knee osteoarthritis. The very low dropout rate compared to the exercise group is also encouraging from a public health perspective -- people were able to fit this supplement easily into their daily lives."
Beyond the reduction in arthritis pain, the researchers are particularly interested in what the findings reveal about interactions between the digestive system, muscles, and nervous system.
The association between GLP-1 and grip strength raises the possibility of a broader biological relationship connecting gut health with physical performance and resilience as people age.
Senior author Professor Ana Valdes from the School of Medicine added: "The link we observed between GLP-1 and grip strength is particularly intriguing and points to a broader gut-muscle-pain axis that warrants further investigation. This could have implications not just for osteoarthritis, but for understanding how gut health influences aging and physical resilience more broadly."
The findings are promising, but the trial was relatively small and lasted only six weeks. Larger studies with longer follow-up periods will be needed to establish whether the benefits persist, identify which patients are most likely to respond, and clarify the biological mechanisms responsible.
The results also do not suggest that fiber supplements should replace exercise or other established arthritis treatments. Instead, they point toward a potentially useful additional approach that could complement existing care.
A New Direction for Arthritis Treatment
The potential importance of this research becomes clearer when considering how many people live with persistent arthritis pain.
Professor Lucy Donaldson, Director of Research at Arthritis UK, said: "The pain of arthritis can severely impact quality of life. Our recent lived experience survey showed that six in ten people are living in pain most or all of the time due to their arthritis.
"Researchers are starting to explore the role of the gut microbiome in our experience of pain. This exciting preliminary research highlights how diet and physiotherapy can act in different ways to have benefits for people with arthritis. We know a variety and balance of healthy foods, including fiber, and regular physical activity matter, and we're glad to be supporting research that explores how they work to help people with arthritis."
For people living with knee osteoarthritis, the findings offer an encouraging possibility: a relatively simple change in daily nutrition may help reduce pain while supporting other aspects of physical health.
Perhaps most intriguingly, the research suggests that treating arthritis may involve looking beyond the joints themselves. By exploring how gut bacteria influence inflammation, pain perception, and muscle function, scientists may uncover new ways to manage a condition that affects millions of people every day.

Effect of Prebiotic Supplementation With and Without Physiotherapy on Pain and Pain Sensitivity in People with Knee Osteoarthritis. Nutrients, 2026; 18 (5): 714 DOI: 10.3390/nu18050714

articles.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
articles.text:
The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- Yale School of Medicine
- Summary:
- A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. The discovery could help explain why some autistic people have difficulty recognizing faces and reading emotions.
- Share:
A major new study has uncovered important differences in how the brains of autistic children respond to human faces. Published in Nature Mental Health, the research is among the most extensive investigations yet into how face perception works in autism.
Some autistic people tend to look at faces less frequently or make less eye contact. They may also find it more difficult to remember faces or interpret facial expressions compared with neurotypical individuals. Scientists have spent decades investigating the brain activity behind these differences. In the early 2000s, for example, researchers at Yale reported that brain regions responsible for processing faces showed lower activity in autistic individuals than in people without autism.
James McPartland, PhD, Harris Professor in the Child Study Center and director of the Center for Brain and Mind Health, studies how autistic people process faces using electroencephalography (EEG), a technique that records the brain's electrical activity. Previous EEG studies, however, have typically examined signals from limited regions rather than analyzing activity across the entire scalp.
To gain a more complete picture, McPartland and his colleagues conducted a study involving approximately 400 autistic children, examining electrical signals recorded across the scalp. They discovered that brain activity associated with face recognition was less clearly distinguishable in autistic participants. They also identified a striking difference in development: In neurotypical children, the brain's response to faces became more specialized with age, while autistic children did not show the same pattern.
"This is the first time we've leveraged the full volume of very rich information provided by an EEG recording to understand face perception and autism," McPartland says.
How Scientists Discovered Differences in Autistic Brain Activity
McPartland compares traditional approaches to studying face recognition with attempting to understand traffic throughout an entire city by monitoring just one downtown street.
"That's the way most research on face processing so far has worked," McPartland says.
The new approach provides a much broader perspective, similar to observing traffic across an entire city using satellite imagery. To investigate these patterns, the researchers analyzed information collected through the Autism Biomarkers Consortium for Clinical Trials (ABC-CT). The dataset included autistic and neurotypical children across different age groups.
During the experiments, participants viewed pictures of faces and everyday objects while EEG equipment recorded their brain activity. Instead of concentrating on a small number of recording locations, the scientists examined electrical signals from all 128 electrodes positioned around each participant's scalp.
They then applied machine learning techniques to determine whether patterns in the recordings could reveal what each child was viewing.
The results showed that brain activity provided a clearer indication of face viewing in neurotypical children than in autistic children. In other words, the electrical signals associated with seeing faces were less distinguishable in the autistic group.
"The neural activity that we measure at the scalp is just not as distinct in autistic children," says first author Jason Griffin, PhD, assistant professor of psychology at University of Houston. Griffin previously worked as a postdoctoral researcher in McPartland's laboratory.
The researchers also found that the ability to identify what a child was viewing from brain activity improved with age among neurotypical participants. This age related improvement was not observed in autistic children, suggesting that their neural responses to faces develop along a different pattern.
"Their face-specific processing is not following the same trajectory," Griffin says.
Face Recognition Differences May Begin Earlier Than Previously Thought
Beyond identifying differences in brain activity, the study offers new insight into how early those differences emerge during face perception.
Recognizing someone involves multiple stages of neural processing. The sequence begins when visual information enters the eyes and continues as the brain interprets that information until a face is recognized.
Much of the earlier research on autism and face perception has concentrated on a brain signal called the N170. This measurable change in electrical activity typically occurs about 170 milliseconds after a person sees a face. Previous studies have shown that the N170 response tends to occur later in autistic individuals.
By analyzing brain activity over a wider period, the researchers found evidence that differences in face processing begin before this familiar signal appears. This suggests that autism related differences may arise at earlier stages of visual processing than researchers had previously established.
"But when you look at face processing through an approach that's more inclusive of the full temporal range of information, we're seeing that differences in autism occur even earlier," McPartland says.
What the Discovery Could Mean for Autism Diagnosis and Early Support
The findings could eventually influence how researchers approach autism diagnosis and the development of supportive interventions.
Historically, some clinicians attempted to address difficulties with face perception by requiring autistic individuals to maintain eye contact. Research has since shown that forcing eye contact is not an effective solution. A better understanding of how face processing develops in the brain could help identify approaches that are more useful and appropriate.
An ongoing challenge in autism research is separating neurological differences associated with autism itself from changes that may develop through the experience of living with the condition. According to the researchers, the patterns identified in this study suggest that differences in face processing are connected to underlying developmental characteristics of autism rather than simply reflecting accumulated life experiences.
"When we're seeing this expected refinement and specialization in non-autistic people, we're seeing a reduced developmental change in autistic people," McPartland explains.
Because the differences appear during development, the findings also raise the possibility that support aimed at helping autistic children interpret facial emotions could be particularly beneficial when introduced earlier in childhood.
However, the researchers emphasize that autism does not necessarily create difficulties that require intervention. Many neurodivergent people experience little or no impairment related to their autism and may neither need nor want additional support. For others, challenges with recognizing faces or understanding facial expressions can complicate everyday social interactions.
"Imagine navigating life when it's hard for you to perceive the information in another person's face, from navigating a playground to navigating a job interview," McPartland says. "This is one of the critical areas that causes difficulty for many autistic people."
New Brain Signals Could Help Improve Autism Diagnosis
Another potential application involves the search for more objective ways to assess autism. Currently, clinicians diagnose autism primarily by evaluating behavior because reliable biological tests are not yet available for routine diagnosis.
Scientists are investigating several possible biomarkers, which are measurable biological characteristics that could improve diagnostic assessments or help distinguish different groups within the autism spectrum.
The newly identified patterns of face related brain activity could contribute to that effort. By examining how these neural signals differ among individuals, researchers may eventually develop additional diagnostic tools or better identify autistic people who are likely to benefit from particular forms of support, including social skills therapy.
Although more research is necessary before these findings can be used in clinical practice, the study provides a new way to investigate how the autistic brain processes faces and how those responses change throughout childhood.
"This is a first step in introducing a new biomarker," McPartland says.

Materials provided by Yale School of Medicine. Original written by Isabella Backman. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:

Levin, Sara Jane Webb, Frederick Shic, Catherine Sugar, James Dziura, James C. McPartland. Decoding the temporal dynamics of face-specific neural representations in autism. Nature Mental Health, 2026; 4 (7): 1109 DOI: 10.1038/s44220-026-00672-y

articles.title: Khỉ bay: Sinh vật bí ẩn trong rừng nhiệt đới, giống khỉ nhưng không phải khỉ, có thể bay mà không có cánh
articles.text:
Trong những khu rừng nhiệt đới, nơi ánh sáng mặt trời khó xuyên qua tán cây rậm rạp và không khí luôn đượm mùi đất ẩm và hương hoa, tồn tại vô số loài sinh vật độc đáo và kỳ diệu. Trong số đó, có một sinh vật đặc biệt mà sự hiện diện của nó luôn gợi lên sự tò mò và ngạc nhiên. Đó là "khỉ bay", một sinh vật không chỉ biết leo trèo mà còn có khả năng lướt qua không trung mà không cần cánh.
Dù mang cái tên "khỉ bay", loài sinh vật này thực tế không phải là khỉ, mà thuộc họ sóc gặm nhấm. Với tên khoa học là Cynocephalus, khỉ bay sở hữu ngoại hình giống một con sóc nhưng có vóc dáng thanh mảnh hơn. Điều đặc biệt khiến chúng trở nên nổi bật chính là màng da mềm mại nối giữa các chi, cho phép chúng lướt bay nhẹ nhàng qua không trung giữa các ngọn cây, giống như những vũ công điêu luyện của rừng già.
Có hàng chục loài khỉ bay sinh sống trong các khu rừng nhiệt đới, đặc biệt là ở Đông Nam Á. Chúng chủ yếu sống trên cây, ăn lá, trái cây, và đôi khi là côn trùng. Khả năng leo trèo của khỉ bay vô cùng xuất sắc. Chúng có thể di chuyển từ cành này sang cành khác một cách nhanh nhẹn, và khi cần di chuyển xa hơn, khỉ bay sẽ bật nhảy từ độ cao, mở màng da và lướt bay trên không trung, bay hàng chục mét mà vẫn hạ cánh chính xác lên mục tiêu.
Khỉ bay không thực sự biết bay như loài chim. Tên gọi này xuất phát từ khả năng di chuyển đặc biệt của chúng giữa các tán cây trong rừng.
Nhờ có màng da rộng nối liền các chi, khỉ bay có thể "lượn, lướt bay" từ cành cây này sang cành cây khác một cách uyển chuyển, tạo cảm giác như đang bay.
Khả năng lướt bay của khỉ bay không chỉ là một kỹ năng ngẫu nhiên, mà là kết quả của hàng triệu năm tiến hóa để thích nghi với môi trường sống phức tạp. Trong các khu rừng nhiệt đới, nơi cây cối mọc dày đặc và mặt đất thường ẩm ướt, khả năng lướt bay giúp khỉ bay dễ dàng di chuyển qua các chướng ngại vật và tránh các mối nguy hiểm khi phải đi trên mặt đất.
Thêm vào đó, khả năng lướt bay trên không cũng giúp chúng tiết kiệm năng lượng khi kiếm ăn, đồng thời nâng cao cơ hội sinh tồn trong môi trường khắc nghiệt này. Chúng không cần phải băng qua các khoảng cách dài bằng cách trèo hoặc đi bộ mà chỉ cần một cú nhảy, giúp tiết kiệm thời gian và giảm thiểu nguy cơ bị kẻ săn mồi phát hiện.
Màng da là đặc điểm phân biệt rõ nhất của khỉ bay. Màng da rộng, mỏng và có nhiều mạch máu, giúp chúng tạo ra lực nâng khi di chuyển giữa các cây.
Không chỉ có khả năng lướt bay độc đáo, khỉ bay còn có nhiều thói quen đặc biệt khác. Chúng thường hoạt động vào ban ngày và nghỉ ngơi trong các hốc cây vào ban đêm. Khỉ bay sống theo nhóm gia đình, nơi các thành viên trưởng thành cùng nhau chăm sóc và bảo vệ con non. Những khỉ con sau khi sinh sẽ nhanh chóng học cách lướt bay bay từ mẹ, và qua thời gian, chúng dần dần phát triển thành những cá thể thành thạo trong việc bay lượn qua rừng.
Điều đáng chú ý là khả năng sinh sản của khỉ bay khá ấn tượng. Mỗi năm, khỉ cái có thể sinh ra một vài con, và ngay từ khi mới sinh, những khỉ con này đã có thể lướt bay qua rừng cùng mẹ, học hỏi và thực hành kỹ năng sinh tồn trong môi trường rừng nhiệt đới đầy thử thách.
Khả năng lướt bay của khỉ bay là kết quả của quá trình tiến hóa thích nghi với môi trường sống trên cây. Nhờ khả năng này, khỉ bay có thể di chuyển nhanh chóng giữa các cây, tránh kẻ thù và tìm kiếm thức ăn hiệu quả hơn.
Trong hệ sinh thái phức tạp của rừng nhiệt đới, khỉ bay đóng vai trò quan trọng, vừa là động vật ăn thịt vừa là con mồi của các loài khác. Chúng tương tác chặt chẽ với nhiều loài thực vật và động vật khác trong khu rừng, góp phần duy trì sự cân bằng sinh thái. Khỉ bay không chỉ giúp duy trì sự đa dạng sinh học mà còn mang lại sự sống động và sức sống cho thế giới tự nhiên.
Hình ảnh khỉ bay lướt bay qua không trung với dáng vẻ duyên dáng, nhẹ nhàng chính là biểu tượng của sự kỳ diệu trong tự nhiên. Sự hiện diện của chúng nhắc nhở chúng ta về vẻ đẹp tuyệt vời và đa dạng của thế giới động vật, khiến ta thêm trân trọng và cảm nhận sâu sắc hơn về sự sống hoang dã.
Khỉ bay là loài động vật có khả năng thích nghi đặc biệt với cuộc sống trên cây. Khả năng lướt bay độc đáo của chúng đã khiến chúng trở thành một trong những loài động vật thú vị nhất trong thế giới tự nhiên.
Câu chuyện về khỉ bay không chỉ là một lời nhắc nhở về sự kỳ diệu của thiên nhiên mà còn là lời kêu gọi chúng ta cùng nhau bảo vệ và gìn giữ những di sản sinh thái quý giá này. Mỗi loài động vật trong tự nhiên đều có một vai trò quan trọng trong hệ sinh thái chung. Việc bảo vệ chúng cũng chính là bảo vệ môi trường sống của chính con người.
Chúng ta cần nhận thức rõ rằng, mỗi hành động nhỏ đều góp phần vào việc duy trì sự đa dạng sinh học trên hành tinh. Hãy chung tay bảo vệ những cánh rừng nhiệt đới – nơi không chỉ là ngôi nhà của loài khỉ bay, mà còn là nơi chứa đựng vô vàn phép màu khác của sự sống.
Khỉ bay, với khả năng lướt bay qua rừng mà không cần cánh, là minh chứng sống động cho sự đa dạng và sức sống mãnh liệt của thiên nhiên. Chúng ta nên trân trọng và bảo vệ những sinh vật kỳ diệu này, để chúng tiếp tục sống và phát triển, góp phần vào bức tranh đa dạng sinh thái của Trái Đất.

articles.title: The asteroid that killed the dinosaurs may have helped ants conquer the world
articles.text:
The asteroid that killed the dinosaurs may have helped ants conquer the world
Scientists discover that mysterious “jumping genes” may have helped ants take over the world after the dinosaurs disappeared.
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- University of Münster
- Summary:
- The asteroid that killed the dinosaurs may have set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with a surprising boost from “jumping genes” hidden in their DNA. Scientists discovered that bursts of activity from these mobile genetic elements coincided with the rise of major ant groups and may have helped sharpen their extraordinary ability to communicate through smell.
- Share:
Around 66 million years ago, an asteroid struck Earth and brought the age of the dinosaurs to an end. The mass extinction that followed created opportunities for countless other animals to evolve and spread. Ants were among the groups that eventually became remarkably successful, and scientists have now identified a surprising genetic factor that may have helped fuel their rise.
Today, ants are the largest family of social insects, with more than 15,000 species found around the world. New research published in Science Advances suggests that their extraordinary evolutionary success was partly driven by mobile segments of DNA known as transposable elements, or "jumping genes."
The international study was led by Dr. Lukas Schrader of the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (IEB) at the University of Münster (Germany).
How "Jumping Genes" Helped Ants Evolve
Jumping genes are pieces of DNA that can move to different locations within a genome and produce additional copies of themselves. Scientists once viewed them primarily as "genomic parasites" because, much like viruses, they can multiply without providing any clear benefit to their host. In some cases, their activity can even contribute to disease.
More recently, however, researchers have begun recognizing that these mobile genetic elements can also create opportunities for evolutionary change. The new findings suggest they played an important role in the remarkable diversification of ants.
When the scientists compared different groups of ants, they discovered that lineages containing the greatest numbers of jumping genes also tended to have the most species today.
Even more revealing was the timing of these genetic changes. The researchers found that several major ant lineages experienced separate surges in jumping gene activity during the early Paleogene (about 66 million years ago). These bursts occurred shortly before the groups began expanding into the thousands of species that exist today.
"The asteroid impact had dramatic consequences for the environment. We have now found the genomic mechanism that connects these ecological upheavals to the subsequent rapid diversification of the ants: transposable elements," explains Lukas Schrader.
Ants are not the only animals showing this evolutionary pattern. Previous studies have also identified periods of increased jumping gene activity associated with the emergence of new species in other groups, including primates and bats.
A Genetic Boost to Ant Communication
The researchers also discovered a connection between jumping genes and the expansion of gene families that allow ants to communicate through chemical signals.
Of particular importance were genes responsible for odorant receptors, which enable ants to detect and respond to smells. These receptors are essential to nearly every aspect of ant social behavior. Ants depend heavily on chemical cues to find their way through the environment, identify members of their own colonies, and coordinate activities with other ants.
The findings suggest that jumping genes may have contributed to the expansion of these sensory systems, potentially improving the ability of ants to detect and interpret the chemical messages that make their complex societies possible.
Tracing 100 Million Years of Ant Evolution
To investigate how jumping genes influenced ant evolution, the international research team examined and compared the genomes of 163 ant species. These represented twelve of the 16 ant subfamilies that survive today, providing a broad picture of the genetic diversity found across modern ants.
Using these genomic comparisons, the scientists reconstructed how transposable elements evolved and changed in activity over the past 100 million years.
Their results reveal a striking connection between ancient bursts of jumping gene activity and the later diversification of ants, suggesting that DNA sequences once dismissed as genetic parasites may have helped one of Earth's most successful insect groups flourish.

articles.title: Scientists discover the immune system’s hidden sense of touch
articles.text:
Scientists discover the immune system’s hidden sense of touch
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- McGill University
- Summary:
- Scientists at McGill University have discovered a surprising new ability of immune cells that could change how we understand long-term immunity. Researchers found that T cells can actually sense how stiff their surrounding tissues are, using these physical signals to help determine whether they develop into long-lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.
- Share:
Scientists at McGill University have discovered a surprising ability in immune cells that could reshape our understanding of how the body develops lasting protection against infections.
For years, researchers believed that tissue-resident memory T cells, specialized immune cells that remain in the body's tissues after an infection and respond quickly if the same threat returns, were guided mainly by chemical signals.
However, a new study published in Nature Immunology challenges that assumption. Researchers found that T cells can detect how stiff their surrounding tissues are and use this physical information to influence whether they develop into long-lasting memory cells. The findings suggest that adjusting to the stronger mechanical forces within tissues may be important for these protective cells to survive over time.
"This is an exciting fundamental finding that challenges the way we think about immune cells," said lead author Judith Mandl, a professor in McGill's Department of Physiology. "It suggests T cells can 'feel' their surroundings and adapt to them, making the physical environment an active force in shaping their behavior."
The research brought together scientists from McGill's Department of Physiology, the Alan Edwards Centre for Research on Pain, the Department of Bioengineering, and the McGill University Health Centre, along with collaborating institutions in the Netherlands and the United States.
How the Discovery Could Influence Cancer and Immune Treatments
Understanding how T cells respond to physical conditions could eventually open new possibilities for treating diseases in which the immune system mistakenly targets healthy tissue. These include autoimmune disorders, allergies, and complications involving transplant rejection.
The discovery could also have important implications for cancer research, particularly efforts to improve treatments that use the immune system to fight tumors.
"Tumors are often dense and physically difficult for immune cells to penetrate. Understanding how T cells adapt to these environments could help researchers design cancer immunotherapies that are better able to reach and attack tumors," said Mandl.
How Scientists Discovered the Immune Cells' Hidden Sense of Touch
To investigate whether physical surroundings influence T cell behavior, the researchers studied immune cells collected from humans and mice. They placed the cells inside specially designed collagen gels that mimicked tissues with different levels of stiffness.
The experiments revealed a clear pattern. As the gels became stiffer, T cells were increasingly likely to acquire characteristics associated with tissue-resident memory cells, which help provide long-term immune protection.
These results indicate that the physical properties of surrounding tissues can help shape how immune cells develop, adding an important new dimension to scientists' understanding of immune memory.
The researchers now hope to identify the specific molecular sensor that enables T cells to detect their physical environment. Determining how this sensor converts mechanical forces into changes in cell behavior could help explain how the immune system establishes lasting protection.
The study received funding from the Human Frontier Science Program, the Canadian Institutes of Health Research, the Canadian Foundation for Innovation, the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada, and the U.S. National Institutes of Health.

articles.title: Lần đầu tiên NASA phải kêu gọi sự giúp đỡ từ công chúng, trong công cuộc khám phá sao Mộc
articles.text:
Tàu thăm dò Juno của NASA là tác giả của một trong số những bức ảnh đẹp nhất về sao Mộc trong những năm trở lại đây. Mới đây. cơ quan vũ trụ đã thành lập một dự án khoa học công dân để công chúng có thể giúp sức trong công việc xác định các đặc điểm khí quyển của hành tinh khí khổng lồ.
Dự án có tên Jovian Vortex Hunter và được dẫn dắt bởi các nhà nghiên cứu tại Đại học Minnesota và NASA, đặt mục tiêu phân loại các loại mây khác nhau trên sao Mộc. Các nhà nghiên cứu quan tâm đến việc xác định động lực học của chất lỏng cơ bản dẫn đến sự hình thành của các xoáy và cấu trúc hỗn loạn trên hành tinh này và kiểm tra các hình ảnh thu được bởi sứ mệnh Juno.
Sao Mộc là hành tinh khí khổng lồ lớn nhất trong Hệ Mặt trời
Sao Mộc chủ yếu chứa vật chất ở trạng thái khí và lỏng. Nó là hành tinh khí khổng lồ lớn nhất trong Hệ Mặt trời với đường kính 142.984 km tại xích đạo. Khối lượng riêng trung bình của hành tinh bằng 1,326 g/cm³, và có khối lượng riêng lớn nhất trong số bốn hành tinh khí khổng lồ.
Nhà nghiên cứu sau tiến sĩ vật lý và thiên văn học Ramanakumar Sankar, người đứng đầu dự án Jovian Vortex Hunter, cho biết: "Có rất nhiều hình ảnh mà nhóm nhỏ của chúng tôi sẽ mất vài năm để kiểm tra tất cả chúng".
"Chúng tôi cần sự giúp đỡ từ công chúng để xác định những hình ảnh nào có xoáy, chúng ở đâu và chúng xuất hiện như thế nào. Với danh mục các đặc điểm (đặc biệt là xoáy), chúng tôi có thể nghiên cứu vật lý đằng sau cách các đặc điểm này hình thành, và chúng liên quan như thế nào đến cấu trúc của khí quyển, đặc biệt là bên dưới các đám mây, nơi chúng tôi không thể quan sát trực tiếp chúng".
NASA cần mọi người giúp đỡ để xác định những hình ảnh nào có xoáy trên sao Mộc.
Vệ tinh Juno của NASA đã có mặt ở bên ngoài khí quyển của sao Mộc từ năm 2016 trong sứ mệnh khám phá hành tinh này. Đó là con tàu vũ trụ có chiều dài bằng 1 sân bóng rổ và quay quanh quỹ đạo của sao Mộc. Hiện vệ tinh này cùng kính viễn vọng James Webb là những công cụ quan trọng giúp NASA cung cấp nhiều cái nhìn chi tiết về sao Mộc, phục vụ việc nghiên cứu.
Các nhà nghiên cứu hy vọng sẽ trả lời được ba câu hỏi chính: Có sự khác biệt về sự đa dạng giữa các đặc điểm xoáy thuận và anticylonic, cấu trúc đám mây khác nhau có thể có là gì, và những khối màu nâu (xoáy thuận dài có màu nâu đậm) khác với các đặc điểm xoáy thuận khác như thế nào?
Trên sao Mộc, hầu hết các đám mây được tạo ra từ các chất hóa học không phải nước.
"Bầu khí quyển của sao Mộc rất giống với bầu khí quyển của chúng ta: có những đám mây có hình dạng và kích thước khác nhau", các nhà nghiên cứu của Jovian Vortex Hunter giải thích: "Trên sao Mộc, hầu hết các đám mây được tạo ra từ các chất hóa học không phải nước, và có thể có kích thước vài nghìn km".
"Một số đám mây cũng được tạo ra từ những cơn bão mạnh có chiều cao hơn 50 km hoặc thậm chí là hàng trăm kilomet. Việc tìm ra cách những đám mây này hình thành là rất quan trọng để hiểu được bầu khí quyển của sao Mộc, và các quá trình tạo ra những đặc điểm tuyệt vời mà chúng ta thấy".
Jovian đề cập đến loại đám mây mà nhóm chủ yếu quan tâm đến việc nghiên cứu.
"Các đám mây khác nhau trên sao Mộc hình thành trong các điều kiện khí quyển khác nhau (ví dụ như bão, lốc xoáy), tương tự như cách chúng ta nhận được các loại mây khác nhau khi bầu khí quyển tĩnh lặng hoặc có bão. Các loại mây trên sao Mộc cũng phụ thuộc nhiều vào hóa chất hình thành chúng. sao Mộc có ba lớp mây chính: những đám mây amoniac chủ yếu là những đám mây mà chúng ta có thể nhìn thấy vì chúng hình thành ở phía trên cùng, tiếp theo là một lớp amoni hydrosunfua và sâu trong bầu khí quyển (khoảng 150 km bên dưới các đám mây amoniac), có thể sẽ là những đám mây nước dày".
"Để hiểu được những đám mây khác nhau này hình thành như thế nào, chúng ta cần xem xét sự đa dạng của các đặc điểm đám mây trong khí quyển. Trong dự án này, chúng tôi sẽ tạo danh mục đó và nhóm các tính năng đám mây khác nhau từ hình ảnh JunoCam lại với nhau".
Jovian Vortex Hunter được phân loại là một dự án khoa học công dân, là sự hợp tác giữa các nhà khoa học và các thành viên quan tâm của công chúng.
| Sao Mộc là hành tinh lớn và nặng nhất trong Hệ Mặt trời. Bán kính trung bình của nó là 69.911± 6 km, lớn gấp 10,97 lần Trái Đất. Khối lượng sao Mộc là 1,8986.1027 kg, tương đương 317,8 lần Trái Đất. Mặc dù vậy, vì là một hành tinh khí, nó có mật độ vật chất nhẹ hơn vào khoảng 1,326 g/cm3. Bên cạnh đó, vì là một khối khí khổng lồ, sao Mộc không có một bề mặt thực sự. Nếu ai đó đứng trên nó, đơn giản là họ sẽ chìm và đi xuyên vào lõi rắn của hành tinh. Kết quả là lực hấp dẫn trên sao Mộc (được định nghĩa trên đỉnh đám mây khí) khoảng 24,79 m/s2, tương đương 2,528 g. |

articles.title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
articles.text:
The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- University of Hawaii at Manoa
- Summary:
- The secret to aging more slowly may be hiding in your gut. Scientists discovered that certain gut bacteria are strongly linked to how quickly the body ages, with microbial differences accounting for about 15% of the variation in biological aging rates. Some bacterial species were associated with slower aging, while others were linked to accelerated aging.
- Share:
Scientists have uncovered a surprising connection between the bacteria living in the human gut and the speed at which the body ages. Researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa found that certain gut microbes are associated with slower biological aging, while others are linked to faster aging.
The study, published in Scientific Reports, found that differences in gut bacterial communities accounted for approximately 15% of the variation in participants' biological aging rates. The results suggest that the gut microbiome, the vast community of microorganisms living in the digestive system, may provide valuable clues about aging at the molecular level.
"This study advances our understanding of the relationship between the gut microbiome and biological aging," said senior author Alika K. Maunakea of the UH Mānoa John A. Burns School of Medicine. "We found that microbial patterns in the gut were significantly associated with molecular measures of aging, even independent of chronological age. These findings open important new directions for understanding how modifiable biological systems influence long-term health trajectories and longevity."
Scientists Identify Gut Bacteria Linked to Faster and Slower Aging
To investigate the relationship between gut bacteria and aging, researchers examined stool and blood samples collected from 123 adults across a wide range of ages. They identified the bacteria present in each participant's gut and compared those findings with blood-based molecular markers used to estimate the body's rate of aging.
These biological measurements differ from chronological age, which simply reflects how many years someone has been alive. Instead, they are designed to assess how quickly aging-related changes are occurring within the body.
The researchers found a notable association between the composition of the gut microbiome and DunedinPACE, an advanced biomarker that measures the pace of biological aging.
Some bacterial species stood out for their particularly strong relationships with aging. Bifidobacterium adolescentis was among the microbes most strongly associated with slower biological aging. In contrast, Succinivibrio dextrinosolvens showed one of the strongest associations with faster aging.
These differences suggest that particular patterns of gut bacteria may offer important information about how rapidly the body is aging.
How Diet, Lifestyle, and Environment May Influence Gut Health
Lead author Braden P. Kunihiro said the discovery adds to growing evidence that the gut microbiome could play an important role in precision health research, which aims to better understand individual differences in health and disease.
Unlike chronological age, the composition of the gut microbiome can change in response to everyday influences, including diet, lifestyle, and environmental conditions. This makes it a particularly interesting area of investigation for scientists studying healthy aging.
"The gut microbiome is highly responsive to lifestyle, diet, environment and other everyday exposures," Kunihiro said. "Our findings suggest that the microbiome may reflect important aspects of biological resilience and aging in ways that could eventually help inform future wellness and healthy aging strategies."
The research also included Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander participants, groups that have historically received limited representation in studies of aging and gut microorganisms.
Co-author Ruben Juarez explained that including these populations could help scientists investigate how social circumstances and environmental conditions leave lasting biological effects over the course of a person's life.
"The microbiome exists at the intersection of behavior, environment and human biology," Juarez said. "Studies like this help illuminate potential pathways through which lived experiences and social factors influence long-term health outcomes."
Could Changing Gut Bacteria Influence How We Age?
Although the findings reveal a meaningful relationship between gut bacteria and biological aging, researchers stress that the study does not establish cause and effect. In other words, finding certain microbes in people who age more slowly does not necessarily mean those bacteria are responsible for slowing the aging process.
Further studies will be needed to determine whether deliberately changing the gut microbiome can influence biological aging or improve long-term health.
Still, the findings offer a promising starting point for exploring how the microorganisms living inside us relate to the aging process and whether they could eventually help guide more personalized approaches to healthy aging.
"This is an important early step toward understanding the gut microbiome's relationship with healthy aging," Maunakea said. "Future research will help clarify the mechanisms involved and whether these microbial signatures may eventually contribute to precision approaches for promoting long-term health and wellness."
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Hawaii at Manoa. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Braden P. Kunihiro, Brennan Y. Yamamoto, Ruben Juarez, Alika K. Maunakea. Gut microbiome signatures associate with DNA methylation-based biological aging. Scientific Reports, 2026; 16 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-52974-x

articles.title: “25 tỉ quả bom nguyên tử” bị khóa kín ở nơi không ngờ trên Trái đất
articles.text:
Nghiên cứu mới chỉ ra chỉ trong vòng nửa thế kỷ - từ năm 1971 đến 2020 - nhân loại đã gây ra một mối đe dọa khủng khiếp bằng cách giữ lại năng lượng gấp 25 tỉ lần quả bom nuyên tử Little Boy gây ám ảnh của Mỹ ngay trên và trong Trái đất.
Nghiên cứu công bố trên Earth Systerm Science Data khẳng định nguồn gốc của "25 tỉ quả bom nguyên tử" - tức nguồn năng lượng mạnh 380 zettajoules - chính là sự nóng lên toàn cầu.
Giải thích trong một bài viết trên chuyên san khoa học The Conversation, các nhà khoa học khí hậu Úc Andrew King từ Đại học Melbourne và Steven Sherwood từ Đại học New South Wales cho biết năng lượng nói trên tương đương 25 tỉ lần "Little Boy", quả bom nguyên tử mà Mỹ thả xuống Hiroshima của Nhật Bản vào năm 1945.
Trái đất đang bị "ép uổng" hấp thụ năng lượng tương đương 25 tỉ quả bom nguyên tử do con người tạo ra - (Ảnh: SHUTTERSTOCK/LIVE SCIENCE).
Chưa kể, năng lượng khổng lồ mà hành tinh của chúng ta bị ép hấp thụ này chỉ tương đương khoảng 60% lượng khí thải nhà kính mà hoạt động của con người gây ra, tức sức phá hoại của nhân loại thậm chí còn cao hơn.
Tuy nhiên, với lượng năng lượng bị giữ lại khủng khiếp này, lẽ ra Trái đất đã phải tăng hàng chục độ so với thời tiền công nghiệp, thay vì mới 1,2 độ C. Vì vậy họ đã đi tìm những thứ đang cố "cứu vớt" địa cầu.
Nghiên cứu chỉ ra 89% số năng lượng này đã được đại dương hấp thụ; trong khi đất hấp thụ 6%. 4% khác đã được sử dụng để làm tan chảy băng ở các tầng lạnh bao gồm tuyết, băng biển, băng nước ngọt, sông băng, thềm băng, băng vĩnh cửu... và chỉ 1% còn lại trong khí quyển.
1% này cũng đủ để Trái đất nóng khủng khiếp như chúng ta thấy.
Phần lớn nhiệt do biển hấp thụ bị giữ lại ở khoảng 1km phía trên đại dương. Nó tạm giải cứu nhân loại, nhưng gây ra sự gia tăng lớn về nhiệt ở bề mặt đại dương, tăng tốc độ băng tan các cực, hủy hoại hệ sinh thái biển và tạo ra những cơn bão nhiệt đới ngày một khốc liệt hơn, chưa kể phá vỡ các dòng hải lưu.
Các tác giả nhấn mạnh các đại dương sẽ không thể bảo vệ hành tinh mãi mãi vì sẽ đến ngày nó "bội thực". Khó định lượng được sự tàn khốc của những thảm họa mà nhân loại sẽ hứng chịu khi đẩy Trái đất đến điểm tới hạn đó.
Những con số rùng mình một lần nữa nhấn mạnh tính cấp thiết của việc hạn chế phát thải khí nhà kính, ngăn sự nóng lên toàn cầu - vốn đang khiến khí hậu trở nên ngày một khắc nghiệt và hỗn loạn.

articles.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
articles.text:
Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- Osaka Metropolitan University
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.
- Share:
Low testosterone can contribute to several health problems, and an unhealthy diet may make some of those risks even worse. One major concern is metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), a condition that affects approximately 40% of adult men worldwide and has become a significant global health issue.
Fatty liver, the earliest stage of MASLD, occurs when excess fat builds up in the liver. Several factors are associated with the condition, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, low testosterone levels, and excessive fructose consumption from sugary drinks and processed foods. However, scientists have not fully understood how these factors interact or whether their combined effects are more harmful than each one individually.
How Low Testosterone and Fructose Affect the Liver
To investigate this connection, a research team from the Graduate School of Agriculture, led by graduate student Hiroki Takahashi and Associate Professor Naoki Harada, examined how reduced testosterone and high fructose intake influence liver health.
The researchers used eight-week-old male mice and divided them into six experimental groups. Some underwent castration to lower testosterone levels, while others received a sham operation. The groups included Sham/Control, Sham/Fructose, Sham/Fructose + Antibiotics, Castration/Control, Castration/Fructose, and Castration/Fructose + Antibiotics.
To determine how these conditions affected the animals, the team analyzed liver cells and tissues, blood plasma, organic acids from the cecum, and samples of gut bacteria.
A Dangerous Combination for Fatty Liver
The results revealed that mice with reduced testosterone levels developed heavier livers when they consumed fructose. However, this increase in liver weight was smaller in mice that also received antibiotics.
When examined separately, low testosterone and fructose intake produced only modest changes in liver triglyceride levels. When combined, however, the two factors had a much stronger effect, significantly increasing fat accumulation and worsening fatty liver.
The researchers also identified changes in the composition of gut bacteria, altered liver gene activity, and elevated levels of pyruvate in the cecum among mice exposed to both reduced testosterone and fructose.
These findings suggested that the gut microbiome could play an important role in explaining why the combination was particularly harmful.
Gut Bacteria Reveal a Hidden Mechanism
Further experiments helped the researchers identify a possible biological explanation for the increased liver fat.
"Upon examining this mechanism, we found that changes in the gut microbiota led to increased levels of pyruvate within the intestine. Furthermore, experiments using mouse-derived primary hepatocytes revealed that pyruvate acts synergistically with fructose to promote neutral lipid accumulation in hepatocytes," explained Takahashi.
In other words, changes in gut bacteria appeared to increase intestinal pyruvate, a compound involved in energy metabolism. Laboratory experiments with liver cells isolated from mice showed that pyruvate and fructose worked together to increase fat storage in those cells.
The discovery suggests that interactions among testosterone levels, dietary fructose, and gut bacteria may help explain how fatty liver develops and worsens.
Potential New Ways to Prevent Fatty Liver Disease
Understanding this relationship could eventually help researchers identify new approaches to preventing or treating fatty liver disease. In particular, targeting the processes through which pyruvate contributes to fat accumulation may offer promising possibilities.
"Going forward, we hope to clarify the mechanism by which pyruvate promotes triglyceride accumulation to pioneer the development of therapeutic drugs and establishment of preventive methods through dietary interventions," added Professor Harada.
Although the findings come from experiments in mice and isolated mouse liver cells, they provide new insight into how hormonal changes and diet may interact to influence liver health.
The study was published in American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Osaka Metropolitan University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Hiroki Takahashi, Naoki Harada, Yohei Hayamizu, Erdenetsogt Dungubat, Masami Nakazawa, Tomoya Kitakaze, Keiichiro Sugimoto, Hiroshi Inui, Eiji Yoshihara, Yoshihisa Takahashi, Ryoichi Yamaji. Testosterone deficiency synergistically exacerbates fructose-induced hepatic steatosis through gut microbiota and pyruvate in mice. American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism, 2026; 330 (2): E233 DOI: 10.1152/ajpendo.00518.2025

articles.title: Chùm ảnh AI mô phỏng cuộc sống con người năm 2100
articles.text:
Trình tạo hình ảnh bằng trí tuệ nhân tạo Midjourney đã tạo ra những mô phỏng về cuộc sống của chúng ta vào năm 2100.
Midjourney cho thấy thế giới vào năm 2100.
AI giúp công việc của con người trở nên dễ dàng hơn nhiều trong việc viết nhạc, tạo văn bản có ý nghĩa và thậm chí chẩn đoán bệnh.
Midjourney có thể tạo ra những bức tranh, cách điệu theo tinh thần của những bộ phim nổi tiếng và tạo nên hình ảnh của những sinh vật trong truyện cổ tích.
Mạng thần kinh là một chương trình được thiết kế dựa trên nguyên tắc kết nối nơ ron trong não người.
Thuật ngữ mạng thần kinh xuất hiện lần đầu tiên vào giữa thế kỷ 20, khi các nhà khoa học quyết định cố gắng tạo ra một công nghệ có thể tái tạo bộ não con người.
Trong tương lai, rất có thể đây sẽ là một phần trong cuộc sống của con người.
Mạng thần kinh hiện đại có thể tự học, tìm lỗi trong công việc và áp dụng kinh nghiệm trước đó.
Ngày nay, mạng lưới thần kinh được sử dụng để giải quyết các vấn đề phức tạp đòi hỏi tính toán phân tích, giống như những vấn đề được thực hiện bởi bộ não con người.
Mạng thần kinh có thể phân phối dữ liệu theo các tham số, đưa ra dự đoán về tình hình hiện tại, chẳng hạn như kinh tế.
Theo Diễn đàn Kinh tế Thế giới, đến năm 2025, trí tuệ nhân tạo sẽ có thể thay thế các chuyên gia trong lĩnh vực nghệ thuật thị giác, điện ảnh, báo chí, lập trình và các lĩnh vực khác.
Midjourney có các thuật toán nâng cao có thể phân tích và bắt chước các phong cách và mẫu khác nhau, cho phép nó tạo ra nhiều loại nội dung trực quan độc đáo và được cá nhân hóa.
Midjourney là một công cụ mang tính cách mạng sử dụng công nghệ trí tuệ nhân tạo để tạo ra những hình ảnh tuyệt đẹp và có độ chân thực cao.
Khả năng của trí tuệ nhân tạo rất lớn.
Midjourney là một trong những mạng thần kinh chính để vẽ.
Midjourney có khả năng tạo ra những hình ảnh vô cùng sặc sỡ theo nhiều kiểu khác nhau từ các mô tả bằng văn bản.

articles.title: Common drugs may help dangerous viruses spread through the body
articles.text:
Common drugs may help dangerous viruses spread through the body
- Date:
- October 27, 2026
- Source:
- Norwegian University of Science and Technology
- Summary:
- A surprising discovery reveals that widely used anti-inflammatory drugs may unintentionally help dangerous viruses spread through the body. Scientists found that JAK inhibitors, prescribed for rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory diseases, can weaken a crucial immune defense against influenza, COVID-19, and other infections. By suppressing genes that normally fight viruses, these medications may leave patients more vulnerable to infection.
- Share:
Medications are designed to treat diseases and relieve symptoms, but some can also produce unintended effects that put patients at risk. While side effects are common with many treatments, researchers have identified a particularly concerning possibility involving drugs used to control inflammation.
Scientists at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) have discovered that a widely used class of anti-inflammatory medications may make it easier for certain viruses to infect cells and spread throughout the body.
"We have found a surprising and potentially serious side effect of a class of anti-inflammatory drugs. They can help viruses spread more easily in the body," says Denis Kainov, a professor at the Department of Clinical and Molecular Medicine at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
Common Anti-Inflammatory Drugs May Help Viruses Spread
The medications at the center of the findings belong to a class called Janus kinase inhibitors, or JAKs. These drugs are widely prescribed to control inflammation, but their effects on the immune system may also leave the body more vulnerable to viral infections.
"Among the viruses that more easily affect the body with the help of these drugs are Rift Valley fever virus, influenza A, adenovirus and SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19," Kainov says.
These viruses can cause significant illness, making any treatment that potentially increases their ability to spread a serious concern.
Why Arthritis Drugs Can Weaken Antiviral Defenses
In a new study published in NAR Molecular Medicine, Kainov and his colleagues investigated how JAK inhibitors influence the body's ability to defend itself against viruses.
"JAK inhibitors are often prescribed for autoimmune diseases and inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis," says Erlend Ravlo, a PhD research fellow at NTNU and first author of the article.
Although these medications can be highly effective at reducing inflammation, their benefits come with an important trade-off. By suppressing certain immune responses, they can also interfere with the mechanisms that normally protect the body from viral infections.
"In particular, the drugs suppress an important immune signalling pathway that helps protect healthy cells from viral attacks," Ravlo said.
This pathway plays a central role in coordinating the body's response when viruses attempt to infect healthy tissue.
Scientists Discover How JAK Inhibitors Disrupt Immune Protection
The research team found that JAK inhibitors, including the medication baricitinib, can reduce the activity of genes involved in fighting viral infections.
"These genes play a crucial role in the body's response to viral infections," said Aleksandr Ianevski, an NTNU researcher and coauthor of the new paper.
When JAK inhibitors interfere with this immune signaling system, they weaken an important layer of antiviral protection. Without the usual defensive response, viruses may find it easier to establish an infection and spread between cells.
To investigate these effects, the scientists combined advanced virology methods with gene expression analysis and organoid technology. Their experiments included cells from the lungs, eyes and brain, along with miniature organ models grown in the laboratory.
These approaches allowed the team to examine how the drugs affect antiviral defenses across different types of human tissue.
"Although JAK inhibitors are effective in the treatment of inflammation, this shows that they can pose a hidden risk for patients who have latent or active viral infections," says Ravlo.
What the Findings Mean for Patients and Future Treatments
The results highlight the importance of carefully considering the risks associated with JAK inhibitors, particularly when patients may already have a viral infection or when outbreaks are occurring.
Researchers suggest that healthcare professionals should exercise caution when prescribing these medications during periods of increased viral transmission.
However, the same immune-suppressing properties that create potential risks for patients could also offer advantages in certain research settings. Under controlled laboratory conditions, these effects may help scientists develop vaccines or evaluate potential antiviral medications.
The researchers hope their findings will encourage greater awareness of how JAK inhibitors influence the immune system and support further investigations into their safest and most effective uses.
"We recommend further studies to better understand how the drugs can be used optimally, especially during virus outbreaks or pandemics," says Ianevski.
Professor Magnar Bjørås of the Department of Clinical and Molecular Medicine provided significant scientific expertise and secured most of the funding for the research. Additional financial support came from the Central Norway Regional Health Authority, the South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority, the Research Council of Norway and the Swedish Research Council.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Norwegian University of Science and Technology. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Erlend Ravlo, Aleksandr Ianevski, Marius Nårstad Skipperstøen, Hilde Lysvand, Jørn-Ove Schjølberg, Ole Solheim, Wei Wang, Miroslava Kissova, Marthe Vestvik, Olli Vapalahti, Teemu Smura, Hanna Vauhkonen, Valentyn Oksenych, Friedemann Weber, Mårten Strand, Magnus Evander, Janne Fossum Malmring, Jan Egil Afset, Magnar Bjørås, Denis E Kainov. JAK inhibitors remove innate immune barriers facilitating viral propagation. NAR Molecular Medicine, 2025; 2 (2) DOI: 10.1093/narmme/ugaf017
