articles.title: Tankers defy sharp escalation of Iranian attacks to keep crude oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz
articles.text:
Within 24 hours of the U.S. and Israel going to war with Iran, Tehran responded with a wave of attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz to cut off one of the world's main sources of crude oil.
Iran's campaign was initially successful, with crude exports plunging nearly 90% to 1.8 million barrels a day in March compared with 16 million bpd in February, according to data provided by Kpler.
But crude flows have rebounded over the past eight months as the U.S. military provides protection to tankers transiting Hormuz. Tehran has responded by escalating its attacks in recent weeks.
More commercial ships have come under attack in October than at any other point in the war. Yet in contrast to March when exports cratered, tankers have continued to ferry substantial volumes of crude oil through Hormuz in a sign that the shipping industry has adapted to wartime in the Persian Gulf.
As of Oct. 27, at least 30 vessels, mostly oil tankers, were hit this month leaving at minimum 16 seafarers injured, according to data from the International Maritime Organization, a United Nations agency. Ship attacks doubled in October compared with 15 confirmed incidents in September.
"It's a difficult situation. Ships are attacked really on a daily basis," said Jakob Larsen, chief safety and security officer at Denmark-headquartered BIMCO, one of the big international shipping trade associations.
Oil prices rise, but flows are resilient
Crude prices have surged more than 13% this month as security conditions have deteriorated in the Persian Gulf. The international Brent contract traded above $117 a barrel on Friday. That's just shy of its wartime closing high of $118.35 during Iran's big wave of ship attacks in March.
Yet actual crude exports through Hormuz stood at nearly 11.1 million bpd on average in October, only about 2% lower from September despite the sharp escalation of violence, Kpler's data shows.
"On balance in terms of oil coming out, there hasn't been a massive impact," said Mary Melton, senior tanker analyst at Braemar, a ship broker headquartered in London.
Crude flows through Hormuz are highly volatile on a daily basis with exports near prewar levels one day while falling well below such levels another day. The final leg of October has seen flows decline to 7.3 million bpd for the week ended Wednesday, more than 40% below the prewar baseline, according to Kpler.
Oil flows are more resilient now because the shipping industry has adjusted its operations to the threats, Larsen said. Freight rates have soared, making it "more attractive for the risk takers in the industry to actually carry out these voyages," he said.
"And when the cost of oil goes up that also means that there's more commercial incentives to get the oil out and sell it in the global market," Larsen said.
Adapting to more perilous times
Shippers have adapted by setting up a shuttle system to reduce the risk of attack. Tankers load crude at Persian Gulf ports, sail through Hormuz with their transponders turned off and transfer the cargo to tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman that then deliver it to refiners in Asia. This reduces insurance costs for the ships waiting outside the strait, Melton said.
The shuttle system has been effective at getting oil out with flows through Hormuz surging more than 70% since July, according to Kpler. But this system is also inefficient, logistically complicated and expensive, Melton said.
It requires more equipment, ships and experienced crews, the analyst said. About 20% of the world's supertanker fleet is tied up helping to shuttle oil out of the Gulf, she said.
Tanker rates have exploded as a consequence. It cost $249,000 per day to hire a supertanker to make the journey from the Gulf of Oman to Asia in early September, Melton said. By the first week of October, the price had surged to more than $900,000 per day. This translates to about $21 in transportation costs per barrel of crude oil compared with $6.50 a barrel in September, the analyst said.
"If you're an importer in Asia, you're used to paying almost nothing for freight," Melton said. "Then you're facing 20% to 30% of the actual delivered cost of crude is going to freight.
"That really starts impacting your margins as a refiner," the analyst said.
More Gulf oil producers are now covering the cost and risk of shipping through Hormuz in a bid to claw back market share in Asia from the U.S. and other Atlantic producers, she said. And they are increasingly using their own tankers to run the gauntlet through the strait, she said.
Uncertainty as midterms approach
It is unclear how long the complex and expensive shuttle system can sustain current export levels. The tankers transiting Hormuz are totally dependent on air support from the U.S. military for their security, Larsen said.
"I don't think there would be many shipowners willing to take the risk if they didn't have that air cover from U.S. fighter jets and helicopters and drones," he said.
It is also uncertain how long the U.S. military will remain engaged, particularly if Democrats regain control of Congress after Tuesday's elections and demand that the president end the war.
The U.S. has told several Gulf Arab nations to be ready for a short but intense military campaign following the Nov. 3 midterm elections, people briefed on the conversations told The Wall Street Journal. The U.S. Navy, which is enforcing a blockade against Iran, has warned ships that don't need to transit the Persian Gulf, Hormuz and Gulf of Oman to steer clear of the region.
"Due to the current geopolitical situation, vessels which do not need to transit the area are advised to remain well clear to avoid unnecessary delays to their voyage," the U.S. military told vessels Wednesday through a notice issued by the Joint Maritime Information Center.

articles.title: The AI investing story had a rough week. It may be time to take profits while you still can
articles.text:
Market professionals are sounding worried about the artificial intelligence trade after a big week of data points in the technology sector.
Investors are focused on the scale of the AI build-out and whether returns are materializing fast enough to justify it.
The overall stock bull market driven originally by the AI boom remains intact, with the S&P 500 just a few percent off a record. A rotation into non-AI stocks like Procter & Gamble and Berkshire Hathaway have stepped in to support the market. But AI-related shares are already in a bear market or teetering on one.
It may be time to take some profits or hedge your risk.
This week, frontier algorithm maker Anthropic's public filing document didn't contain much information on forthcoming revenues after the company reported a deceleration in sales from the second to the third quarter. At the same time, we learned from the Big Tech earnings reports that hyperscalers are pulling back on their capital expenditures, suggesting they see a terminal level of required computing power at some point in the future.
We've reached the point where profits need to be showing up in force from AI to justify the buildout that's happened so far and is still to come, investors and traders say.
The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF was off 4% this week, bringing its losses for October to 8%.The ETF is now off 15% from its record over the summer, a stone's throw from a bear market. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell deeper into a bear market this week, off 29% from its recent high.
Doubts creeping in
"You want to make sure that the reward is worth the risk," JJ Kinahan, SVP at Cboe Global Markets, told CNBC on Friday. "I think the reward will be [there], but it continues to be a lot of money up front."
Kinahan said he thought the recent AI boom over the past few years was "in question."
AI-linked Technology stocks were getting housed on Friday in a variety of sectors. Intel was down 25% on lackluster revenue guidance, Micron was down 5.5%, and Nvidia was down 4%.
Hyperscalers were also getting clobbered, with Amazon down 2% and Google down another 1%. Google had its worst trading day ever on Thursday after reporting a drop in its core advertising sales revenues.
Like traders, technology investors were also sounding down about the AI trade on Friday.
"I'm a little worried about the trade," Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist, said. "I think we're probably going to get a little bit more chopping here."
Accordingly, options specialists say they're seeing more people pursuing downside insurance.
"Historically, tech stocks have call skews. So people are more willing to buy greed [with] upside calls than they are to buy insurance downside puts. I've seen that reverse in the last three days," Dennis Davitt, CIO and co-founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth, said.
There's another interesting signal coming from options, Davitt noted: While investors may be getting cold feet about the big tech companies associated with the AI trade writ large, they may also be gaining confidence about the commercial prospects of AI technology itself, specifically with new successful consumer agents, such as Meta's Muse.
"I think the ChatGPTs and the [other AI algorithms] of the world are actually taking over from the Amazons of the world as well as the Googles of the world," he said. "You see Muse of Facebook – If you look at options pricing in Muse, there's less fear priced in Meta than there is in Amazon."
Longer-term confidence in AI could be a silver lining for the slip in bread-and-butter ad sales reported by Alphabet this week. The stock fell by more than 10% after reporting earnings on Wednesday.
Google executive Philipp Schindler called attention to the growth of AI mode use at the company even as it still has lower monetization at this point.
"It's worth noting the strong growth in AI mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI mode," he said Wednesday.
Still, the shifts in usage and monetization matter less to the fate of the AI trade than overall productivity and profit. All that capex needs to produce a profit, propelled by boosted productivity from businesses using AI.
Macroeconomic reflections about this from top investors over the past few weeks are sounding rather gloomy, though nobody is super about the specific timing.
"Maybe the markets will continue to kick the can down the road," Paul Tudor Jones, Tudor Investment Corporation founder, said earlier this month, contemplating the possibility of a "tipping point" and saying that the odds were 60-40 that "we're down that path."
"[AI-related issuance as a share of GDP] is 50% more than railroads, triple that of highways, telecoms, the other big infrastructure buildouts in history. So that competition between AI buildout and sovereigns may take us to the tipping point," he added.
Technical analyst Jonathan Krinsky at BTIG recommended fading the chip bounce earlier this month, making comparisons in the SOX semiconductor index to some major down-legs in its history.
Investors were rotating away from the tech sector on Friday, with names like Coca-Cola, Walmart and Eli Lilly all up over 1%.

articles.title: AI-driven layoffs are creating a new class of boomerang employees—companies are realizing they 'pulled the plug too quickly'
articles.text:
AI-driven layoffs dominated the headlines this year.
Employers cited AI as the primary reason for almost 40% of the job cuts announced in May 2026, according to a report from outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
But new research shows that some employers may be rethinking those job cuts and reversing course in a trend experts call "AI rebounding."
In a survey of more than 1,000 U.S. workers, nearly 1 in 5 respondents say that they have been laid off or replaced by AI and then asked to return, according to a recent report from SHL, a talent acquisition and talent management company. The survey, which SHL commissioned from market research firm Propeller Insights, also polled over 1,000 U.K. workers. It was conducted between June and July 2026 and had a margin of error of 5%.
These findings indicate that companies are realizing they "pulled the plug too quickly" on their human employees, according to Lucy Beaumont, global senior vice president of product and design at SHL.
Several large employers like Ford and Amazon have reversed course after enacting AI-related layoffs in the past year. A March report by Orgvue found that 32% of organizations that let workers go due to AI have had to rehire staff.
It's a mistake for companies to approach AI implementation as if it were any other software rollout, says Joseph Fuller, professor of management practice at Harvard Business School.
From a company's perspective, "in order to spend money on a new technology, we have to find some savings in the budget, and the way we've done that with previous technology deployments is by laying people off."
But AI is most useful when it's linked with a human worker's "contextual intelligence," i.e. their background knowledge and understanding of an issue, he says: "The more you know about important processes, the more value you can extract from the AI."
AI can't fully replace "people that know the business, that know their customers, that have judgment, that can bring empathy, that have that human connection," Beaumont says.
Returning workers have new demands
Most workers are open to returning after a layoff: only 6.6% of U.S. workers say they would refuse to come back under any circumstances, according to the SHL study.
But those who do return are "going to be a lot more demanding of what they expect from an employer," Beaumont says.
According to SHL's research, almost half of surveyed U.S. workers would require a significant pay increase to return to their roles, and 43% would want "written guarantees" of job security. A similar number, 40%, would require "full transparency" regarding how AI would be used in their role before they'd rejoin the company. And 30% of workers say that an apology or acknowledgment from leadership is a key condition of their return.
Above all, employees are looking for reassurance, Beaumont says: "How do I know that this isn't going to happen again?"
Even when workers do return, employers need to understand that company morale is going to take a hit, according to Beaumont. Being laid off "fundamentally changes" the psychological contract between employer and employee, she says, and being rehired isn't enough to repair that relationship.
"You've really broken the trust with those people," Beaumont says.
As a result, returning workers are unlikely to have the same levels of "productivity and engagement" as they did before a layoff, she says. "Culture is so difficult to change, and once you've impacted it negatively, it's so difficult to recover from."
What skills workers should practice
To stay relevant in the job market, employees are prioritizing skill development, Beaumont says: U.S. survey respondents say that they're teaching themselves how to use AI tools (44%), developing industry-specific skills that can't be easily replicated by AI (42.6%), working on interpersonal and leadership skills (40%) and honing creative and strategic thinking (38%).
Given how quickly AI's capabilities will grow, the most important skill for employees to hone is adaptability, Fuller says. He urges workers to practice working with AI regularly and "seek out opportunities" to upskill with the technology.
Workers will also need to get comfortable with change, he says. In the near future, Fuller predicts that AI will create "permanent tumult" within many organizations as they continue to recalibrate their staffing needs around AI advancements.
Beaumont recommends that workers identify the areas where their unique skills can have the most impact: "If AI is going to take away some of those easily automated tasks, what's left for me to do, and how can I optimize the human side that I can bring?"
Leaders should focus on questions like, "What kind of upskilling do people need? What new opportunities are there for people? What kind of internal mobility am I opening up as a result of AI?" she says.
The organizations that will be successful are the ones who "are using AI to optimize what they do," Beaumont says — not just to cut costs.

articles.title: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Intel, Lumentum, Sandisk, Twilio, Coinbase & more
articles.text:
Market Insider
Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Intel, Lumentum, Sandisk, Twilio, Coinbase & more
Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Semiconductor stocks — Chipmakers suffered Friday as technology stocks sold off and concern reemerged about the strength of the artificial intelligence trade. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) slumped 7%, Astera Labs ' stock tumbled 12%, shares of Qualcomm dropped 11% and Nvidia 's stock lost 4%. AI infrastructure plays — The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) slumped more than 7%, and shares of Micron Technology slid more than 5%, Lumentum Holding s by more than 10% and Arista Networks by almost 8%, as stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout continued to lose air. CNBC's David Faber also said Friday that the proposed deal for Lumentum by Marvell Technology won't come at a big premium. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals — The biotech company's stock jumped 11%. Third-quarter results beat estimates, with Regeneron earning $20.07, excluding items, on revenue of $5.12 billion. The FactSet consensus sought $16.42 per share and $4.56 billion. For the full-year period, Regeneron is calling for non-GAAP gross margin on net product sales of about 86%, up from its earlier guidance of 84% to 85%. Sandisk — Shares fell 12% even after the data storage device manufacturer reported an earnings and revenue beat in its fiscal first-quarter financial report. It delivered adjusted earnings of $49.51 per share compared with analysts' estimates for $46.22, per LSEG. Sandisk also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split. Twilio — Shares dropped about 17% after the consumer engagement platform's current-quarter guidance reflected slowing organic revenue growth. Twilio sees fourth-quarter revenue in a range of $1.595 billion to $1.605 billion and year-over-year organic revenue growth in a range of 11% to 12%. In the third quarter, however, organic revenue grew 16% year over year. Roblox — Shares of the gaming platform shed 20% after the company gave disappointing guidance for the fourth quarter. Projected bookings for the period range from $1.89 billion to $2 billion, while analysts anticipated $2 billion. Mondelez International — The company behind Sour Patch Kids and Oreo cookies saw its stock add more than 3%. Mondelez reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 78 cents a share, topping the FactSet consensus estimate of 71 cents per share. FedEx Freight — Shares jumped 15% after the freight transportation services business gave strong guidance for the fourth quarter. FedEx Freight expects quarterly revenue between $2.3 billion and $2.37 billion, compared to $2.07 billion a year ago. It anticipates adjusted operating income between $185 million and $205 million, up from $162 million a year prior. Intel — Shares tumbled 29% after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter . The company sees adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue ranging between $15 billion and $16 billion. That's below LSEG estimates of 43 cents in earnings per share and revenue of $17.1 billion. Rivian Automotive — Shares jumped over 8% after the electric vehicle maker reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Rivian lost an adjusted 48 cents per share on revenue of $2.16 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a loss of 62 cents per share on revenue of $1.99 billion. The company also increased its guidance on deliveries . Amazon — Shares slipped 1% after the e-commerce giant reported third-quarter results that missed analyst expectations. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12-month period. Reddit — The company announced it will require users to log in to access its social media platform and issued weaker-than-expected revenue guidance for the fourth quarter. Shares tumbled 29%. Crypto-related stocks — Shares of Coinbase and Robinhood shed 12% and 8%, respectively, following one of the largest crypto hacks ever on Thursday when Binance reported an estimated $6.3 billion was affected. The company also estimates roughly $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets were frozen. Chevron — Shares added 1% after Chevron reported its net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion in the third quarter. The company also posted better-than-expected revenue for the period. Exxon Mobil — Shares gained more than 1% after the oil giant's profits doubled to $15.4 billion from $7.5 billion in the year-earlier period. AstraZeneca — Shares of the biopharmaceutical company jumped over 7% following better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The company reported core earnings of $2.79 per share on revenue of $16.21 billion. Analysts expected a profit of $2.60 per share on revenue of $16.05 billion. — CNBC's Michelle Fox, Scott Schnipper, Nick Wells and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.

articles.title: Google lost nearly half a trillion this week. Here's how Mike Khouw is trading it
articles.text:
"Be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful," said the great Warren Buffett is his classic Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter in 1986.
This week's tech sell-off might provide an opportunity to put that adage to work, particularly if you're inclined to use options.
Alphabet's (GOOGL) Q3 2026 earnings report triggered a historic gap down; the stock fell over 12% to $285, shaving nearly $500 billion in market cap. Despite a 103% surge in Cloud revenue that points to underlying fundamental strength, the market focused on the EPS miss ($2.12 vs. $3.02 estimate) and negative free cash flow (AI capital expenditures are relentless!). For options traders, this environment sets up a compelling range-bound play via a short strangle, capitalizing on inflated implied volatility and a deadlocked near-term outlook.
While the core business remains fundamentally intact, two near-term anchors are likely to suppress any rapid recovery. First, the sell-side reaction was swift: several firms either downgraded the stock, cut price targets, or lowered forward estimates. Historically, stocks that absorb a wave of downgrades underperform or trade sideways over the next 30 days as institutional repositioning caps upside momentum. (Fodder for another article, but this is one of the most predictive "factors to watch")
Second, the technical posture is severely damaged. Alphabet was already weak before the print, and this earnings gap only confirmed the breakdown. With the RSI plunging into the low 20s and the MACD accelerating its sell signal, the technical overhead is heavy. However, extreme oversold conditions at the bottom of the 52-week range ($270.70) should stem a total freefall.
Strategy Setup: To exploit this anticipated 30-day chop, a short strangle lets traders collect premium while leaving room for consolidation.
Target Expiration: Standard December 18, 2026 (capturing the 30- to 45-day window for post-downgrade underperformance).
Trade Dynamics & Risks This position profits if GOOGL trades strictly between $250 and $325 through expiration, allowing time decay (theta) and the post-event volatility crush (vega) to erode the options' value. Given the stock's current trajectory, the main risk is a broader market sell-off dragging GOOGL below the $250 short strike, but that would be a reasonably attractive entry price. Conversely, an unexpected catalyst would need to drive shares past $310 to threaten the upside, which remains improbable given the technical damage and Wall Street's renewed skepticism over Alphabet's AI spending bill.
By the way, you'll notice that the probability of profit on this trade is quite high; both the short call and short put each have a probability of profit close to 90%. articles.title: Alaska Senate election: DOJ wants to 'segregate' all ballots for 2nd Sullivan candidate
articles.text:
The Department of Justice wants "to preserve and segregate all ballots ranking" a candidate named Dan Sullivan for a potential investigation of whether voters in Alaska's U.S. Senate election mistakenly ranked him in the belief he was incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, a federal prosecutor told a judge in a court filing late Friday.
The filing came in a lawsuit by the DOJ, which asks District Court Judge Sharon Gleason to block state election officials from immediately certifying the Senate election if Sen. Sullivan loses by a margin that might be attributable to voter confusion from the presence of the other Sullivan on the ballot. The DOJ wants to conduct an investigation to determine voter intent if the incumbent loses.
"Election Day is on November 3, 2026, which poses a substantial risk that the candidacy before us will mislead voters and ultimately result in an electoral process that lacks integrity," U.S. Attorney for Alaska Michael Heyman said in the filing, signed by one of his assistant prosecutors.
"The United States of America contends that the proposed precautionary measures will be impossible after Election Day, showing good cause for expedited consideration," the filing said.
Heyman earlier Friday told reporters at a press conference that there is an "ongoing" criminal investigation into how and why retired school teacher Dan Sullivan decided to run for the Senate for the first time this year.
The DOJ's suit, which President Donald Trump said he had requested, claims the "sole purpose" of the non-incumbent Sullivan running was to benefit the campaign of Democratic nominee Mary Peltola by reducing the number of votes for Sen. Sullivan.
"We will not let anyone or any group undermine this election," said Heyman at a press conference in Anchorage, which was held just four days before Election Day.
"There is both a civil investigation and a criminal investigation that is ongoing," Heyman said. "There is a surge of FBI resources and resources in this office."
"Every Alaskan deserves a fair election, and they're going to get one," the prosecutor said.
He said that the criminal probe has been underway for months. Heyman had previously recused himself from the probe because he was being considered for a judicial nomination, but that recusal was rescinded Thursday because he was no longer under consideration.
Heyman said the criminal investigation has been accelerated because of a New York Times report on Wednesday that said aides Peltola's campaign and senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee helped recruit the retired teacher to enter the Senate race with the hope of drawing votes from the incumbent Sullivan.
"When credible information comes out, we are committed to pursuing that information … and we will act on it," Heyman said.
Peltola's campaign and the DSCC deny being involved in the retiree's Senate campaign.
Heyman, when questioned by reporters, would not say what criminal statute might have been violated
Earlier Friday, a federal judge kept on a fast track efforts to dismiss the DOJ's suit.
Judge Sharon Gleason ordered the DOJ to respond by 1 p.m. Alaska Time to the new dismissal motions, which were filed hours after the department amended its suit in U.S. District Court in Anchorage on Thursday to add a new legal claim.
The DOJ's updating of the civil complaint forced Gleason to rule the prior dismissal motions were moot.
Gleason gave state election officials, the campaign of Democratic nominee and other groups until noon Saturday to reply to the DOJ's response.
The judge's order leaves open the possibility that she will rule on the dismissal motions before Tuesday, which is Election Day, as both the state and Peltola's campaign have requested.
The state, the campaign, and other intervenors in the suit argue the DOJ has no legal authority to block certification of an election because two candidates on a four-candidate ballot happen to share the same name.
The winner of Alaska's race could determine which party holds a majority in the Senate starting in January. Republicans currently have 53 seats in the 100-member chamber.
Alaska's election uses ranked-choice voting. If no candidate obtains more than 50% of the vote in the first count, then the fourth-place finisher will be eliminated, and the second choice on that candidate's ballots will be allocated to the remaining candidates.
Only Peltola and Sen. Sullivan are considered likely to draw large shares of the votes.
The DOJ's suit seeks to delay certification of the Senate election if Sen. Sullivan loses by a margin that could be attributable to voter confusion over the presence of the other candidate, who is listed as Daniel J. Sullivan, on the ballot.
The amended complaint, which updates the suit filed Oct. 23, added a claim under the Supremacy Clause of the U.S. Constitution to the first claim, under the National Voter Registration Act.
It also contained added details from the Times article.
Peltola's campaign, in its dismissal motion filed Thursday, said, "Rather than defend its indefensible legal claims as it was ordered to do, the Department of Justice ... has filed an Amended Complaint that does nothing to address the fatal problems that preclude it from bringing this case or obtaining the relief that it seeks."
"The U.S. Constitution leaves the regulation of federal elections exclusively to the States and to Congress, and DOJ has no statutory authority to bring this case," the motion said.
In their own dismissal motion, state election officials said the amended lawsuit "rests on the same meritless theory that the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) — a voter registration law — governs this case, which has nothing to do with voter registration."
"Because this reading of the NVRA fails, the amended complaint fails," the motion said.

articles.title: Xe mới đổ bộ dồn dập: Cơ hội nào cho xe Trung Quốc tại Việt Nam?
articles.text:
Xe mới đổ bộ dồn dập: Cơ hội nào cho xe Trung Quốc tại Việt Nam?
Thị trường ô tô Việt Nam ngày càng có thêm nhiều thương hiệu mới, từ iCAUR tới Li Auto. Tuy nhiên, tìm được chỗ đứng giữa những đối thủ đã hiện diện không phải bài toán dễ dàng.
Thêm thương hiệu mới, cạnh tranh ngày càng lớn
Vài năm trở lại đây, thị trường ô tô Việt Nam có thêm nhiều cái tên mới như MG, BYD, Geely, Lynk & Co, Omoda & Jaecoo, GAC hay Wuling. Phần lớn tập trung vào SUV, xe điện và hybrid, mang đến thêm lựa chọn về thiết kế, công nghệ và giá bán.
Sự xuất hiện của các hãng xe mới khiến cuộc cạnh tranh ngày càng đa dạng. Tuy nhiên, có sản phẩm khác biệt chưa đồng nghĩa với việc dễ dàng chiếm được thị phần.
Bên cạnh giá bán và trang bị, các thương hiệu mới còn phải giải quyết bài toán nhận diện, niềm tin khách hàng, mạng lưới đại lý, phụ tùng và dịch vụ hậu mãi. Đây đều là những yếu tố mà các hãng xe lâu năm có lợi thế nhất định.
iCAUR chuẩn bị tiếp cận thị trường Việt Nam
iCAUR là một trong những thương hiệu ô tô mới đang hướng tới thị trường Việt Nam. Hãng tập trung vào dòng SUV năng lượng mới, với hình ảnh sản phẩm mang phong cách thiết kế vuông vức, gợi liên tưởng đến những mẫu xe địa hình.
Trong một sự kiện dành cho người dùng tổ chức tại Vũ Hồ (Trung Quốc) mang tên iCAUR International User Summit 2026 từ ngày 19-23/10 vừa qua, iCAUR giới thiệu 20 mẫu V25 được cá nhân hóa. Đây là hoạt động bên lề, không có nhiều liên hệ trực tiếp với kế hoạch kinh doanh của hãng tại Việt Nam.
Đối với thị trường trong nước, vấn đề đáng quan tâm hơn là iCAUR sẽ đưa những sản phẩm nào về phân phối, định giá ra sao và xây dựng hệ thống bán hàng, hậu mãi như thế nào.
Trong bối cảnh người mua đã có nhiều lựa chọn từ các thương hiệu như BYD, MG, Geely hay Omoda & Jaecoo, iCAUR sẽ phải cạnh tranh với những cái tên đã có thời gian hiện diện nhất định. Thiết kế khác biệt có thể tạo sự chú ý ban đầu, nhưng khả năng cạnh tranh vẫn cần được đánh giá qua sản phẩm và chính sách kinh doanh thực tế.
Khác biệt chưa đủ để bảo đảm thành công
Thực tế cho thấy thị trường ô tô Việt Nam vẫn có dư địa cho những thương hiệu mới, đặc biệt khi nhu cầu của người tiêu dùng ngày càng đa dạng. Tuy nhiên, cạnh tranh không chỉ dừng lại ở việc đưa ra một sản phẩm có thiết kế khác biệt hay nhiều công nghệ.
Các thương hiệu như BYD, MG, Geely hay Omoda & Jaecoo đều phải đầu tư vào hệ thống phân phối, dịch vụ và hoạt động tiếp cận khách hàng. Mỗi hãng có cách triển khai khác nhau, nhưng đều phải đối mặt với bài toán tạo dựng niềm tin và duy trì hoạt động lâu dài.
Với iCAUR, khả năng cạnh tranh tại Việt Nam vẫn phụ thuộc vào danh mục sản phẩm, giá bán và chất lượng dịch vụ khi chính thức hoạt động. Đây cũng là những yếu tố quyết định thương hiệu có thể duy trì sức hút sau giai đoạn đầu gia nhập thị trường hay không.
Trong bối cảnh người tiêu dùng có ngày càng nhiều lựa chọn, khác biệt có thể giúp một thương hiệu được chú ý, nhưng giá trị sử dụng và khả năng đáp ứng nhu cầu thực tế mới là những yếu tố quyết định vị thế lâu dài.

articles.title: Halloween gets pricier as chocolate costs climb — Hershey may feel the pinch
articles.text:
Halloween shopping got costlier this year as higher prices hit everything from the candy bowl to the pumpkin on your front porch.
It's not only rough on consumers, but may also hit companies like Hershey.
Americans are expected to spend $13.5 billion on Halloween, up from last year's record $13.1 billion, according to the National Retail Federation.
"Consumers continue to make Halloween a spending priority, but they are also approaching the season with affordability in mind," said Allison Zeller, NRF vice president of industry and consumer insights.
Inflation is rippling through everything from candy to costumes. Pumpkins are costlier too. The average retail price reached $5.36 this year, up 11% from September 2020, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Drought reduced yields by roughly 30% to 40% in parts of Texas, a major pumpkin-growing state.
Candy and chocolate
Candy remains one of the biggest expenses this Halloween and prices increases are running ahead of broader food inflation, though the rate of increase has slowed.
Candy and chewing gum prices were up 7.7% in September from a year earlier, according to the latest Consumer Price Index data. The sugar-and-sweets category increased 5.5% over the same period. Adverse weather, including the impact of El Niño, tightened the outlook for sugar supply. Unusually wet conditions disrupted Brazil's sugarcane harvest, while drought and other weather extremes affected production in other major growing regions.
"As Halloween swiftly approaches, candy stands out in the grocery store as one of the more expensive categories, relative to prices last year," food economist Richard Volpe wrote on LinkedIn. "In past years, this has left me swimming with candy," he added. "As I write this, Halloween is days away and I have a paltry three bags of candy sitting on my desk."
Nielsen IQ Early Market data showed Halloween candy sales down 11.7% through September 19. Four weeks later, the decline narrowed to 6.7%, with chocolate at -7.2% and confection at -5.3%, according to the report.
Chocolate so far has been the most vulnerable, especially after a disruption in cocoa supply in West Africa, which was hit by poor growing conditions in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana. A potential El Niño and dry Harmattan trade winds could put pressure on the 2026-27 West African cocoa crop.
There was some relief in commodity markets after cocoa prices fell sharply from its historic highs, according to David Branch, sector manager at the Wells Fargo Agri-Food Institute.
But that drop has yet to translate into cheaper chocolates.
Wells Fargo Agri-Food estimates chocolate prices will be about 8% higher than last Halloween, with effective transaction prices rising roughly 5% to 8% after promotions. Much of the chocolate on shelves this Halloween was produced using cocoa bought six to 12 months earlier.
"The worst of the cocoa crisis has passed, but price relief hasn't reached store shelves yet," Branch told CNBC. "For chocolate manufacturers, the principal 2026 issue is no longer simply cocoa availability. It is the timing mismatch between falling futures, high-cost inventories, retailer negotiations, and consumer elasticity."
Halloween chocolate dollar sales were down 7.2% from a year earlier through the nine weeks ended Oct. 17, according to NIQ, with weakness in milk chocolate leading the decline.
NIQ estimates Halloween chocolate sales to be down $33.1 million from last year, with milk chocolate accounting for a $34.4 million decline. Dark chocolate, meanwhile, gained $2.3 million. Overall Halloween candy, gum and mint sales were down 6.7%.
To help juice sales, retailers are offering discounts — Walmart and Target have flash deals and heavy discounts on items from candy to Halloween costumes.
Candy shoppers, meanwhile, appear to be moving toward smaller packages. Small candy packs of nine ounces or less are up 24% in dollar terms and 14% in units, while every larger package size is declining, according to NIQ.
Wells Fargo expects shoppers to increasingly favor value packs and alternatives that use less cocoa, including gummies, sour candy, wafers and caramel.
"Consumers will continue buying candy, but shopping baskets are likely to contain fewer chocolate pieces, more value packs, and a greater share of gummies, sour products, wafers, caramel, and other lower-cocoa alternatives," Branch said.
Hershey stock was rising on Friday as consumers ditched AI stocks for safer consumer staples. But analysts see trouble brewing for the candy maker.
The company, which reported third quarter results on Thursday, lowered its 2026 organic sales growth forecast to 3% (from 3%-3.5%). That implies "flattish" organic growth in the fourth quarter, according to Jefferies analyst Scott Marks
Hershey's commentary was "incrementally cautious," he added in a note, saying "consumer and cost pressures" are weighing on the near-term outlook.
"We're looking at areas like in convenience as you see a consumer that's under pressure to give more value and drive pricing through bespoke promotions versus overall price decreases," Hershey CEO Kirk Tanner told analysts on an earnings call.
Marks cut his price target on the stock to $170, joining cuts at brokerages such as DA Davidson, BNP Paribas, Bernstein and Deutsche Bank. Consensus estimates for 2027 earnings fell 3.7% to $9.49 a share, according to FactSet.
CNBC's Alex Harring contributed to the reporting.

articles.title: Bắt Phan Văn Triệu SN 2001 và Nguyễn Thanh Tuấn Duy SN 1992 tại khách sạn
articles.text:
Bắt Phan Văn Triệu SN 2001 và Nguyễn Thanh Tuấn Duy SN 1992 tại khách sạn
Tổ công tác đã bắt giữ Phan Văn Triệu và Nguyễn Thanh Tuấn Duy cùng quê tỉnh Vĩnh Long, tại khách sạn Saysombom.
Công an Hà Nội tối 30/10/2026 cho biết, Phòng Cảnh sát điều tra tội phạm về ma túy Công an thành phố vừa phối hợp với các đơn vị nghiệp vụ triệt phá thành công đường dây mua bán, vận chuyển trái phép chất ma túy xuyên quốc gia từ Lào về Việt Nam, thu giữ hơn 55 kg ma túy tổng hợp, bắt giữ các đối tượng liên quan.
Trước đó, ngày 17/9/2026, từ nguồn tin về một nhóm đối tượng nghi vấn vận chuyển lượng lớn ma túy từ Lào về Việt Nam qua đường chuyển phát nhanh, Phòng Cảnh sát điều tra tội phạm về ma túy Công an thành phố Hà Nội khẩn trương xác minh, xác định địa điểm giao nhận ma túy tại phường Xuân Phương, thành phố Hà Nội.
Theo công an thành phố, tình hình tội phạm ma túy trên các tuyến biên giới diễn biến phức tạp, các đối tượng liên tục thay đổi phương thức hoạt động, lợi dụng dịch vụ bưu chính, chuyển phát nhanh để vận chuyển ma túy, Công an thành phố Hà Nội đã chủ động triển khai các biện pháp công tác, quyết tâm ngăn chặn ma túy thẩm lậu vào địa bàn Thủ đô.
Đến ngày 19/9/2026, Phòng Cảnh sát điều tra tội phạm về ma túy CATP Hà Nội đã phối hợp của Cục Cảnh sát điều tra tội phạm về ma túy (Bộ Công an), Công an tỉnh Quảng Trị, lực lượng Hải quan, Đồn Biên phòng Cửa khẩu quốc tế La Lay và Công an phường Xuân Phương nhanh chóng điều tra, xử lý các đối tượng vi phạm.
Tại địa bàn phường Xuân Phương, lực lượng chức năng bắt quả tang Phạm Tuấn Cường (sinh năm 1993, trú tại tỉnh Vĩnh Long) khi đang nhận kiện hàng chứa khoảng 25 kg ma túy tổng hợp dạng Methamphetamine.
Tiếp tục đấu tranh, mở rộng điều tra, truy xét các đối tượng cầm đầu, trong ngày 19/9/2026, tổ công tác tại Lào đã bắt giữ Phan Văn Triệu (sinh năm 2001) và Nguyễn Thanh Tuấn Duy (sinh năm 1992), cùng quê tỉnh Vĩnh Long, tại khách sạn Saysombom. Khám xét nơi ở của các đối tượng, lực lượng chức năng thu giữ thêm khoảng 30 kg ma túy dạng đá.
Việc triệt phá đường dây, thu giữ tổng cộng hơn 55 kg ma túy là kết quả nổi bật trong công tác phối hợp đấu tranh với tội phạm ma túy xuyên quốc gia. Chiến công thể hiện tinh thần chủ động, mưu trí, kiên quyết của lực lượng Công an, góp phần ngăn chặn nguồn ma túy lớn xâm nhập nội địa, bảo vệ an ninh, trật tự và cuộc sống bình yên của Nhân dân.
Hiện vụ án đang được tiếp tục củng cố hồ sơ, mở rộng điều tra, xử lý nghiêm các đối tượng theo quy định của pháp luật.

articles.title: Cập nhật lợi nhuận quý 3/2026 các ngân hàng sáng 31/10: Kết quả bất ngờ của Vietcombank, VietinBank
articles.text:
Cập nhật lợi nhuận quý 3/2026 các ngân hàng sáng 31/10: Kết quả bất ngờ của Vietcombank, VietinBank
Có 6 ngân hàng lãi trước thuế hơn 10.000 tỷ trong quý 3/2026.
Vietcombank tiếp tục đứng đầu về lợi nhuận trước thuế 9 tháng (LNTT) với 40.440 tỷ đồng, tăng 22,1% so với cùng kỳ. Tuy vậy, LNTT riêng quý 3 của ngân hàng đạt 11.218 tỷ đồng, gần như không đổi so với quý 3/2025. Phần tăng trưởng 9 tháng của Vietcombank chủ yếu đến từ nửa đầu năm.
VietinBank bám sát ở vị trí thứ hai với 39.557 tỷ đồng LNTT 9 tháng, tăng 33,9%, chỉ thấp hơn Vietcombank chưa đến 900 tỷ đồng. Riêng quý 3, VietinBank lãi trước thuế 13.689 tỷ đồng, tăng 29%, cao nhất trong các ngân hàng đã công bố. Thu nhập lãi thuần 9 tháng của VietinBank đạt 61.931 tỷ đồng, tăng 27,7%, lãi thuần từ dịch vụ tăng 42,5% lên 6.602 tỷ đồng, trong khi chi phí dự phòng rủi ro tín dụng tăng 22,6% lên 20.781 tỷ đồng.
BIDV lãi trước thuế 29.483 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, tăng 24,8%, đứng thứ năm. Quý 3, LNTT của BIDV đạt 10.579 tỷ đồng, tăng 39,3%. Thu nhập lãi thuần quý 3 tăng 12,4% lên 17.056 tỷ đồng, còn chi phí dự phòng rủi ro tín dụng giảm 25% xuống 4.640 tỷ đồng.
Xếp sau VietinBank là MB với 30.518 tỷ đồng LNTT 9 tháng, tăng 31,9%, VPBank với 29.911 tỷ đồng, tăng 46,7%, và Techcombank với 28.915 tỷ đồng, tăng 23,7%. Riêng quý 3, cả ba ngân hàng này đều lãi trước thuế trên 10.000 tỷ đồng. VPBank đạt 11.031 tỷ đồng, tăng 20,3% và xấp xỉ Vietcombank, trong khi MB tăng 42,5% và Techcombank tăng 25,8%.
SHB lãi trước thuế 14.309 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, tăng 17%, trong đó riêng quý 3 tăng tới 57,1% lên 5.166 tỷ đồng.
LPBank vượt mốc 10.000 tỷ đồng với 10.421 tỷ đồng LNTT 9 tháng, quý 3 tăng 29%. TPBank đạt 7.464 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, tăng 23,4%, và cũng có quý 3 tăng mạnh với 2.981 tỷ đồng, cao hơn 56,7% so với cùng kỳ. VIB lãi trước thuế 7.592 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, tăng 7,7%.
Ở nhóm ngân hàng quy mô nhỏ hơn, NCB có mức tăng nổi bật khi LNTT 9 tháng đạt 1.574 tỷ đồng, gấp 2,4 lần cùng kỳ. Riêng quý 3, ngân hàng lãi trước thuế 847 tỷ đồng, gấp 4,4 lần quý 3/2025.
ABBank đạt 4.301 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, tăng 85,5%, lợi nhuận quý 3 gần gấp đôi cùng kỳ.
BVBank tăng 88,9% sau 9 tháng, song lợi nhuận quý 3 lại giảm 19,1%.
Nhiều ngân hàng tăng trưởng âm sau 9 tháng
Ở chiều ngược lại, Sacombank có LNTT 9 tháng đạt 5.893 tỷ đồng, giảm 46,4% so với cùng kỳ, riêng quý 3 giảm 51,9% xuống 1.757 tỷ đồng. Eximbank lãi trước thuế 864 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, giảm 57,8%, trong đó quý 3 giảm 66,8%. Saigonbank chỉ đạt 65,9 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng, giảm 74,5%.

articles.title: Fed officials are already saying they’ll need to get back to hiking rates
articles.text:
Two Federal Reserve presidents on Friday said interest rates will need to move higher to rein in inflation.
The St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem said another rate hike will need to happen soon. And Lorie Logan of the Dallas Fed predicted that the central bank will need to raise rates by quarter-point increments at least two more times.
The comments from the two officials offer the first morsels of insight into what leaders at the Fed see next after the central bank on Wednesday elected to leave rates unchanged for now. The remarks are likely to bolster the view among investors that the Federal Open Market Committee will return to hiking rates at its next meeting in December.
Fed funds futures traders are pricing in a roughly 76% likelihood of the Fed lifting rates by a quarter percentage point at that gathering, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
"I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said in prepared remarks for the Shadow Open Market Committee, a gathering of economists in New York focused on the central bank.
"Incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later," Musalem said. "Moving sooner in smaller steps while inflation expectations are anchored has a better chance of succeeding without adverse impact on the labor market or economic growth."
In remarks roughly an hour later, Logan said: "It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the FOMC needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases."
Still, she said, that doesn't mean the Fed has to raise rates at every meeting.
"Skipping a meeting does not change the monetary policy destination," Logan told students at Davidson College in North Carolina, according to her prepared remarks. "Indeed, by making the destination clear, the FOMC can better help the economy adapt and obtain the promised benefits of a skip."
After the predicted two rate hikes, Logan said, "it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate."
Logan will be among the Fed officials voting on the rate decision in December; Musalem is slated to be a non-voting member of the committee until 2028.
Inflation is 'too high'
In his remarks, Musalem broadly spoke positively about the state of the U.S. economy, which he described as "resilient." He pointed to Thursday's data on U.S. GDP, which showed a stronger-than-expected growth rate of 3.4%.
He said there are several factors boosting the economy, including the artificial-intelligence buildout and financial conditions that "remain accommodative."
Musalem said the labor market has been "remarkably stable and balanced." The unemployment rate of 4.2% sits at the median of long-run projections by participants in the FOMC, he noted.
But Musalem warned that inflation is "too high," citing the personal consumption expenditures price index released Thursday that showed annual inflation above 3%. In the question-and-answer portion of the event, Musalem said he's watching core inflation closely, and is on alert for any indications that current inflationary pressures are broadening out.
Fed officials have been closely monitoring inflation expectations among consumers and investors to ensure they don't get too far above the central bank's long-term target of 2%.
Musalem said there's a likely scenario where inflation remains above 2% into the future unless the Fed adjusts monetary policy.
"The best that monetary policy can do now for employment and economic growth is to restore price stability in a timely manner," Musalem said. "The short-run economic costs of reducing inflation are less when the central bank acts before inflation has become entrenched and is expected to persist."
Two of the 12 FOMC voters dissented from Wednesday's decision to keep rates unchanged — Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack — both of whom wanted the committee to raise rates by a quarter percentage point.
Former Fed officials weigh in
Speaking on CNBC Friday, former Richmond Fed President Jeffrey Lacker said he too would have been in favor of a rate hike this week.
"I've been surprised by the lack of urgency. Inflation's been high around three, three-and-a-half percent for so long," Lacker told Kelly Evans on CNBC's "The Exchange." "Maybe they'll come around in the next couple of meetings, but I've been surprised at the lack of urgency."
A December increase would be the second of 2026, after the FOMC elected for a quarter-point hike in September. That marked the central bank's first increase to borrowing costs since 2023.
James Bullard, a former St. Louis Fed president, told CNBC that he was not in favor of Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's plan to make certain Fed meetings focused on broader strategy rather than on live interest rate decisions.
Warsh on Wednesday announced a plan for one Fed meeting in 2027 and two meetings in 2028 to center on bigger policy discussions. Warsh said he did not expect to announce rate decisions or make Fed statements at these adjusted meetings.
"I don't think skipping a meeting is a good idea," Bullard said. "If you don't have a meeting, and then it's a pretty volatile world and you have to act, you're going to have to call a special meeting in that circumstance."
Lacker recommended Warsh take the opposite approach.
"If you want to take the pressure off individual meetings, have more of them," he said.

articles.text:
Điều kiện để người nộp thuế được hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh là gì?
Các trường hợp cơ quan thuế ban hành Thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh với người nộp thuế.
- 30-10-2026Đề xuất xóa tiền chậm thuế cho doanh nghiệp chờ giải thể: Người dân cần làm gì?
- 29-10-2026Đề xuất giảm tiền phạt doanh nghiệp 'bỏ không' nhiều năm
Theo Cục Thuế, căn cứ quy định tại Điều 28 Nghị định số 252/2026/NĐ-CP, cơ quan thuế ban hành Thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh khi người nộp thuế thuộc một trong các trường hợp sau:
(1) Đối với cá nhân kinh doanh, chủ hộ kinh doanh: Nộp thuế để hạ số thuế nợ xuống dưới ngưỡng 50 triệu đồng hoặc được xóa tiền thuế nợ theo quy định.
(2) Đối với chủ sở hữu hưởng lợi/người đại diện theo pháp luật của doanh nghiệp, hợp tác xã, liên hiệp hợp tác xã: Nộp thuế để hạ số thuế nợ xuống dưới ngưỡng 500 triệu đồng hoặc được xóa tiền thuế nợ theo quy định.
(3) Đối với cá nhân kinh doanh, chủ hộ kinh doanh, chủ sở hữu hưởng lợi/người đại diện theo pháp luật của doanh nghiệp, hợp tác xã, liên hiệp hợp tác xã sau 120 ngày kể từ ngày cơ quan thuế ban hành thông báo không hoạt động tại địa chỉ đã đăng ký: Có hồ sơ đề nghị khôi phục mã số thuế, nộp hồ sơ khai thuế, nộp thuế để số tiền thuế nợ dưới ngưỡng quy định (50 triệu đồng đối với cá nhân kinh doanh, chủ hộ kinh doanh; 500 triệu đồng đối với doanh nghiệp, hợp tác xã, liên hiệp hợp tác xã) hoặc được chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế theo quy định.
(4) Đối với người nước ngoài, người Việt Nam xuất cảnh để định cư ở nước ngoài, người Việt Nam định cư ở nước ngoài trước khi xuất cảnh từ Việt Nam: Hoàn thành 100% nghĩa vụ nộp thuế hoặc được xóa tiền thuế nợ theo quy định.
Trong thời hạn bao lâu kể từ khi người nộp thuế hoàn thành nghĩa vụ thuế thì Cơ quan thuế phải ban hành Thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh?
Theo quy định tại Điều 28, Nghị định số 252/2026/NĐ-CP cơ quan quản lý thuế thông qua Hệ thống thông tin quản lý thuế ban hành thông báo hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh ngay sau khi xác định NNT đủ điều kiện hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh.
Cơ quan quản lý xuất nhập cảnh thực hiện hủy bỏ tạm hoãn xuất cảnh ngay sau khi nhận được thông báo từ hệ thống của cơ quan quản lý thuế.

articles.title: Đọc nhãn chăn ga cuối năm: tránh trả tiền cho chữ "lụa"
articles.text:
Đọc nhãn chăn ga cuối năm: tránh trả tiền cho chữ "lụa"
Mùa mua sắm cuối năm, chữ "lụa" xuất hiện dày đặc trên nhãn chăn ga, trong khi không ít bộ thực chất là polyester bóng. Bài viết chỉ cách đọc thành phần sợi, chi số và mật độ dệt, kèm vài phép thử nhanh tại nhà, để tiền bỏ ra đúng với thứ vải mang về.
Giữa tháng 11, các gian hàng chăn ga ở trung tâm thương mại bắt đầu treo biển giảm giá đón mùa cưới và Tết dương lịch. Trên mặt túi nilon của nhiều bộ chăn ga, chữ to nhất thường là "lụa" hoặc "silk", in kèm hình bông hoa. Dòng chữ nhỏ ghi thành phần sợi lại nằm ở mặt sau, cỡ chữ bằng nửa, và hầu như không ai lật lên đọc.
Khoảng chênh giữa hai dòng chữ ấy chính là chỗ người mua hay mất tiền oan.
"Lụa" trên nhãn thường là cách gọi, không phải sợi tơ
Trong ngành vải, satin là một kiểu dệt cho bề mặt trơn và hơi ánh, chứ không chỉ định sợi làm ra nó. Người ta có thể dệt satin từ tơ tằm, từ cotton, hoặc từ polyester. Giá ba loại chênh nhau nhiều lần dù nhìn ảnh trên sàn thì khá giống nhau.
Vì vậy, cụm "lụa gấm", "lụa cao cấp", "silk touch" trên bao bì gần như luôn là tên thương mại do người bán tự đặt. Thứ duy nhất đáng tin là dòng thành phần: 100% cotton, 100% Lyocell, hay 100% polyester. Nếu nhãn chỉ ghi "lụa" mà không có dòng thành phần nào, mặc định nên hiểu đó là sợi tổng hợp.
Ba nhóm vải thường gặp và điểm yếu của từng nhóm
Cotton satin là cotton dệt satin. Mặt vải có ánh nhẹ, đứng dáng, trải giường lên nhìn phẳng và gọn, chịu được giặt máy nhiều lần. Nhược điểm là sau giặt vẫn cần là nếu muốn phẳng hoàn toàn, và vào ngày nóng ẩm thì không mát bằng nhóm sợi gốc gỗ.
TENCEL™ Lyocell là sợi kéo từ bột gỗ bạch đàn. Sợi này hút hơi ẩm vào lõi rồi nhả dần ra ngoài, nên mặt vải giữ được cảm giác mát và khô, hợp với những đêm còn oi ở miền Nam. Đổi lại, vải rủ xuống theo trọng lực, không đứng dáng như cotton satin, ai thích giường căng phẳng kiểu khách sạn sẽ thấy hơi mềm quá.
Washed cotton là cotton đã qua công đoạn giặt xử lý ngay tại xưởng. Mua về là mềm sẵn, mặt vải nhăn tự nhiên nên gần như không phải là.
Polyester in chữ "lụa" thì bóng hơn cả ba loại trên, giá rẻ nhất, nhưng không hút ẩm. Mồ hôi đọng lại giữa da và vải, nằm lâu thấy bí. Mùa hanh lại dễ tích điện.
Chi số và mật độ sợi: hai con số nên nhìn
Chi số sợi, ký hiệu kiểu 40s hay 60s, cho biết sợi mảnh tới đâu. Số càng lớn, sợi càng mảnh, vải càng mịn tay và nhẹ. Mật độ sợi tính bằng số sợi trên mỗi inch vuông, viết tắt TC, cho biết vải dệt dày hay thưa.
Hai con số này nên đi cùng nhau. Mật độ cao mà sợi thô thì vải nặng và cứng. Sợi mảnh nhưng dệt thưa lại dễ xô và nhanh xuống mặt.
Ở nhóm hàng trong nước, các dòng ga giường cotton satin Melinen ghi rõ 60s và 310TC trên mô tả sản phẩm, tương tự dòng TENCEL™ Lyocell 60s mật độ 310 sợi/inch, nên người mua có cơ sở để đối chiếu thay vì đoán theo ảnh.
Mặt vải cotton satin 60s, ánh nhẹ đặc trưng của kiểu dệt satin.
Ba phép thử nhanh trước khi quyết định
Nếu đang đứng trước tấm vải thật, có vài cách kiểm tra chỉ mất một phút.
1.Vò một góc vải trong lòng bàn tay chừng mười giây rồi thả ra. Cotton để lại nếp nhăn khá rõ. Polyester gần như bật lại nguyên trạng vì sợi nhựa có tính đàn hồi.
2.Nhỏ vài giọt nước lên mặt vải. Sợi tự nhiên và Lyocell thấm xuống, vệt nước loang và sẫm màu. Polyester để giọt nước đọng tròn trên bề mặt một lúc rồi mới ngấm.
3.Đốt một đoạn chỉ thừa ở đường may trong. Sợi gốc cellulose cháy thành tro xốp, bóp là tan. Polyester co lại, vón thành hạt cứng và có mùi khét kiểu nhựa.
Phép đốt nên làm ở nhà với mẩu chỉ thừa sau khi đã mua, hoặc xin người bán một mảnh vải mẫu. Không ai cho đốt hàng đang bày.
Vì sao vẫn nên sờ vải thật trước khi chốt
Ảnh chụp sản phẩm đã qua chỉnh sáng khiến polyester bóng và cotton satin trông na ná nhau trên màn hình. Độ nặng tay, độ rủ, cảm giác mát khi áp lòng bàn tay xuống thì ảnh không truyền được. Với một món dùng hằng đêm suốt vài năm, bỏ nửa buổi đi sờ thử là hợp lý.
Cửa hàng của Melinen ở 33 Thảo Điền, phường An Khánh, TP.HCM là một trong những nơi khách có thể trực tiếp so ba loại vải cạnh nhau. Nếu không tiện đi, ít nhất nên yêu cầu người bán chụp ảnh nhãn thành phần.
Bộ TENCEL 60s hoạ tiết Lupins.
Đối chiếu giá: mua lẻ hay mua bộ
Biết mình mua loại sợi nào rồi thì giá mới so được với nhau. Trên website Melinen, một chiếc ga cotton satin màu trơn có giá 900.000 đến 1.350.000 đồng tuỳ kích thước, ga TENCEL 60s 1.050.000 đến 1.500.000 đồng, ga washed cotton 1.250.000 đến 1.500.000 đồng.
Bộ năm món có thêm vỏ chăn thì lên 2.550.000 đến 3.150.000 đồng tuỳ chất liệu và cỡ giường. Ga lại chia theo chiều rộng giường từ 1m2 đến 2m và theo độ dày nệm, nên đo nệm trước rồi hãy mở bảng giá.

articles.title: Class action lawsuit blames Trump officials for student loan forgiveness delays
articles.text:
The American Federation of Teachers sued the Trump administration Friday, alleging it unlawfully blocked student loan forgiveness for tens of thousands of borrowers who qualify.
The plaintiffs argue in their lawsuit, Weingarten v. McMahon, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, that U.S. Department of Education Secretary Linda McMahon has mismanaged the popular Public Service Loan Forgiveness program by incorrectly counting borrowers' payment timelines and not awarding people credit for time served.
PSLF, which President George W. Bush signed into law in 2007, allows certain not-for-profit and government employees to have their federal student loans canceled after 120 payments, generally paid over 10 years. The Biden administration later adapted the program, making it easier to qualify for it and clearing the way for more than 1 million borrowers to have their loans forgiven under the program.
"Secretary McMahon has flagrantly ignored her responsibility to help teachers, nurses and first responders," said AFT President Randi Weingarten, the lead plaintiff, in a statement. The other plaintiffs include AFT members and public service workers. The AFT is a teacher's union representing some 1.8 million members. 
"This lawsuit demands that McMahon stop stalling and do her job," Weingarten said. 
The lawsuit accuses Trump officials of denying borrowers relief under the Biden administration-era PSLF Buyback program. That opportunity allows borrowers who've hit 120 months of qualifying employment to submit a request to the Education Department to retroactively pay for any months they missed because of a forbearance or deferment.
Buyback applications have piled up under the Trump administration, with 88,000 borrowers still waiting for a decision as of the spring, according to a court filing.
The borrowers bringing the lawsuit also say the U.S. Department of Education unfairly lowered their qualifying payment counts out of the blue earlier this year, prolonging borrowers' student loan forgiveness timeline.
"The Department of Education has ripped away the loan forgiveness credit I earned without any explanation," said Elizabeth Schoepflin, a speech-language pathologist and co-plaintiff from New York, in a statement. "Every month this drags on is another payment I shouldn't have to make."
An Education Department spokesperson defended the PSLF program changes, saying the agency is correcting "coding errors" made by the Biden administration.
"These errors resulted in inaccurate payment counts for some borrowers," the spokesperson wrote to CNBC in an email. "The Department remains committed to ensuring that every qualifying payment is properly credited to a borrower's account."

articles.title: “Thành phố cuối tuần” Qtopia: Đủ gần để đi mỗi tuần, đủ vui để quay lại nhiều lần
articles.text:
“Thành phố cuối tuần” Qtopia: Đủ gần để đi mỗi tuần, đủ vui để quay lại nhiều lần
Kết hợp mô hình đô thị nghỉ dưỡng với tổ hợp vui chơi, giải trí và ẩm thực ngày đêm, Qtopia được phát triển theo định vị “Thành phố cuối tuần” của siêu đô thị TP.HCM. Dự án đón đầu nhu cầu về biển cuối tuần của người dân thành phố cùng cơ hội mở rộng nguồn khách từ hạ tầng liên vùng đã và đang hoàn thành.
Đón lực cầu từ siêu đô thị TP.HCM, đủ gần để đi mỗi tuần
Những chuyến về biển dịp nghỉ cuối tuần hoặc Lễ/Tết từ lâu đã trở thành thói quen của người dân TP.HCM và các tỉnh phía Nam. Với nhu cầu lặp lại thường xuyên, một điểm đến thuận tiện di chuyển, đa dạng hoạt động trải nghiệm sẽ có lợi thế thu hút du khách quay lại.
Đáng chú ý, Qtopia nằm trên mặt tiền đường ven biển Võ Thị Sáu, Phước Hải, TP.HCM, thừa hưởng trọn vẹn lợi thế kết nối từ các tỉnh phía Nam có nhu cầu đi biển cuối tuần bởi "đi nhanh về gần".
Cụ thể, cao tốc Biên Hoà – Vũng Tàu đi vào vận hành từ đợt tháng 5/2026 rút ngắn thời gian từ TP. Đồng Nai đến Qtopia chỉ hơn 60 phút di chuyển; từ TP.HCM chỉ khoảng 75 phút lái xe. Song song, cao tốc Bến Lức – Long Thành vừa thông xe đầu tháng 10/2026 tiếp tục tạo cú huých rút ngắn thời gian di chuyển từ các tỉnh miền Tây đến dự án chỉ khoảng 2,5 - 3 giờ.
Thêm một điểm cộng dành cho vị trí đắc địa của Qtopia là dự án kết nối cực nhanh đến sân bay quốc tế Long Thành, chỉ khoảng 30 phút lái xe qua cao tốc cùng các tuyến quốc lộ đang mở rộng. Khi sân bay quốc tế Long Thành đi vào vận hành ổn định, kỳ vọng Qtopia sẽ là điểm đến hút tệp khách ngoại khổng lồ.
"Thành phố cuối tuần" đẹp và vui để du khách muốn quay lại thường xuyên
Qtopia được phát triển trên quy mô hơn 7,3 ha, gồm 9 tòa căn hộ du lịch, thương mại dịch vụ. Dự án kết hợp mô hình Resort City với tổ hợp vui chơi, giải trí và nghỉ dưỡng, đáp ứng nhu cầu lưu trú, trải nghiệm và khai thác cho thuê.
Điểm nhấn trong quy hoạch Qtopia là hệ Mega Facilities, được bố trí nguyên tầng cho các nhóm tiện ích chuyên biệt. Cùng với đó, 9 tòa tháp sở hữu tiện ích nội tòa và hệ thống cảnh quan trên tầng mái. Cách tổ chức này mở rộng không gian nghỉ dưỡng, vui chơi từ mặt đất lên các tầng cao, đồng thời tạo nét riêng cho từng tòa tháp thông qua chủ đề thiết kế và các tiện ích đi kèm.
Với gia đình có trẻ nhỏ, các không gian vui chơi dưới nước và Mega Kids Wonderland mở ra hoạt động khám phá, vận động. Mega Entertainment & Gaming Center tạo thêm lựa chọn để cả nhà cùng tham gia. Trong khi đó, lợi thế "trước biển – sau núi – gần rừng", sở hữu bãi biển riêng tư, clubhouse, hệ hồ bơi, spa và sauna, giúp chủ nhân có những khoảng nghỉ thư thái. Sự đan xen giữa vận động và thư giãn giúp kỳ nghỉ phù hợp với nhiều thế hệ.
Phối cảnh Ocean Galaxy tại Qtopia, tâm điểm vui chơi, giải trí sôi động ngày đêm
Nhịp trải nghiệm tại Qtopia tiếp tục được nối dài khi chiều xuống. Ocean Galaxy, beach club, pool party cùng phố ẩm thực và trạm Quậy tạo không gian cho những cuộc hẹn nhóm bạn bên biển. Âm nhạc, ánh sáng và các hoạt động giải trí bổ sung sức hút, giúp du khách có thêm lựa chọn giải trí sau một ngày khám phá Phước Hải, TP.HCM.
Được biết, dự kiến tháng 11, Qtopia sẽ chính thức khai trương trạm Quậy tại dự án, kỳ vọng trở thành thành điểm hẹn sự kiện cuối tuần và giải trí hấp dẫn của khu vực.
Giới chuyên gia cho rằng, khi lưu trú và vui chơi được kết nối thuận tiện, du khách có thêm lý do ở lại, sử dụng dịch vụ tại chỗ, lựa chọn những lịch trình dài hơn, chi tiêu nhiều hơn.
Phối cảnh Qtopia với kiến trúc hiện đại, không gian nghỉ dưỡng và giải trí được quy hoạch đồng bộ, hướng đến tiêu chuẩn vận hành quốc tế
Bên cạnh đầu tư tiện ích, Qtopia hướng đến trải nghiệm nghỉ dưỡng tiêu chuẩn quốc tế khi được quản lý vận hành bởi CBRE, vừa chuyên nghiệp trong cách phục vụ du khách vừa có chi phí hợp lý, tối ưu lợi nhuận cho chủ sở hữu. Đặc biệt, dự án linh hoạt tiêu chuẩn bàn giao full nội thất hoặc cơ bản, đáp ứng theo nhu cầu của từng khách hàng.
"Chúng tôi lựa chọn phát triển Qtopia từ nhu cầu thực tế của người TP.HCM nói riêng và người dân miền Nam nói chung yêu biển, muốn đi biển vào cuối tuần. Bởi đây là dịp cá nhân hoặc cả gia đình được nghỉ ngơi, vui chơi và dành thời gian bên nhau. Điều chúng tôi quan tâm là cách tổ chức trải nghiệm để một gia đình nhiều thế hệ hay một nhóm bạn có thể cùng tận hưởng mà vẫn tìm thấy không gian phù hợp với mình. Qtopia cần đủ thuận tiện để khách thường xuyên trở lại và đủ trải nghiệm phong phú để mỗi chuyến đi đều có thêm lựa chọn", đại diện nhà phát triển, Công ty Cổ phần Phát triển Bất động sản Phát Đạt (PDR: HOSE) chia sẻ.
Thanh Niên Việt

articles.title: Broadridge runs Wall Street’s market plumbing. Tokenization may expand its role
articles.text: Broadridge's core franchise is difficult to displace, with its governance and technology systems deeply embedded across financial institutions, making switching complex. Tokenization is creating more business for Broadridge, not less. Broadridge is already participating in the transition to tokenization through products such as its distributed ledger repo platform, which processed roughly $360 billion of tokenized collateral per day in September. Artificial intelligence has so far looked more like a productivity tool than a direct threat to Broadridge's business. At roughly 16.4 times forward earnings, the stock trades well below its five-year average despite posting 8% recurring-revenue growth and 12% adjusted earnings growth in fiscal 2026. Broadridge Financial Solutions operates behind many of the routine functions that allow financial markets to work. It distributes proxy materials and processes shareholder votes, while its technology is used by large financial institutions for trade processing, books and records, settlement and other back-office functions. Those businesses have historically produced steady recurring revenue and earnings growth, but Broadridge shares have fallen 20% in 2026 as investors have questioned whether new technologies could make some of that infrastructure less valuable. While artificial intelligence and tokenization are changing how financial institutions operate, Broadridge's existing business remains deeply embedded in the financial system. AI is beginning to automate portions of Broadridge's own operations, raising the possibility that more of its operational work can be automated. At the same time, the early development of tokenized markets is creating new technology needs for the banks, brokers and other institutions the company already serves. Together, those developments make technological change less of a threat to Broadridge than investors currently assume and, in parts of the business, is a source of growth. Governance moat Broadridge's governance business is built around a structural feature of the U.S. equity market: most individual investors do not appear directly on the shareholder register of the companies they own. Instead, shares are generally held in "street name" through a brokerage firm or other intermediary. When companies need to communicate with investors or conduct a shareholder vote, those beneficial owners still have to be reached. Broadridge handles much of that process. It distributes proxy materials, collects voting instructions and reports the results through the system. In fiscal 2026, the company processed communications for more than a billion equity positions. That scale would be difficult for a new competitor to reproduce. Broadridge is connected to issuers, broker-dealers, custodians and investors across the market, and the service has to work accurately across all of them. Regulation adds another layer. Broker-dealers are required to forward proxy materials to beneficial owners, while much of the reimbursement framework is governed by industry rules rather than freely negotiated by Broadridge. Its technology business also operates in heavily regulated areas. Financial institutions use Broadridge for functions including trade processing, books and records, settlement and collateral management. Broker-dealers face detailed requirements around maintaining and preserving those records, including when third parties perform the work. Replacing one of these systems therefore involves more than selecting new software. Financial institutions also have to ensure that a new platform continues to satisfy regulatory and operational requirements. Implementation can also be lengthy because the systems touch multiple parts of a financial institution. That doesn't make Broadridge immune from competition, but it makes switching more complicated than replacing a typical enterprise software product. Tokenization demand Tokenization could eventually alter some of those existing workflows. In a more fully on-chain financial system, ownership might be recorded directly on a blockchain, some corporate actions could become automated and shareholders could potentially vote through digital infrastructure. That could simplify some functions Broadridge performs today. The current tokenized-equities market, however, looks quite different. Ondo Finance CEO Ian De Bode said that, as of October, roughly 90% of the tokenized-stock market was structured as notes backed by shares held within the traditional financial system. When Ondo's token holders want to vote, the company collects their voting preferences and casts the corresponding votes through Broadridge. That is how most tokenized stocks work. They are not shares originally issued on a blockchain. Instead, an issuer holds the underlying stock within the traditional financial system and creates a blockchain-based instrument backed by those shares. The token changes how the investor holds or transfers the exposure, but the underlying security remains within existing brokerage or custody infrastructure. Voting shows why that matters. A tokenized note may not directly carry the voting rights associated with the underlying share. But the issuer can collect a token holder's voting preference and then exercise the corresponding vote using the shares it owns, and the channel it uses to do so is the same one every other beneficial owner uses. For now, tokenization therefore still intersects with much of the existing financial infrastructure. That is likely to remain important as financial institutions begin adopting the technology. Banks already operate extensive systems for client accounts, trading, custody, settlement, books and records and compliance. Adding tokenized assets introduces another set of technology that has to work alongside those systems. Traditional and tokenized markets are likely to coexist for years. A hybrid market The shift to tokenization is unlikely to happen all at once. For years, financial institutions may have to operate across both traditional and blockchain-based systems, with some securities held and settled through existing infrastructure while others increasingly move on-chain. That hybrid environment creates its own set of problems. Banks and brokers still need to reconcile ownership records, accounts, collateral and corporate actions across different systems, while issuers still need to know who owns their securities and who is entitled to vote or receive distributions. That could work in Broadridge's favor. Much of its existing business is built around connecting institutions and reconciling complex financial-market infrastructure. Rather than eliminating that need immediately, tokenization may initially add another layer that has to be integrated with the systems already in place. Broadridge's existing institutional relationships give it a head start as customers adopt tokenized technology. Its distributed ledger repo platform , or DLR, is an early example.nagement expects activity to increase as clients already signed onto the platform finish implementation and move more volume onto it. Broadridge is also developing tokenization capabilities beyond repo through its broader DLX platform. Those businesses are still small compared with Broadridge overall, so tokenization is not yet a major earnings driver. But DLR provides evidence that institutions are already willing to pay Broadridge for products built around distributed-ledger technology. Tokenization also feeds the governance business. Broadridge's investor-communications revenue is influenced by the number of investment positions requiring communications and voting services. New investment products and easier market access have historically contributed to growth in those positions. Tokenized equities broaden access to U.S. securities, particularly among international investors using cryptocurrency-based platforms. Not every tokenized asset will translate into additional revenue for Broadridge. But broader participation in financial markets expands the number of positions and ownership structures requiring investor communications. That gives Broadridge several ways to participate as tokenization develops. AI: Productivity tool or threat? AI creates a different question for Broadridge. Banks may increasingly use AI to automate operational work they previously outsourced. Broadridge, however, is also deploying the technology within its own managed-services business. Its agentic AI tools are being used for tasks including investigating trade breaks, resolving exceptions and automating other repetitive operational work, and management has cited meaningful productivity improvements from those deployments. If Broadridge can perform the same work with less manual intervention, AI reduces the cost of providing some services. How much of those savings ultimately remains with Broadridge rather than being passed back to clients remains an open question. But AI doesn't eliminate the need for the underlying systems. While an AI application may help identify why a trade failed, a financial institution still needs records showing what was traded, which account owns the position and how the transaction should settle. That infrastructure remains central to Broadridge's business. The setup Broadridge's stock weakness hasn't been driven entirely by technological concerns. New contract signings weakened for several quarters as some larger platform deals took longer to close. Because those contracts can take more than a year to convert into recurring revenue, investors closely watch closed sales as an indicator of future growth. Fiscal fourth-quarter results improved considerably, with Broadridge reporting a record $158 million of closed sales. Broadridge faces a difficult comparison when it reports its first-quarter results on Tuesday because the year-ago period included unusually high event-driven proxy revenue. That could make near-term growth look weaker even if the underlying recurring business remains healthy. BR YTD mountain Broadridge Financial Services shares year to date The stock trades at roughly 16.4 times consensus fiscal 2027 earnings, compared with a five-year average closer to 22 times. Fiscal 2026 recurring revenue increased 8% and adjusted earnings per share rose 12%. The investment case doesn't require tokenization to become a major contributor immediately, nor does it depend on AI dramatically changing Broadridge's margins. The core business continues to generate recurring revenue and earnings while both opportunities develop. There are still risks. The biggest are execution, client concentration and the pace at which newer businesses become financially meaningful. Broadridge ended fiscal 2026 with a record fourth quarter for closed sales, but one strong quarter doesn't establish a trend, and large platform deals can take 12 to 24 months to implement. Sustaining bookings and converting the backlog into recurring revenue will be important to watch. The company's technology platforms are also deeply embedded with large financial institutions, which supports high retention but means the loss of a major client could hurt revenue faster than a new win can offset it. And while DLR already processes hundreds of billions of dollars of tokenized collateral each day, tokenization remains a very small contributor to Broadridge's overall revenue, so the upside could take years to become meaningful to earnings. For now, however, traditional and tokenized infrastructure are developing alongside one another, and Broadridge is participating in both. With the stock trading at a substantial discount to its historical patterns even as its core business continues to grow, investors don't need to assume a large contribution from tokenization or AI for the valuation to look attractive. Instead, both provide additional upside if Broadridge continues to capture the transition.
